verses.1:1: The vision of Isaiah son of Amoz that he saw regarding Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
verses.1:2: Listen, heavens, and give ear, earth, for the LORD has spoken: "I have raised sons and exalted them, yet they have rebelled against Me.
verses.1:3: An ox knows its owner, and a donkey its master's feeding trough; Israel does not know, My people do not discern."
verses.1:4: Woe, sinful nation, a people heavy with iniquity, seed of evildoers, sons who act corruptly! They have abandoned the LORD, they have spurned the Holy One of Israel, they have turned backward in estrangement.
verses.1:5: Why will you still be struck? You keep adding defection! The entire head is sick, and the entire heart is ailing.
verses.1:6: From the sole of the foot to the head there is no soundness in it: gashes, bruises, and fresh wounds; they have not been pressed out, nor bound up, nor softened with oil.
verses.1:7: Your land is a desolation; your cities are burned with fire; your soil—in your presence foreigners are devouring it, and it is a desolation like an overthrow by foreigners.
verses.1:8: And Daughter Zion is left behind like a booth in a vineyard, like a lodging hut in a cucumber field, like a city under siege.
verses.1:9: Had the LORD of hosts not left behind a few survivors for us, we would have become like Sodom; we would have resembled Gomorrah.
verses.1:10: Listen to the word of the LORD, leaders of Sodom; give ear to the instruction of our God, people of Gomorrah.
verses.1:11: "What is the abundance of your sacrifices to Me?" says the LORD. "I have had My fill of burnt offerings of rams and the fat of fattened beasts, and I take no delight in the blood of bulls, lambs, and male goats.
verses.1:12: When you come to appear in My presence, who has required this from your hand, to trample My courts?
verses.1:13: Do not keep bringing futile offerings; incense is an abomination to Me. New moon and Sabbath, the summoning of a convocation—I cannot bear iniquity and a solemn gathering.
verses.1:14: My soul hates your new moons and your appointed festivals; they have become a burden upon Me; I have grown weary of carrying them.
verses.1:15: And when you spread out your palms, I will hide My eyes from you; even though you multiply prayer, I am not listening; your hands are filled with bloodshed.
verses.1:16: Wash yourselves, purify yourselves; remove the evil of your practices from before My eyes; stop doing evil.
verses.1:17: Learn to do good; seek justice, correct the oppressor; vindicate the fatherless, plead the case of the widow."
verses.1:18: "Come now, and let us settle the matter," says the LORD. "Even if your sins are like scarlet, they will turn white like snow; even if they are red like crimson, they will become like wool.
verses.1:19: If you are willing and obey, you will eat the good things of the land;
verses.1:20: but if you refuse and rebel, by the sword you will be devoured," for the mouth of the LORD has spoken.
verses.1:21: How the faithful city has become a prostitute—she who was full of justice! Righteousness used to lodge in her, yet now murderers.
verses.1:22: Your silver has turned into dross; your choice drink is diluted with water.
verses.1:23: Your officials are rebels and associates of thieves; every one of them loves a bribe and pursues payoffs. They do not vindicate the fatherless, and the case of the widow does not come to them.
verses.1:24: Therefore the Lord, the LORD of hosts, the Mighty One of Israel, declares: "Ah, I will gain relief from My adversaries and avenge Myself against My enemies.
verses.1:25: And I will turn My hand back against you; I will refine away your dross as with lye, and remove all your alloy.
verses.1:26: And I will restore your judges as at first, and your advisers as at the outset; after this you will be called City of Righteousness, Faithful City."
verses.1:27: Zion will be redeemed through justice, and those in her who turn back, through righteousness.
verses.1:28: Yet shattering awaits rebels and sinners together, and those who abandon the LORD will perish.
verses.1:29: For they will be ashamed because of the terebinths that you desired, and you will be disgraced because of the gardens that you chose.
verses.1:30: For you will become like a terebinth whose foliage is withering, and like a garden that has no water.
verses.1:31: And the mighty one will become tinder, and his work a spark; both of them will burn together, with no one to extinguish them.
verses.2:1: The word that Isaiah son of Amoz saw regarding Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.2:2: And it will happen in the latter days that the mountain of the house of the LORD will be firmly established at the summit of the mountains and lifted up above the hills, and all the nations will stream to it.
verses.2:3: And many peoples will go and say, "Come, let us ascend to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob, so that He may instruct us about His ways and we may walk in His paths." For from Zion instruction will go out, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.
verses.2:4: And He will judge between the nations and arbitrate for many peoples; they will pound their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning knives; nation will not raise a sword against nation, and they will not learn warfare anymore.
verses.2:5: House of Jacob, come, and let us walk in the light of the LORD.
verses.2:6: For You have forsaken Your people, the house of Jacob, because they are filled with what comes from the east, and are diviners like the Philistines, and clasp hands with the children of foreigners.
verses.2:7: And their land is filled with silver and gold, and their treasuries have no end; their land is filled with horses, and their chariots have no end.
verses.2:8: And their land is filled with idols; to the work of their hands they bow down, to what their fingers have made.
verses.2:9: So mankind is bowed down, and each man is brought low; and do not forgive them.
verses.2:10: Go into the rock and hide yourself in the dust, away from the dread of the LORD and from the splendor of His grandeur.
verses.2:11: The haughty eyes of mankind will be brought low, and the loftiness of men will be bowed down; and the LORD alone will be exalted on that day.
verses.2:12: For a day belongs to the LORD of hosts against everything proud and lofty, and against everything lifted up, so that it will be brought low;
verses.2:13: and against all the lofty and lifted-up cedars of Lebanon, and against all the oaks of Bashan;
verses.2:14: and against all the lofty mountains, and against all the hills that are lifted up;
verses.2:15: and against every tall tower, and against every fortified wall;
verses.2:16: and against all the ships of Tarshish, and against all the prized vessels.
verses.2:17: And the haughtiness of mankind will be bowed down, and the loftiness of men will be brought low; and the LORD alone will be exalted on that day.
verses.2:18: And the idols will altogether vanish.
verses.2:19: And people will go into caves in the rocks and into holes in the dust, away from the dread of the LORD and from the splendor of His grandeur, when He arises to strike terror into the earth.
verses.2:20: On that day people will fling away their idols of silver and their idols of gold, which they made for themselves to bow down to, to the moles and to the bats,
verses.2:21: to go into the clefts of the rocks and into the crevices of the cliffs, away from the dread of the LORD and from the splendor of His grandeur, when He arises to strike terror into the earth.
verses.3:1: For look, the Lord, the LORD of hosts, is removing from Jerusalem and from Judah support and mainstay, every support of bread and every support of water;
verses.3:2: hero and man of war, judge and prophet, diviner and elder,
verses.3:3: commander of fifty and honored man, counselor, skilled craftsman, and expert in charms.
verses.3:4: And I will make youths their officials, and willful children will rule over them.
verses.3:5: And the people will oppress one another, one against another and each against his neighbor; the youth will act arrogantly toward the elder, and the disdained toward the honored.
verses.3:6: When a man takes hold of his brother in his father's house, saying, "You have a cloak; be our leader, and let this ruin be under your hand,"
verses.3:7: on that day he will speak up, saying, "I will not be a binder of wounds, and in my house there is no bread and no cloak; you must not make me leader of the people."
verses.3:8: For Jerusalem has stumbled and Judah has fallen, because their tongue and their deeds are against the LORD, to defy the eyes of His glory.
verses.3:9: The appearance of their faces testifies against them, and they proclaim their sin like Sodom; they do not conceal it. Woe to their souls, for they have dealt evil to themselves!
verses.3:10: Say of the righteous that it will be well, for they will eat the fruit of their deeds.
verses.3:11: Woe to the wicked! It will go ill, for the repayment of his hands will be done to him.
verses.3:12: My people—a child is their taskmaster, and women rule over them. My people, those who direct you are leading you astray, and they confound the way of your paths.
verses.3:13: The LORD stations Himself to contend, and He stands to judge peoples.
verses.3:14: The LORD comes into judgment with the elders of His people and its officials: "You yourselves have consumed the vineyard; what was robbed from the poor is in your houses.
verses.3:15: What right do you have to crush My people and grind the faces of the poor?" declares the Lord GOD of hosts.
verses.3:16: And the LORD said, "Because the daughters of Zion are haughty and walk with necks stretched out, flirting with their eyes, tripping along as they walk and jingling with their feet,
verses.3:17: therefore the Lord will cover the scalps of the daughters of Zion with scabs, and the LORD will expose their private parts."
verses.3:18: On that day the Lord will remove the splendor of the anklets, the sun-disks, and the crescents,
verses.3:19: the ear-drops, the bracelets, and the veils,
verses.3:20: the headdresses, the ankle chains, the sashes, the scent bottles, and the charms,
verses.3:21: the rings and the nose rings,
verses.3:22: the festive robes, the mantles, the shawls, and the purses,
verses.3:23: and the hand mirrors, the fine linens, the turbans, and the wraps.
verses.3:24: And it will be that instead of perfume there will be decay; instead of a belt, a rope; instead of braided hair, baldness; instead of a fine robe, a wrapping of sackcloth; and a brand mark instead of beauty.
verses.3:25: Your men will fall by the sword, and your might in war.
verses.3:26: And her gates will grieve and mourn, and emptied out, she will sit on the ground.
verses.4:1: And seven women will grasp one man on that day, saying, "Our own bread we will eat, and our own garments we will wear; only let your name be called over us; remove our disgrace."
verses.4:2: On that day the branch of the LORD will be beauty and glory, and the fruit of the land will be majesty and splendor for the survivors of Israel.
verses.4:3: And it will be that whoever is left in Zion and whoever remains in Jerusalem will be called holy, everyone written down for life in Jerusalem,
verses.4:4: once the Lord has washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion and rinsed the bloodstains of Jerusalem from her midst with a spirit of judgment and a spirit of burning.
verses.4:5: Then the LORD will create over the entire place of Mount Zion and over her assemblies a cloud by day and smoke, and the radiance of a blazing fire by night; indeed, over all the glory there will be a canopy.
verses.4:6: And there will be a shelter for shade by day from the heat, and as a refuge and cover from downpour and from rain.
verses.5:1: Let me sing now for my dear friend the song of my beloved concerning His vineyard: My dear friend had a vineyard on a fertile ridge.
verses.5:2: He hoed it and cleared its stones, and planted it with choice vines. He built a tower inside it and also carved a wine vat in it. Then He hoped for it to produce grapes, but it produced foul grapes.
verses.5:3: And now, residents of Jerusalem and men of Judah, please judge between Me and My vineyard.
verses.5:4: What else was to be done for My vineyard that I did not do in it? Why, when I hoped for it to produce grapes, did it produce foul grapes?
verses.5:5: And now let Me make known to you what I am about to do to My vineyard: I will take away its hedge, and it will be consumed; I will breach its wall, and it will be trampled underfoot.
verses.5:6: And I will make it a desolation; it will neither be pruned nor hoed, and thorns and briers will spring up; and I will command the clouds not to rain any rain on it.
verses.5:7: For the vineyard of the LORD of hosts is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah are the planting of His delight. He hoped for justice, yet look, bloodshed; for righteousness, yet look, an outcry!
verses.5:8: Woe to those who connect house to house, bringing field next to field, until no space remains and you are made to live alone in the middle of the land.
verses.5:9: In my ears the LORD of hosts has spoken: "Surely many houses will turn to desolation, large and fine ones, with no one dwelling in them.
verses.5:10: For ten acres of vineyard will produce a single bath, and a homer of seed will produce an ephah."
verses.5:11: Woe to those who rise early in the morning, chasing after strong drink, who linger into the evening while wine inflames them!
verses.5:12: Their feasts are lyre and harp, tambourine and flute and wine, yet they do not look at the deed of the LORD, nor do they see the work of His hands.
verses.5:13: Therefore My people have gone into exile for lack of knowledge; their honored ones are men of hunger, and their throng is parched from thirst.
verses.5:14: Therefore Sheol has widened its throat and opened its mouth without limit, and down descend her splendor, her throng, her uproar, and whoever exults in her.
verses.5:15: So mankind is bowed down and each man is brought low, and the eyes of the lofty will be brought low.
verses.5:16: But the LORD of hosts is lifted high by justice, and the holy God proves Himself holy by righteousness.
verses.5:17: Then lambs will graze as in their own pasture, and sojourners will feed on the ruins of the wealthy.
verses.5:18: Woe to those who haul iniquity with cords of deceit, and sin as with wagon ropes,
verses.5:19: who say, "Let Him hurry, let Him speed up His work so that we may see it; let the plan of the Holy One of Israel approach and arrive so that we may know it!"
verses.5:20: Woe to those who pronounce evil good and good evil, who set darkness as light and light as darkness, who set bitter as sweet and sweet as bitter!
verses.5:21: Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes and discerning before their own faces!
verses.5:22: Woe to those who are champions at drinking wine and men of valor at mixing strong drink,
verses.5:23: who declare the wicked righteous for a bribe, yet take away the righteousness of the righteous from each of them!
verses.5:24: Therefore, as a tongue of fire eats up stubble and dry grass sinks into flame, so their root will become like decay and their blossom will rise like dust; because they have rejected the instruction of the LORD of hosts and have spurned the word of the Holy One of Israel.
verses.5:25: For this reason the anger of the LORD flared against His people, and He stretched out His hand against them and struck them. The mountains quaked, and their corpses were like refuse in the middle of the streets. Despite all this, His anger has not turned back, and still His hand is stretched out.
verses.5:26: He will raise a banner for the nations far away and whistle for them from the end of the earth; and look, swiftly and rapidly they come!
verses.5:27: Not one among them is weary, and not one stumbles; not one dozes and not one sleeps; no belt on their waists is loosened, nor is any strap of their sandals snapped.
verses.5:28: Their arrows are sharpened, and all their bows are strung; the hooves of their horses are reckoned like flint, and their wheels like a storm wind.
verses.5:29: Their roar is like a lion; they roar like young lions. They growl and seize prey, and carry it away, with no one to rescue.
verses.5:30: And on that day they will roar over it like the roaring of the sea. And if one looks to the land, look, darkness and distress, and the light has grown dark in its clouds.
verses.6:1: In the year of the death of King Uzziah, I saw the Lord seated on a throne, lofty and lifted up, and the hems of His robe were filling the temple.
verses.6:2: Seraphim were standing above Him; each one had six wings: with two he would cover his face, and with two he would cover his feet, and with two he would fly.
verses.6:3: And one would call to another and say, "Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of hosts; the fullness of all the earth is His glory."
verses.6:4: And the bases of the thresholds trembled at the voice of the one calling, and the house was filling with smoke.
verses.6:5: Then I said, "Woe to me, for I am destroyed, because I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips; for my eyes have seen the King, the LORD of hosts."
verses.6:6: And one of the seraphim flew to me, and in his hand was a glowing coal that he had taken with tongs from the altar.
verses.6:7: He touched it to my mouth and said, "Look, this has touched your lips; your iniquity has departed, and your sin is atoned for."
verses.6:8: And I heard the Lord's voice saying, "Whom shall I send, and who will go for Us?" So I said, "Here I am; send me."
verses.6:9: And He said, "Go and tell this people, 'Keep hearing, yet do not understand; and keep seeing, yet do not know.'
verses.6:10: Make the heart of this people fat, make its ears heavy, and smear its eyes shut, otherwise it might see with its eyes, and hear with its ears, and understand with its heart, and turn back and be healed."
verses.6:11: Then I said, "How long, Lord?" And He said, "Until cities fall into ruins without an inhabitant, and houses without a human being, and the ground is ruined into a desolation,
verses.6:12: and the LORD has sent humanity far away, and forsakenness grows vast in the midst of the land.
verses.6:13: And even though a tenth still remains in it, it will again be for burning—like a terebinth and like an oak which, when felled, still have a stump in them; a holy seed is its stump."
verses.7:1: Now it happened in the days of Ahaz, son of Jotham, son of Uzziah, king of Judah, that Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up to Jerusalem for war against it, yet he was not able to fight against it.
verses.7:2: When it was reported to the house of David, "Aram has settled upon Ephraim," his heart and the heart of his people trembled as the trees of a forest tremble before the wind.
verses.7:3: Then the LORD said to Isaiah, "Go out now to meet Ahaz, you and your son Shear-jashub, at the end of the water channel of the upper pool, by the highway of the launderer's field,
verses.7:4: and say to him, 'Take care and keep calm; do not be afraid, and do not let your heart grow faint because of these two tail ends of smoking firebrands, at the burning anger of Rezin and Aram and the son of Remaliah.
verses.7:5: Because Aram has devised evil against you, along with Ephraim and the son of Remaliah, saying,
verses.7:6: "Let us go up against Judah and fill it with dread, and breach it for ourselves, and install a king in its midst, the son of Tabeel,"
verses.7:7: this is what the Lord GOD says: "It will not stand, and it will not happen.
verses.7:8: For the head of Aram is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin; and within another sixty-five years Ephraim will be shattered from being a people.
verses.7:9: And the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is the son of Remaliah. If you do not trust, surely you will not remain firm."'"
verses.7:10: And the LORD spoke again to Ahaz, saying,
verses.7:11: "Ask a sign for yourself from the LORD your God; go deep in asking, or go high above."
verses.7:12: Then Ahaz said, "I will not ask, and I will not test the LORD."
verses.7:13: Then he said, "Listen now, house of David: is it too small a thing for you to weary men, that you weary my God as well?
verses.7:14: Therefore the Lord Himself will give you a sign: see, the young woman is pregnant and will give birth to a son, and she will call his name Immanuel.
verses.7:15: He will eat curds and honey by the time he knows how to reject the evil and choose the good.
verses.7:16: For before the boy knows how to reject the evil and choose the good, the land that you dread because of its two kings will be forsaken.
verses.7:17: The LORD will bring on you, and on your people, and on your father's house, days that have not come since the day Ephraim departed from Judah—the king of Assyria.
verses.7:18: And it will happen on that day that the LORD will whistle for the fly that is at the end of the streams of Egypt, and for the bee that is in the land of Assyria.
verses.7:19: And all of them will come and settle in the precipitous ravines, and in the crevices of the crags, and on all the thornbushes, and at all the watering places.
verses.7:20: On that day, with a razor hired from the regions beyond the River—with the king of Assyria—the Lord will shave the head and the hair of the feet, and it will sweep away the beard as well.
verses.7:21: And it will happen on that day that a man will keep alive a young cow of the herd and two sheep,
verses.7:22: and it will happen that because of the abundance of milk they produce, he will eat curds; for everyone remaining in the midst of the land will eat curds and honey.
verses.7:23: And it will happen on that day that every spot where there are a thousand vines, valued at a thousand silver pieces, will belong to briers and thorns.
verses.7:24: With arrows and a bow one will go there, for the whole land will be briers and thorns.
verses.7:25: And as for all the hills that used to be hoed with a hoe, you will not go there out of fear of briers and thorns; instead, it will become a place for turning an ox loose and a trampling ground for sheep."
verses.8:1: Then the LORD said to me, "Take for yourself a large tablet and write on it with a human stylus, 'Belonging to Maher-shalal-hash-baz.'
verses.8:2: And I will summon for Myself trustworthy witnesses—Uriah the priest and Zechariah son of Jeberechiah."
verses.8:3: Then I approached the prophetess, and she conceived and bore a son. And the LORD said to me, "Call his name Maher-shalal-hash-baz;
verses.8:4: for before the boy knows how to call out, 'My father' and 'My mother,' the wealth of Damascus and the plunder of Samaria will be carried off before the king of Assyria."
verses.8:5: And the LORD spoke to me yet again, saying,
verses.8:6: "Because this people has rejected the waters of Shiloah that flow gently, and rejoices with Rezin and the son of Remaliah,
verses.8:7: therefore, look, the Lord is bringing up over them the mighty and abundant waters of the River—the king of Assyria and all his glory; and it will rise over all its channels and flow over all its banks.
verses.8:8: It will sweep on into Judah, overflowing and passing through; it will reach up to the neck, and the spread of its wings will fill the width of your land, Immanuel."
verses.8:9: Break to pieces, peoples, and be shattered, and give ear, all far reaches of the earth! Gird yourselves, and be shattered; gird yourselves, and be shattered!
verses.8:10: Devise a plan, and it will be frustrated; speak a word, and it will not stand, for God is with us.
verses.8:11: For this is how the LORD spoke to me with the force of His hand, and admonished me not to walk in the way of this people, saying,
verses.8:12: "You must not call 'conspiracy' all that this people calls 'conspiracy,' and what it fears you must not fear, nor regard with dread.
verses.8:13: The LORD of hosts—Him you must regard as holy; He is to be your fear, and He is to be your dread.
verses.8:14: And He will become a sanctuary, and a stone of striking and a rock of stumbling to the two houses of Israel, a trap and a snare to the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
verses.8:15: And many will stumble over them; they will fall and be broken, and be snared and captured."
verses.8:16: Bind up the testimony; seal the instruction among my disciples.
verses.8:17: And I will wait for the LORD, who conceals His face from the house of Jacob, and I will hope for Him.
verses.8:18: Look, I and the children whom the LORD has given me are for signs and portents in Israel from the LORD of hosts, who dwells on Mount Zion.
verses.8:19: And when they say to you, "Inquire of the mediums and the spiritists who chirp and mutter," should not a people inquire of its God? Should they inquire of the dead on behalf of the living?
verses.8:20: To the instruction and to the testimony! If they do not speak in accordance with this word, it is because there is no dawn for them.
verses.8:21: Each one will pass through the land, hard-pressed and hungry; and it will happen that when he is hungry, he will grow enraged and curse his king and his God, and turn upward.
verses.8:22: Then he will look toward the earth, and see: distress and darkness, the gloom of anguish; and he will be thrust into thick darkness.
verses.8:23: Yet there will be no gloom for her who was in anguish. In the earlier time He brought dishonor upon the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, but in the later time He will bring honor to the way of the sea, the region across the Jordan, Galilee of the nations.
verses.9:1: The people walking in darkness have seen a great light; on those living in a land of death's shadow, light has shone.
verses.9:2: You have multiplied the nation; for it You have made the joy great. They rejoice before You like the joy in the harvest, just as they exult when they divide plunder.
verses.9:3: For You have shattered the yoke of its burden, and the staff across its shoulder, the rod of the one oppressing it, just as on the day of Midian.
verses.9:4: For every boot of one tramping in tumult, and every cloak rolled in blood, will be for burning, food for fire.
verses.9:5: For a child has been born to us, a son has been given to us; and the dominion will be on his shoulder, and his name will be called Wonder-Counselor, Mighty God, Father of Eternity, Prince of Peace.
verses.9:6: Of the increase of the dominion and of peace there will be no end, upon the throne of David and over his kingdom, to establish it and to sustain it with justice and with righteousness, from now on and forever. The zeal of the LORD of hosts will perform this.
verses.9:7: The Lord sent a word against Jacob, and it has fallen upon Israel.
verses.9:8: And the whole people will know it—Ephraim and those dwelling in Samaria—saying in pride and haughtiness of heart,
verses.9:9: "Bricks have fallen, yet we will build with hewn stone; sycamores have been felled, yet we will substitute cedars for them."
verses.9:10: So the LORD raised high the adversaries of Rezin against him and spurred on his enemies.
verses.9:11: Aram from the east and the Philistines from the west—they devoured Israel with wide-open mouth. Despite all this, His anger has not turned back, and His hand is still outstretched.
verses.9:12: Yet the people have not turned back to Him who struck them, and they have not sought the LORD of hosts.
verses.9:13: So the LORD cut off from Israel head and tail, palm frond and bulrush, in a single day.
verses.9:14: The elder and the distinguished man is the head, and the prophet teaching falsehood is the tail.
verses.9:15: And those guiding this people have become ones who lead astray, and those guided by them are swallowed up.
verses.9:16: Therefore the Lord will not rejoice over their young men, nor will He show compassion to their orphans and their widows; for each of them is godless and practices evil, and every mouth utters folly. Despite all this, His anger has not turned back, and His hand is still outstretched.
verses.9:17: For wickedness has burned like fire; it devours briers and thorns; it ignites among the thickets of the forest, and they billow upward in a swelling of smoke.
verses.9:18: Through the fury of the LORD of hosts, the land has been scorched, and the people have become like food for fire; no one spares his brother.
verses.9:19: One slices off on the right and remains hungry, and eats on the left, yet they are not filled; each person consumes the flesh of his own arm.
verses.9:20: Manasseh consumes Ephraim, and Ephraim consumes Manasseh, and both together are against Judah. Despite all this, His anger has not turned back, and His hand is still outstretched.
verses.10:1: Woe to those who enact statutes of iniquity, and to scribes who write out oppression,
verses.10:2: to turn the poor away from justice and to rob the afflicted of My people of their legal right, so that widows become their plunder and they may loot the orphans.
verses.10:3: And what will you do for the day of reckoning, and at the devastation arriving from far away? To whom will you flee for aid, and where will you leave your glory?
verses.10:4: There is nothing left except to bow down beneath the captives or to fall beneath the slaughtered. Despite all this, His anger has not turned back, and His hand is still outstretched.
verses.10:5: Woe, Assyria, rod of My anger—and the staff in their hand is My indignation!
verses.10:6: I send him forth against a godless nation, and against the people of My fury I charge him, to plunder spoil and to loot booty, and to make them a trampling place like mud of the streets.
verses.10:7: Yet he does not intend it this way, and his heart does not think this way; rather, it is in his heart to destroy and to cut off not a few nations.
verses.10:8: For he says, "Are not my princes kings altogether?
verses.10:9: Is Calno not like Carchemish? Is Hamath not like Arpad? Is Samaria not like Damascus?
verses.10:10: Just as my hand found the kingdoms of the idols, whose carved images surpassed those of Jerusalem and Samaria,
verses.10:11: just as I have done to Samaria and to her idols, will I not do the same to Jerusalem and to her images?"
verses.10:12: And it will happen, when the Lord has finished all His work on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, that I will punish the fruit of the king of Assyria's haughty heart and the boastfulness of his lofty eyes.
verses.10:13: For he said, "By the strength of my hand I have acted, and by my wisdom, for I am discerning; I removed the borders of peoples, and their stored treasures I pillaged, and like a mighty one I brought down the inhabitants.
verses.10:14: And like a nest my hand found the wealth of the peoples; just as someone gathers abandoned eggs, I myself gathered the whole earth, and there was not one flapping a wing, or opening a mouth, or chirping."
verses.10:15: Will the ax boast over the one who chops with it, or will the saw exalt itself over the one who swings it? As though a rod should swing those who lift it, or as though a staff should lift someone who is not wood!
verses.10:16: Therefore the Lord, the LORD of hosts, will send a wasting illness among his stout ones, and beneath his glory a burning will blaze like the blaze of fire.
verses.10:17: And the Light of Israel will turn into a fire, and its Holy One into a flame; it will blaze and consume his thorns and his briers in a single day.
verses.10:18: And He will bring to an end the glory of his forest and his fruitful orchard, from soul even to flesh, and it will be like a sick man melting away.
verses.10:19: And the remnant of the trees in his forest will be few in number, and a boy could write them down.
verses.10:20: And it will happen in that day that the remnant of Israel and the surviving ones of the house of Jacob will no longer lean on the one who struck them, but will lean in truth on the LORD, the Holy One of Israel.
verses.10:21: A remnant will return—the remnant of Jacob—to Mighty God.
verses.10:22: For even though your people Israel should be like the sand of the sea, a remnant among them will return; annihilation is decreed, flooding with righteousness.
verses.10:23: For the Lord GOD of hosts is carrying out a complete and decreed destruction in the midst of the entire earth.
verses.10:24: Therefore this is what the Lord GOD of hosts says: "Do not fear Assyria, My people dwelling in Zion, when he strikes you with the rod and raises his staff against you in the manner of Egypt.
verses.10:25: For in just a very short while, indignation will be over, and My anger will turn to their destruction."
verses.10:26: And the LORD of hosts will rouse a whip against him, like the striking of Midian at the rock of Oreb; and His staff will be over the sea, and He will raise it in the manner of Egypt.
verses.10:27: And it will happen in that day that his burden will lift from your shoulder, and his yoke from your neck, and the yoke will be destroyed because of fatness.
verses.10:28: He has come upon Aiath; he has passed through Migron; at Michmash he deposits his supplies.
verses.10:29: They have crossed the pass; at Geba they took their night's lodging; Ramah quakes; Gibeah of Saul has fled.
verses.10:30: Cry shrilly with your voice, daughter of Gallim! Listen closely, Laishah! Afflicted Anathoth!
verses.10:31: Madmenah flees away; the residents of Gebim have taken refuge.
verses.10:32: Even today he will stop at Nob; he shakes his hand against the mountain of Daughter Zion, the hill of Jerusalem.
verses.10:33: Look, the Lord, the LORD of hosts, is lopping off the boughs with terrifying force; the tall in stature are felled, and the high ones will sink low.
verses.10:34: And He will chop down the thickets of the forest with iron, and Lebanon will fall by a Mighty One.
verses.11:1: Yet a shoot will come out from the stump of Jesse, and a sprout from his roots will bear fruit.
verses.11:2: And the Spirit of the LORD will rest on him—the Spirit of wisdom and discernment, the Spirit of counsel and power, the Spirit of knowledge and the fear of the LORD.
verses.11:3: And his delight will be in the fear of the LORD; he will not judge according to the sight of his eyes, nor decide according to the hearing of his ears.
verses.11:4: Rather, he will judge the poor in righteousness, and he will decide in fairness for the humble of the earth; with the rod of his mouth he will strike the earth, and with the breath of his lips he will put the wicked to death.
verses.11:5: And righteousness will be the sash around his waist, and faithfulness the sash around his loins.
verses.11:6: And a wolf will dwell with a lamb, and a leopard will lie down with a young goat; a calf and a young lion and a fatling will be together, and a small boy will lead them.
verses.11:7: A cow and a bear will graze; together their young will lie down, and a lion, like the ox, will eat straw.
verses.11:8: And a nursing infant will play over a cobra's hole, and a weaned child will stretch out his hand over a viper's den.
verses.11:9: They will do no harm and cause no destruction throughout all My holy mountain, for the earth will be filled with knowledge of the LORD, just as the waters cover the sea.
verses.11:10: And it will happen in that day that the root of Jesse, who stands as a banner for peoples—nations will seek him out, and his place of rest will be glorious.
verses.11:11: And it will happen in that day that the Lord will once more reach out His hand a second time to reclaim the remnant of His people that is left from Assyria, from Egypt, from Pathros, from Cush, from Elam, from Shinar, from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea.
verses.11:12: And He will raise a banner for the nations, and He will gather the outcasts of Israel and assemble the scattered ones of Judah from the four corners of the earth.
verses.11:13: And Ephraim's envy will pass away, and the adversaries of Judah will be cut off; Ephraim will not envy Judah, and Judah will not show hostility toward Ephraim.
verses.11:14: And they will swoop down on the slope of the Philistines toward the west; together they will loot the sons of the east. Against Edom and Moab they will stretch out their hand, and the sons of Ammon will be obedient to them.
verses.11:15: And the LORD will completely destroy the tongue of the Sea of Egypt; He will wave His hand over the River with the scorching heat of His wind, and He will strike it into seven streams and make people walk across in sandals.
verses.11:16: And there will be a highway for the remnant of His people that is left from Assyria, just as there was for Israel on the day they came up from the land of Egypt.
verses.12:1: And on that day you will say, "I will thank You, LORD, for although You were angry with me, Your anger has turned back and You comfort me.
verses.12:2: Look, God is my salvation; I will trust and will not be terrified, for the LORD, the LORD, is my strength and song, and He has become salvation to me."
verses.12:3: And you will draw water with gladness from the springs of salvation.
verses.12:4: And on that day you will say, "Give thanks to the LORD; call on His name; make His deeds known among the peoples; declare that His name is exalted.
verses.12:5: Sing praises to the LORD, for He has done majestic things; this is made known in all the earth.
verses.12:6: Cry aloud and sing out, inhabitant of Zion, for the Holy One of Israel is great in your midst."
verses.13:1: The pronouncement concerning Babylon that Isaiah the son of Amoz saw.
verses.13:2: On a bare mountain lift up a banner; raise your voice to them; wave a hand, so that they may enter the gates of the nobles.
verses.13:3: I Myself have commanded My consecrated ones; I have also summoned My mighty warriors for My anger, those who exult in My majesty.
verses.13:4: The sound of a tumult on the mountains, the likeness of a vast people! The sound of an uproar of kingdoms, of nations assembling together! The LORD of hosts is marshaling an army for war.
verses.13:5: They are coming from a distant land, from the end of the heavens, the LORD and the instruments of His indignation, to ruin all the earth.
verses.13:6: Wail, for the day of the LORD is near; like devastation from the Almighty it will come.
verses.13:7: Therefore all hands will go limp, and the heart of every mortal will melt.
verses.13:8: And they will be terrified; pangs and birth pains will grip them; like a woman giving birth they will writhe. Each will stare aghast at his companion; their faces will be faces of flames.
verses.13:9: Look, the day of the LORD is coming, cruel, with wrath and burning anger, to make the earth a desolation, and He will wipe out its sinners from it.
verses.13:10: For the stars of the heavens and their constellations will not shine out their light; the sun will grow dark as it rises, and the moon will not cause its light to shine.
verses.13:11: And I will call the world to account for evil, and the wicked for their iniquity; I will make the arrogance of the insolent cease, and the pride of the ruthless I will bring low.
verses.13:12: I will make mortals scarcer than refined gold, and human beings than the choice gold of Ophir.
verses.13:13: Therefore I will make the heavens tremble, and the earth will quake from its place at the wrath of the LORD of hosts and on the day of His burning anger.
verses.13:14: And it will be that like a chased gazelle, and like a flock with no one gathering it, each will turn to his own people, and each will flee to his own land.
verses.13:15: Everyone who is found will be pierced through, and everyone who is caught will fall by the sword.
verses.13:16: And their little children will be dashed to pieces before their eyes; their houses will be looted, and their wives will be violated.
verses.13:17: Look, I am rousing the Medes against them, who do not value silver, and as for gold, they take no pleasure in it.
verses.13:18: And bows will dash young men to pieces; they will have no compassion on the fruit of the womb; their eye will not spare children.
verses.13:19: And Babylon, the splendor of kingdoms, the beauty of the pride of the Chaldeans, will be as in God's overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah.
verses.13:20: It will never be inhabited, nor will it be dwelt in from generation to generation; no Arab will pitch a tent there, and no shepherds will let their flocks lie down there.
verses.13:21: But desert animals will lie down there, and their houses will be filled with howling creatures; ostriches will dwell there, and wild goats will leap about there.
verses.13:22: Hyenas will howl in its citadels, and jackals in palaces of luxury. Its time is near to come, and its days will not be drawn out.
verses.14:1: For the LORD will show compassion to Jacob and will choose Israel once more, and settle them on their own land; and the sojourner will join himself to them, and they will attach themselves to the house of Jacob.
verses.14:2: And peoples will take them and bring them to their place, and the house of Israel will take them as an inheritance on the land of the LORD, as male servants and female servants; and they will be captors of their captors and rule over their oppressors.
verses.14:3: And it will happen on the day the LORD gives you rest from your pain and your agitation, and from the hard labor you were made to serve,
verses.14:4: that you will take up this taunt against the king of Babylon and say, "How the oppressor has ceased! The exaction of gold has ceased!
verses.14:5: The LORD has broken the staff of the wicked, the rod of the rulers,
verses.14:6: that struck peoples in wrath with a blow without ceasing, that ruled nations in anger with persecution without restraint.
verses.14:7: All the earth rests and is still; they burst forth into a shout of joy.
verses.14:8: Even the cypresses rejoice over you, the cedars of Lebanon: 'Since you have lain down, no woodcutter comes up against us.'
verses.14:9: Sheol below is agitated for you to meet your coming; it rouses the shades for you, all the leaders of the earth; it raises up from their thrones all the kings of the nations.
verses.14:10: All of them will answer and say to you, 'You also have been made weak like us; you have become just like us.'
verses.14:11: Your pomp has been brought down to Sheol, the music of your harps; beneath you maggots are spread out, and worms are your coverings.
verses.14:12: How you have fallen from the heavens, Shining One, son of the dawn! You have been hewn down to the earth, you who laid nations prostrate!
verses.14:13: Yet you said in your heart, 'To the heavens I will ascend; above the stars of God I will lift up my throne, and I will sit on the mountain of assembly, in the farthest recesses of the north;
verses.14:14: I will ascend above the cloud heights; I will become like the Most High.'
verses.14:15: Instead, you will be brought down to Sheol, to the farthest recesses of the Pit.
verses.14:16: Those who see you will gaze intently at you; they will consider you closely: 'Is this the man who made the earth tremble, who made kingdoms quake,
verses.14:17: who made the world like the wilderness and demolished its cities, who did not release his prisoners to go home?'
verses.14:18: All the kings of the nations, all of them, lie in honor, each in his own house.
verses.14:19: But you have been thrown out away from your grave like a detested branch, clothed with those killed, pierced by the sword, who go down to the stones of the Pit, like a corpse trampled underfoot.
verses.14:20: You will not be united with them in burial, for you have ruined your land, you have killed your people. The seed of evildoers will never be named.
verses.14:21: Prepare a slaughter place for his sons because of the iniquity of their fathers, so that they will not rise up and possess the earth and fill the surface of the world with cities."
verses.14:22: "And I will rise up against them," declares the LORD of hosts, "and I will cut off from Babylon name and remnant, offspring and descendants," declares the LORD.
verses.14:23: "And I will turn it into a possession for the hedgehog and marshes of water, and I will sweep it away with the broom of destruction," declares the LORD of hosts.
verses.14:24: The LORD of hosts has sworn, saying, "Surely, just as I have intended, so it will happen, and just as I have planned, that will stand:
verses.14:25: to break Assyria in My land, and on My mountains I will trample him underfoot; and his yoke will depart from them, and his burden will depart from his shoulder."
verses.14:26: This is the plan that has been planned over all the earth, and this is the hand stretched out over all the nations.
verses.14:27: For the LORD of hosts has planned, and who will thwart it? And His outstretched hand—who will turn it back?
verses.14:28: In the year of King Ahaz's death, this pronouncement came:
verses.14:29: Do not rejoice, Philistia, all of you, that the rod of the one who struck you has been broken; for out of the snake's root a viper will come forth, and its fruit will be a flying fiery serpent.
verses.14:30: And the firstborn of the poor will graze, and the needy will lie down in security; but I will put your root to death by famine, and he will kill your remnant.
verses.14:31: Wail, gate; cry out, city; melt away, Philistia, all of you! For smoke is coming from the north, and no one straggles in his ranks.
verses.14:32: And what will one reply to the messengers of the nation? "The LORD has founded Zion, and in it the afflicted of His people will take refuge."
verses.15:1: The pronouncement concerning Moab: Truly, in a night Ar of Moab is ravaged, it is cut off; truly, in a night Kir of Moab is ravaged, it is cut off.
verses.15:2: Bayith and Dibon have gone up to the high places to weep; over Nebo and over Medeba Moab wails. On all its heads is baldness; every beard is shaved off.
verses.15:3: In its streets they have wrapped themselves in sackcloth; on its rooftops and in its public squares everyone wails, going down in weeping.
verses.15:4: Heshbon and Elealeh cry out; as far as Jahaz their voice is heard. Therefore the armed warriors of Moab shout aloud; its soul quivers within it.
verses.15:5: My heart cries out for Moab; its fugitives flee as far as Zoar, to Eglath-shelishiyah. For on the ascent of Luhith one goes up with weeping; for along the road to Horonaim they stir up a cry of ruin.
verses.15:6: For the waters of Nimrim will become desolations; indeed, the grass has dried up, the tender shoots have vanished, no greenery remains.
verses.15:7: Therefore the surplus it has acquired and their stored possessions they carry across the Wadi of the Willows.
verses.15:8: For the outcry has encircled the border of Moab; as far as Eglaim reaches its wailing, and to Beer-elim its wailing.
verses.15:9: For the waters of Dimon are full of blood; indeed, I will lay still more upon Dimon: a lion for those of Moab who escape, and for the remnant of the land.
verses.16:1: Send a lamb for the ruler of the land, from Sela across the wilderness to the mountain of Daughter Zion.
verses.16:2: And it will be that like a fleeing bird, a nest driven out, so the daughters of Moab will be at the fords of the Arnon.
verses.16:3: Bring counsel, execute judgment; set your shade like the night in the middle of noon; hide the outcasts, do not expose the fugitive.
verses.16:4: Let My outcasts sojourn with you, Moab; be a shelter for them from the ravager. For the oppressor has ceased, ravaging has come to an end, and those who trample are gone from the land.
verses.16:5: And a throne will be established in loyal love, and in truth a judge will sit upon it in the tent of David, seeking justice and swift in righteousness.
verses.16:6: We have heard of Moab's pride, how exceedingly proud it is—of its arrogance, its pride, and its insolence; its boasts are not true.
verses.16:7: Therefore Moab will wail for Moab; all of it will wail. For the raisin cakes of Kir-hareseth you will groan, utterly crushed.
verses.16:8: For the fields of Heshbon wither, as does the vine of Sibmah; the lords of the nations have struck down its choice vines—they reached as far as Jazer, they strayed into the wilderness; its shoots spread out, they crossed the sea.
verses.16:9: Therefore I will weep with Jazer's weeping for the vine of Sibmah; I will soak you with My tears, Heshbon and Elealeh, for upon your summer fruit and upon your harvest the shouting has fallen.
verses.16:10: And gladness and joy are withdrawn from the orchard; in the vineyards there will be no singing for joy and no cheering; no treader will tread wine in the winepresses; I have made the shouting cease.
verses.16:11: Therefore My inward parts groan like a lyre for Moab, and My inner being for Kir-heres.
verses.16:12: And it will happen that when Moab appears, when it wears itself out on the high place and comes to its sanctuary to pray, it will not prevail.
verses.16:13: This is the word that the LORD spoke about Moab long ago.
verses.16:14: And now the LORD has spoken, saying, "In three years, as the years of a hired laborer, the glory of Moab will be dishonored, along with all the great multitude; and the remnant will be very small and meager, not mighty."
verses.17:1: The pronouncement concerning Damascus: Look, Damascus is being removed from being a city, and it will become a fallen heap of ruins.
verses.17:2: Abandoned are the cities of Aroer; they will belong to flocks, and they will lie down with no one to alarm them.
verses.17:3: The fortress will cease from Ephraim, and kingship from Damascus, and the remnant of Aram—they will be like the glory of the sons of Israel, declares the LORD of hosts.
verses.17:4: And it will come about on that day that the glory of Jacob will dwindle, and the fatness of his flesh will waste away.
verses.17:5: And it will be as when a harvester gathers standing grain and his arm harvests the heads of grain; and it will be like someone gleaning heads of grain in the Valley of Rephaim.
verses.17:6: Yet gleanings will remain in it, as at the beating of an olive tree: two or three berries at the tip of the topmost bough, four or five on the branches of a fruit-bearing tree, declares the LORD, the God of Israel.
verses.17:7: On that day man will look toward his Maker, and his eyes will gaze upon the Holy One of Israel.
verses.17:8: And he will not look toward the altars, the work of his hands, nor will he gaze upon what his fingers have made—the Asherah poles and the incense altars.
verses.17:9: On that day the cities of his stronghold will be like the abandoned places of the woodland and the summit, which they abandoned before the sons of Israel; and it will become a desolation.
verses.17:10: For you have forgotten the God of your salvation and have not remembered the Rock of your stronghold. Therefore you plant plantings of delight and sow alien vine shoots.
verses.17:11: On the day of your planting you make it grow, and in the morning you bring your seed to blossom; yet gone is the harvest on a day of sickness and incurable pain.
verses.17:12: Woe! The roar of many peoples—like the roaring of seas they roar! And the thunder of nations—like the thunder of mighty waters they thunder!
verses.17:13: Nations thunder like the thunder of many waters, yet He will rebuke them, and they will flee far away, and be pursued like chaff of the mountains before the wind and like tumbleweed before a whirlwind.
verses.17:14: At evening time, look—terror! Before morning, they are gone. This is the share of those who despoil us, and the lot for those who loot us.
verses.18:1: Ah, land of buzzing wings, which lies beyond the rivers of Cush,
verses.18:2: sending envoys by the sea and in papyrus vessels upon the surface of the waters. Go, swift messengers, to a nation tall and smooth, to a people dreaded far and wide, a nation of might and trampling, whose land rivers cut through.
verses.18:3: All inhabitants of the world and dwellers on the earth, when a banner is lifted on the mountains, look, and when a horn is blown, listen.
verses.18:4: For this is what the LORD has said to me: "I will stay quiet and watch from My dwelling place, like glowing heat in sunlight, like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest."
verses.18:5: For before the harvest, when the blossoming is over and the flower becomes a ripening grape, He will cut off the shoots with pruning knives, and the spreading branches He will remove and lop off.
verses.18:6: They will be left together for the birds of prey of the mountains and for the beasts of the earth; the birds of prey will pass the summer on them, and all the beasts of the earth will pass the winter on them.
verses.18:7: At that time tribute will be brought to the LORD of hosts from a people tall and smooth, and from a people dreaded far and wide, a nation of might and trampling, whose land rivers cut through, to the place of the name of the LORD of hosts, Mount Zion.
verses.19:1: A pronouncement concerning Egypt. Look, the LORD is riding on a swift cloud and coming into Egypt; the idols of Egypt will shake before Him, and the heart of Egypt will melt within it.
verses.19:2: "And I will incite Egypt against Egypt, and they will fight, each against his brother and each against his neighbor, city against city, kingdom against kingdom.
verses.19:3: And the spirit of Egypt will be emptied out within it, and I will confound its counsel; they will consult the idols and the ghosts, the mediums and the spiritists.
verses.19:4: And I will deliver Egypt into the hand of a harsh master, and a fierce king will rule over them," declares the Lord, the LORD of hosts.
verses.19:5: And the waters will fail from the sea, and the river will be parched and dry up.
verses.19:6: The rivers will grow foul; the channels of Egypt will dwindle and be parched; reed and rush will wither away.
verses.19:7: There will be bare places along the Nile, at the mouth of the Nile, and all the sown land of the Nile will dry up, be blown away, and be no more.
verses.19:8: The fishermen will lament, and all who cast a hook into the Nile will mourn, and those who spread a net upon the surface of the waters will languish.
verses.19:9: Those who work with combed flax and those who weave white cloth will be put to shame.
verses.19:10: Its pillars will be crushed; all who work for wages will be grieved in soul.
verses.19:11: The officials of Zoan are sheer fools; the wisest of Pharaoh's counselors give senseless counsel. How can you say to Pharaoh, "I am a son of the wise, a son of kings of old"?
verses.19:12: Where, then, are your wise men? Let them tell you now, and let them know what the LORD of hosts has planned against Egypt.
verses.19:13: The officials of Zoan have become fools; the officials of Memphis are deceived; the cornerstones of its tribes have led Egypt astray.
verses.19:14: The LORD has mixed a spirit of bewilderment within it, and they have caused Egypt to reel in all its work, like a drunkard reeling in his vomit.
verses.19:15: And there will be no work for Egypt that head or tail, palm branch or reed can do.
verses.19:16: In that day Egypt will be like women, and it will tremble and be terrified before the brandishing of the hand of the LORD of hosts that He brandishes against it.
verses.19:17: And the land of Judah will become a terror to Egypt; everyone to whom it is mentioned will be terrified, because of the plan of the LORD of hosts that He is planning against it.
verses.19:18: In that day there will be five cities in the land of Egypt speaking the language of Canaan and swearing loyalty to the LORD of hosts; one will be called City of Destruction.
verses.19:19: In that day there will be an altar to the LORD in the middle of the land of Egypt, and a pillar beside its border to the LORD.
verses.19:20: It will be a sign and a witness to the LORD of hosts in the land of Egypt. When they cry out to the LORD because of oppressors, He will send them a savior and a champion, and will rescue them.
verses.19:21: And the LORD will make Himself known to Egypt, and the Egyptians will know the LORD in that day; they will worship with sacrifice and offering, and they will make a vow to the LORD and fulfill it.
verses.19:22: And the LORD will strike Egypt, striking and healing; they will return to the LORD, and He will respond to their plea and heal them.
verses.19:23: In that day there will be a highway from Egypt to Assyria; Assyria will come into Egypt and Egypt into Assyria, and the Egyptians will worship with the Assyrians.
verses.19:24: In that day Israel will be a third alongside Egypt and Assyria, a blessing in the midst of the earth,
verses.19:25: whom the LORD of hosts has blessed, saying, "Blessed be My people Egypt, and the work of My hands, Assyria, and My inheritance, Israel."
verses.20:1: In the year that the chief commander came to Ashdod, when Sargon king of Assyria sent him, he fought against Ashdod and captured it.
verses.20:2: At that time the LORD spoke through Isaiah son of Amoz, saying, "Go and untie the sackcloth from your waist, and remove your sandals from your feet." And he did so, walking naked and barefoot.
verses.20:3: Then the LORD said, "Just as My servant Isaiah has walked naked and barefoot for three years as a sign and a portent against Egypt and against Cush,
verses.20:4: so the king of Assyria will drive away the captives of Egypt and the exiles of Cush, young and old, naked and barefoot, with bared buttocks, Egypt's nakedness.
verses.20:5: And they will be dismayed and put to shame because of Cush, their hope, and because of Egypt, their pride.
verses.20:6: And the inhabitants of this coastland will say in that day, 'Look, so it is with our hope, to which we fled for help to be rescued from the king of Assyria! And how can we ourselves escape?'"
verses.21:1: A pronouncement concerning the wilderness of the sea: Like stormwinds in the Negev sweeping by, it comes out of the wilderness, from a fearsome land.
verses.21:2: A severe vision has been declared to me: the betrayer betrays, and the devastator devastates. "Go up, Elam! Lay siege, Media! I have put an end to all her groaning."
verses.21:3: Therefore my loins are filled with writhing pain; pangs have gripped me like the pangs of a woman giving birth. I am doubled over, unable to hear; I am dismayed, unable to see.
verses.21:4: My heart reels; shuddering has terrified me. He has turned the twilight of my desire into trembling for me.
verses.21:5: Set the table, spread the rugs, eat, drink! Rise up, commanders, oil the shield!
verses.21:6: For the Lord spoke to me in this way: "Go, station the lookout; whatever he sees, let him declare.
verses.21:7: When he sees chariotry, a pair of horsemen, riders on donkeys, riders on camels, let him listen intently, with utmost attentiveness."
verses.21:8: Then he cried out like a lion, "On the watchtower, Lord, I stand continually by day, and at my guard post I am stationed all the nights.
verses.21:9: And look, here comes a chariot of men, a pair of horsemen!" Then he answered and said, "Babylon has fallen, has fallen! And all the carved images of her gods He has smashed to the ground."
verses.21:10: My threshed one and son of my threshing floor, what I have heard from the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, I have declared to you.
verses.21:11: A pronouncement concerning Dumah: Someone is calling to me from Seir, "Watchman, what is left of the night? Watchman, what is left of the night?"
verses.21:12: The watchman said, "Morning has come, and night as well. If you wish to inquire, inquire; return, come!"
verses.21:13: A pronouncement concerning Arabia: In the thicket in Arabia you will spend the night, caravans of Dedanites.
verses.21:14: Bring water to meet the thirsty, inhabitants of the land of Tema; greet the fugitive with his bread.
verses.21:15: For they have fled from swords, from the unsheathed sword, from the strung bow, and from the heaviness of battle.
verses.21:16: For this is what the Lord said to me: "Within one more year, like the years of a hired laborer, all the glory of Kedar will come to an end,
verses.21:17: and the remainder of the number of bows of the mighty men of the sons of Kedar will be few," for the LORD, the God of Israel, has spoken.
verses.22:1: A pronouncement concerning the valley of vision: What is wrong with you now, that you have all gone up to the rooftops,
verses.22:2: you who are full of clamor, noisy city, exultant town? Your fallen are not fallen by the sword, nor dead in battle.
verses.22:3: All your commanders have fled together; without a bow they were taken prisoner. All of your people who were found were taken prisoner together, though they had escaped to a distance.
verses.22:4: Therefore I said, "Look away from me; let me weep bitterly. Do not press to comfort me over the devastation of the daughter of my people."
verses.22:5: For the Lord GOD of hosts has a day of turmoil and trampling and perplexity in the valley of vision, a tearing down of the wall and a cry for help to the mountain.
verses.22:6: Elam took up the quiver, with chariots of men and horsemen, and Kir uncovered the shield.
verses.22:7: Your finest valleys became filled with chariots, and the horsemen firmly stationed themselves at the gate.
verses.22:8: He stripped away the covering of Judah, and on that day you looked to the weaponry of the House of the Forest.
verses.22:9: And you saw that the breaches of the city of David were numerous, and you gathered the waters of the lower pool.
verses.22:10: And you numbered the houses of Jerusalem, and you demolished the houses to fortify the wall.
verses.22:11: You also made a reservoir between the two walls for the waters of the old pool; yet you did not look to Him who made it, nor did you see Him who fashioned it long ago.
verses.22:12: On that day the Lord GOD of hosts called for weeping and lamentation, for baldness and for binding on sackcloth.
verses.22:13: Yet look, jubilation and gladness, killing cattle and slaughtering sheep, eating meat and drinking wine: "Eat and drink, for tomorrow we die!"
verses.22:14: And the LORD of hosts revealed Himself in my ears: "This iniquity will certainly not be atoned for you until you die," said the Lord GOD of hosts.
verses.22:15: This is what the Lord GOD of hosts says: "Go, approach this steward, to Shebna, who is over the household:
verses.22:16: 'What do you have here, and whom do you have here, that you have hewn out a tomb for yourself here, hewing out his tomb on high, chiseling a dwelling for himself in the rock?
verses.22:17: Look, the LORD is about to hurl you violently away, strong man, and He will wrap you up completely.
verses.22:18: He will surely wind you up tightly like a ball into a broad land. There you will die, and there will be the chariots of your glory, you disgrace of the house of your master.
verses.22:19: And I will push you out of your post, and from your station He will pull you down.
verses.22:20: And it will happen on that day that I will call for My servant Eliakim, the son of Hilkiah,
verses.22:21: and I will dress him in your tunic, and fasten your sash securely on him, and put your authority into his hand; and he will be a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem and to the house of Judah.
verses.22:22: And I will put the key of the house of David on his shoulder; he will open, and no one will close; he will close, and no one will open.
verses.22:23: I will drive him as a peg into a secure place, and he will become a throne of glory for the house of his father.
verses.22:24: And they will hang upon him all the glory of the house of his father, the offspring and the offshoots, every small vessel, from the bowls all the way to all the jars.'"
verses.22:25: "On that day," declares the LORD of hosts, "the peg driven into a secure place will come loose; it will be sheared off and fall, and the load that was on it will be cut off," for the LORD has spoken.
verses.23:1: A pronouncement concerning Tyre: Wail, ships of Tarshish, for it has been devastated, with no house and no entry! From the land of Kittim it has been revealed to them.
verses.23:2: Be silent, inhabitants of the coastland, whom the merchants of Sidon, crossing the sea, have filled.
verses.23:3: And across many waters the grain of Shihor, the harvest of the Nile, was her revenue; and she became the marketplace of nations.
verses.23:4: Be ashamed, Sidon, for the sea has spoken, the stronghold of the sea, saying, "I have not been in labor, and I have not given birth; I have not raised young men, nor reared virgins."
verses.23:5: When the news comes to Egypt, they will writhe in anguish at the news of Tyre.
verses.23:6: Cross over to Tarshish! Wail, inhabitants of the coastland!
verses.23:7: Is this your exultant one, whose antiquity is from ancient days, whose feet used to carry her far off to sojourn?
verses.23:8: Who has purposed this against Tyre, who bestows crowns, whose merchants are princes, whose traders are the esteemed of the earth?
verses.23:9: The LORD of hosts has purposed it, to profane the pride of all splendor, to bring into contempt all the esteemed of the earth.
verses.23:10: Overflow your land like the Nile, daughter of Tarshish; there is no longer any restraint.
verses.23:11: He has stretched out His hand over the sea; He has caused kingdoms to tremble. The LORD has commanded concerning Canaan to destroy her strongholds.
verses.23:12: And He said, "You will exult no longer, oppressed virgin daughter of Sidon. Rise up, cross over to Kittim; even there you will have no rest."
verses.23:13: Look at the land of the Chaldeans! This is the people that is no more; Assyria appointed her for desert creatures. They raised up their siege towers, stripped bare her citadels; it made her a ruin.
verses.23:14: Wail, ships of Tarshish, for your stronghold has been devastated.
verses.23:15: And it will come about on that day that Tyre will be forgotten for seventy years, like the days of one king. At the end of seventy years, it will be with Tyre as in the song of the prostitute:
verses.23:16: "Take a lyre, walk around the city, forgotten prostitute! Play skillfully, sing many songs, so that you may be remembered."
verses.23:17: And it will come about at the end of seventy years that the LORD will visit Tyre, and she will return to her hire and prostitute herself with all the kingdoms of the earth upon the face of the ground.
verses.23:18: Yet her merchandise and her hire will be holy to the LORD; it will not be stored up nor hoarded, for her merchandise will belong to those who dwell before the LORD, for eating to satisfaction and for stately clothing.
verses.24:1: Look, the LORD is emptying the earth and stripping it bare; He warps its surface and disperses its inhabitants.
verses.24:2: And it will be: like the people, so the priest; like the servant, so his master; like the female servant, so her mistress; like the buyer, so the seller; like the lender, so the borrower; like the creditor, so the one who owes him.
verses.24:3: The earth will be entirely emptied and entirely plundered, because the LORD has spoken this word.
verses.24:4: The earth mourns and fades; the world languishes and fades; the lofty ones of the people of the earth languish.
verses.24:5: And the earth is defiled beneath its inhabitants, because they have transgressed laws, altered the statute, and broken the eternal covenant.
verses.24:6: Therefore a curse devours the earth, and those who dwell in it bear guilt; therefore the inhabitants of the earth are scorched, and few mortals remain.
verses.24:7: The new wine mourns, the vine languishes, and all who are glad of heart groan.
verses.24:8: The joy of tambourines has ceased, the clamor of the revelers has ended, the joy of the lyre has ceased.
verses.24:9: With singing they do not drink wine; strong drink turns bitter to those who drink it.
verses.24:10: The city of chaos is shattered; every house is shut up so that no one may come in.
verses.24:11: An outcry for wine is in the streets; all gladness has darkened; the joy of the earth has gone into exile.
verses.24:12: Desolation remains in the city, and the gate is smashed into ruin.
verses.24:13: For so it will be in the midst of the earth, among the peoples: like the beating of an olive tree, like the gleanings when the grape harvest has ended.
verses.24:14: They lift up their voice; they sing for joy; over the majesty of the LORD they cry out from the sea.
verses.24:15: Therefore in the east honor the LORD; in the coastlands of the sea, the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
verses.24:16: From the edge of the earth we have heard songs: "Splendor to the Righteous One!" But I said, "I am wasting away! I am wasting away! Woe to me! The treacherous have acted treacherously; with treachery the treacherous have acted treacherously."
verses.24:17: Terror, pit, and snare are upon you, inhabitant of the earth!
verses.24:18: And it will happen that whoever flees from the sound of the terror will fall into the pit, and whoever climbs up from the midst of the pit will be caught in the snare; for the windows from on high are opened, and the foundations of the earth quake.
verses.24:19: The earth is completely shattered; the earth is thoroughly split apart; the earth totters violently.
verses.24:20: The earth staggers wildly like a drunkard and sways to and fro like a shelter; its transgression weighs heavily upon it, and it falls and will not rise again.
verses.24:21: And it will come about on that day that the LORD will punish the host of the height on high, and the kings of the earth on the earth.
verses.24:22: They will be gathered together as prisoners into a pit, and they will be shut away in prison; after many days they will be punished.
verses.24:23: Then the moon will be abashed and the sun put to shame, because the LORD of hosts reigns on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, and before His elders there will be glory.
verses.25:1: LORD, You are my God; I will exalt You and give thanks to Your name, because You have done marvelous deeds, plans from long ago, in faithfulness and sureness.
verses.25:2: For You have turned a city into a heap, a fortified town into a ruin; the citadel of foreigners is no longer a city, and forever it will not be rebuilt.
verses.25:3: Therefore a strong people will honor You; the city of ruthless nations will fear You.
verses.25:4: For You have been a fortress for the poor, a fortress for the needy in his distress, a refuge from the rainstorm, and shade from the heat; for the blast of the ruthless is like a rainstorm against a wall.
verses.25:5: Like heat in a parched land, You subdue the clamor of foreigners; as heat by the shade of a cloud, the song of the ruthless is brought low.
verses.25:6: And the LORD of hosts will prepare for all the peoples on this mountain a banquet of rich fare, a banquet of aged wine: rich fare full of marrow, aged wine thoroughly refined.
verses.25:7: And He will swallow up on this mountain the surface of the shroud that enshrouds all the peoples, and the veil that is spread over all the nations.
verses.25:8: He will swallow up death forever, and the Lord GOD will wipe tears from every face; and the reproach of His people He will remove from the entire earth, because the LORD has spoken.
verses.25:9: And it will be said on that day, "Look, this is our God; we waited for Him so that He would save us. This is the LORD; we waited for Him; let us exult and be glad in His salvation!"
verses.25:10: For the hand of the LORD will rest on this mountain, while Moab will be trampled down in his own place, just as straw is trampled down in a dung pit.
verses.25:11: And he will spread out his hands inside it just as a swimmer spreads out his hands to swim, but He will bring down his pride along with the craftiness of his hands.
verses.25:12: And the lofty fortification of your walls He will humble, bring low, and bring down to the ground, to the very dust.
verses.26:1: On that day this song will be sung in the land of Judah: "We have a strong city; He appoints salvation as walls and a rampart.
verses.26:2: Open the gates so that a righteous nation may enter, one that keeps faithfulness.
verses.26:3: You will guard a steadfast mind in complete peace, because it trusts in You.
verses.26:4: Trust in the LORD forever and ever, because the LORD, the LORD, is an eternal Rock.
verses.26:5: For He has humbled those who dwell on high, the exalted city; He brings it low, He brings it low to the ground; He brings it down to the dust.
verses.26:6: The foot tramples it down, the feet of the afflicted, the footsteps of the poor."
verses.26:7: The way of the righteous is level; Upright One, You make even the course of the righteous.
verses.26:8: Yes, in the way of Your judgments, LORD, we have waited for You; the longing of the soul is for Your name and for Your remembrance.
verses.26:9: With my soul I long for You in the night; yes, with my spirit within me I seek You eagerly; for when Your judgments are on the earth, those who dwell in the world learn righteousness.
verses.26:10: Even if grace is shown to a wicked person, he does not learn righteousness; in a land of uprightness he commits injustice and does not see the majesty of the LORD.
verses.26:11: LORD, Your hand is raised high, yet they do not see it. Let them see Your zeal for the people and be put to shame; indeed, let the fire for Your adversaries devour them.
verses.26:12: LORD, You will ordain peace for us, because You have also accomplished all our deeds for us.
verses.26:13: LORD our God, masters besides You have ruled over us, yet by You alone we call Your name to remembrance.
verses.26:14: Dead, they will not live; departed spirits, they will not rise; therefore You have punished them and destroyed them, and blotted out every remembrance of them.
verses.26:15: You have increased the nation, LORD, You have increased the nation; You have shown Yourself glorious; You have pushed far out all the boundaries of the land.
verses.26:16: LORD, in distress they sought You out; they poured out a whisper when Your chastening was on them.
verses.26:17: As a pregnant woman nears the time to give birth, writhing and crying out in her labor pangs, so have we been in Your presence, LORD.
verses.26:18: We conceived, we writhed in labor, and it was as if we gave birth to wind; we have not achieved deliverance for the earth, nor have those who dwell in the world fallen.
verses.26:19: Your dead will live; my corpses will rise! Awake and ring out in joy, you who dwell in the dust! For Your dew is a dew of lights, and the earth will bring forth the departed spirits.
verses.26:20: Go, my people, enter your inner rooms and shut your door behind you; hide yourself for a brief moment until indignation passes by.
verses.26:21: For look, the LORD is coming out from His place to punish the inhabitant of the earth for his iniquity; and the earth will uncover its bloodshed and will no longer cover over those killed upon it.
verses.27:1: On that day the LORD, with His severe, great, and strong sword, will punish Leviathan the fleeing serpent and Leviathan the coiled serpent, and He will kill the dragon that is in the sea.
verses.27:2: On that day: A vineyard of wine! Sing about it:
verses.27:3: "I, the LORD, am its keeper; moment by moment I water it. So that no one harms it, night and day I guard it.
verses.27:4: There is no wrath in Me. If only briers and thorns faced Me in battle! I would stride against them; I would set them ablaze altogether.
verses.27:5: Or else let him take hold of My stronghold; let him make peace with Me, let him make peace with Me."
verses.27:6: In the days to come Jacob will take root; Israel will blossom and bud, and they will fill the face of the world with fruit.
verses.27:7: Has He struck him like the striking of his striker? Or has he been killed like the slaughter of those killed by Him?
verses.27:8: Measure by measure, by sending her away, You contended with her; He removed her with His severe wind on the day of the east wind.
verses.27:9: Therefore, by this Jacob's iniquity will be atoned for, and this is all the fruit of taking away his sin: when he makes all the altar stones like shattered chalkstones, Asherah poles and incense altars will not stand.
verses.27:10: For the fortified city is solitary, a dwelling place deserted and forsaken like the wilderness; there a calf grazes, and there it lies down and consumes its branches.
verses.27:11: When its boughs grow dry, they are broken off; women come and kindle fires with them. For they are not a people of understanding; therefore their Maker will not have compassion on them, and the One who formed them will not be gracious to them.
verses.27:12: And it will happen on that day that the LORD will thresh from the channel of the River to the Brook of Egypt, and you will be gleaned one by one, sons of Israel.
verses.27:13: And it will happen on that day that a great ram's horn will be sounded, and those who were perishing in the land of Assyria and the outcasts in the land of Egypt will come, and they will bow down to the LORD on the holy mountain in Jerusalem.
verses.28:1: Woe to the crown of pride of the drunkards of Ephraim, and to the fading flower, the beauty of its splendor, which is at the head of the rich valley of those overcome with wine!
verses.28:2: Look, the Lord has a strong and mighty one; like a downpour of hail, a storm of destruction, like a downpour of massive sweeping waters, he casts it down to the ground by hand.
verses.28:3: Underfoot it will be trampled, the crown of pride of the drunkards of Ephraim.
verses.28:4: And the fading flower, the beauty of its splendor, which is at the head of the rich valley, will be like a first-ripe fig before summer, which the observer sees, and while it is still in his palm he swallows it.
verses.28:5: On that day the LORD of hosts will be a crown of beauty and a diadem of splendor for the remnant of His people,
verses.28:6: and a spirit of justice for the one who sits in judgment, and strength for those who turn back the battle to the gate.
verses.28:7: And these also reel with wine and stagger with strong drink: priest and prophet reel with strong drink, they are swallowed up by wine, they stagger from strong drink; they reel in vision, they stumble in judgment.
verses.28:8: For all tables are full of vomit and filth; there is no space left.
verses.28:9: "To whom will he teach knowledge, and to whom will he explain the message? Those weaned from milk, those taken away from the breasts?
verses.28:10: For it is command after command, command after command, line after line, line after line, a little there, a little there."
verses.28:11: For with stammering speech and with another tongue He will speak to this people,
verses.28:12: to whom He said, "This is the place of rest; give rest to the weary, and this is repose," yet they were unwilling to listen.
verses.28:13: So the word of the LORD will become to them, "Command after command, command after command, line after line, line after line, a little there, a little there," so that they may go and stumble backward, and be broken, ensnared, and captured.
verses.28:14: Therefore, hear the word of the LORD, men of scoffing, rulers of this people who are in Jerusalem.
verses.28:15: For you have said, "We have made a covenant with death, and with Sheol we have made an agreement; when the sweeping scourge passes through, it will not reach us, for we have made falsehood our refuge, and in deceit we have hidden ourselves."
