verses.51:1: Listen to Me, you who pursue righteousness, who seek the LORD; look to the rock from which you were carved out, and to the hollow of the pit from which you were dug out.
verses.51:2: Look to Abraham your father, and to Sarah who gave birth to you; for while he was just one I called him, and I blessed him and multiplied him.
verses.51:3: For the LORD has comforted Zion; He has comforted all her ruins, and He has made her wilderness like Eden and her desert plain like the garden of the LORD; joy and gladness will be found in her, thanksgiving and the sound of song.
verses.51:4: Attend to Me, My people, and give ear to Me, My nation; for instruction will go out from Me, and I will establish My justice as a light to the peoples.
verses.51:5: Near is My righteousness; My salvation has gone out, and My arms will judge the peoples; for Me the coastlands will wait, and for My arm they will hope.
verses.51:6: Lift up your eyes to the heavens, and look at the earth below; for the heavens will dissipate like smoke, and the earth will wear out like a garment, and its inhabitants will die in the same way. But My salvation will be forever, and My righteousness will not be shattered.
verses.51:7: Listen to Me, you who know righteousness, a people with My instruction in their heart: do not be afraid of the reproach of mortal man, and do not be dismayed at their insults.
verses.51:8: For the moth will eat them like a garment, and the grub will eat them like wool; but My righteousness will be forever, and My salvation through generation after generation.
verses.51:9: Awake, awake, put on strength, arm of the LORD! Awake as in ancient days, the generations of ages past! Are You not the One who hacked Rahab apart, who pierced the sea monster?
verses.51:10: Are You not the One who dried up the sea, the waters of the great deep, who made the depths of the sea a road for the redeemed to cross over?
verses.51:11: And the ransomed of the LORD will return and come to Zion with ringing song, with everlasting gladness on their heads; they will attain joy and gladness; grief and sighing will flee.
verses.51:12: I, I Myself am He who comforts you. Who are you that you should fear mortal man who will die, and a son of man who will be made like grass,
verses.51:13: and have forgotten the LORD, your Maker, who stretches out the heavens and lays the foundation of the earth, and dread continually all day long before the fury of the oppressor when he makes ready to destroy? And where is the fury of the oppressor?
verses.51:14: The one bowed down will swiftly be loosed; he will not die in the pit, and his bread will not fail.
verses.51:15: And I am the LORD your God, who stirs the sea so that its waves roar—the LORD of hosts is His name.
verses.51:16: And I have placed My words in your mouth and covered you in the shadow of My hand, to plant the heavens and lay the foundation of the earth, and to say to Zion, "You are My people."
verses.51:17: Rouse yourself, rouse yourself! Arise, Jerusalem, you who have drunk from the hand of the LORD the cup of His fury; the goblet of the cup of staggering you have drunk, you have drained it dry.
verses.51:18: There is no one to guide her from all the sons she has borne, and no one holding her by the hand from all the sons she has raised.
verses.51:19: These two things have come upon you—who will grieve over you?—devastation and ruin, and famine and sword; how can I comfort you?
verses.51:20: Your sons have fainted; they lie at the head of all the streets like an antelope in a net, full of the fury of the LORD, the rebuke of your God.
verses.51:21: Therefore, hear this now, afflicted one, you who are drunk, yet not from wine:
verses.51:22: This is what your Lord, the LORD, and your God who pleads the case of His people says: "Look, I have taken from your hand the cup of staggering; the goblet of the cup of My fury you will never drink again.
verses.51:23: And I will place it in the hand of your tormentors, who said to your soul, 'Bow down so that we may pass over,' and you set your back like the ground, and like the street for those passing over."
verses.52:1: Awake, awake, put on your strength, Zion! Put on your garments of splendor, Jerusalem, the holy city; for never again will the uncircumcised and the unclean enter into you.
verses.52:2: Shake yourself from the dust; arise, take your seat, Jerusalem; loose from yourself the bonds of your neck, captive daughter of Zion.
verses.52:3: For this is what the LORD says: "For nothing you were sold, and not with money will you be redeemed."
verses.52:4: For this is what the Lord GOD says: "To Egypt My people went down at first to sojourn there, and Assyria oppressed them without cause.
verses.52:5: And now, what do I have here," declares the LORD, "since My people have been taken away for nothing? Those who rule over them howl," declares the LORD, "and continually all day long My name is treated with contempt.
verses.52:6: Therefore My people will know My name; therefore on that day they will know that I am He who speaks—here I am!"
verses.52:7: How lovely upon the mountains are the feet of a herald of good news, who proclaims peace, who heralds what is good, who proclaims salvation, who says to Zion, "Your God reigns!"
verses.52:8: The voice of your watchmen! They raise their voice; together they shout for joy, for eye to eye they will see when the LORD returns to Zion.
verses.52:9: Burst out, shout for joy together, ruins of Jerusalem! For the LORD has comforted His people; He has redeemed Jerusalem.
verses.52:10: The LORD has laid bare His holy arm before the eyes of all the nations, and all the ends of the earth will see the salvation of our God.
verses.52:11: Depart, depart, come out from there! Do not touch anything unclean; come out from her midst, make yourselves pure, you who carry the vessels of the LORD.
verses.52:12: For not in haste will you go out, and not in flight will you go; for the LORD is going before you, and your rear guard is the God of Israel.
verses.52:13: Look, My servant will act wisely; he will be exalted and lifted up, and will be exceedingly high.
verses.52:14: Just as many were appalled at you—so disfigured was his appearance beyond that of a man, and his form beyond the sons of men—
verses.52:15: so he will sprinkle many nations; kings will close their mouths because of him, for what had not been recounted to them they will see, and what they had not heard they will comprehend.
verses.53:1: Who has believed what we have heard? And the arm of the LORD, to whom has it been revealed?
verses.53:2: He grew up before Him like a young shoot, and like a root out of parched ground. He had no form and no splendor; and when we looked at him, there was no appearance that we should find him desirable.
verses.53:3: He was despised and abandoned by people, a man of pains and familiar with sickness; and like one from whom faces are hidden, he was despised, and we did not value him.
verses.53:4: Yet surely it was our sicknesses that he bore, and our pains that he carried; but we ourselves regarded him as stricken, struck down by God, and afflicted.
verses.53:5: But he was pierced because of our transgressions, crushed because of our iniquities; the discipline for our peace was on him, and by his welts healing has come to us.
verses.53:6: All of us have strayed like sheep; we have turned, each one, to his own way; and the LORD has made the iniquity of us all land on him.
verses.53:7: He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, yet he would not open his mouth; like a lamb that is led to the slaughter, and like a ewe that is silent before her shearers, he would not open his mouth.
verses.53:8: By restraint and judgment he was taken away; and as for his generation, who considered it? For he was cut off from the land of the living; because of the transgression of my people the blow fell on him.
verses.53:9: And they assigned his grave with the wicked, and with a rich man in his deaths, although he had done no violence, and there was no deceit in his mouth.
verses.53:10: Yet the LORD was pleased to crush him; He made him sick. If his soul makes a guilt offering, he will see seed, he will lengthen his days, and the pleasure of the LORD will succeed in his hand.
verses.53:11: Because of the anguish of his soul he will see, he will be satisfied; by his knowledge the righteous one, My servant, will make the many righteous, and he himself will carry their iniquities.
verses.53:12: Therefore I will give him a portion among the many, and with the mighty he will divide the spoil, because he laid bare his soul to death and was counted with the transgressors; yet he himself bore the sin of many, and for the transgressors he will intercede.
verses.54:1: "Ring out in joy, barren woman who has not given birth; burst into joyful song and cry aloud, you who have not been in labor! For more numerous are the children of the desolate woman than the children of the married woman," says the LORD.
verses.54:2: "Widen the space of your tent, and let them stretch out the curtains of your dwellings; do not hold back! Lengthen your cords, and strengthen your pegs.
verses.54:3: For to the right and to the left you will spread out, and your seed will possess nations and populate desolate cities.
verses.54:4: Do not be afraid, for you will not be ashamed; and do not be humiliated, for you will not be disgraced; for you will forget the shame of your youth, and you will no longer remember the reproach of your widowhood.
verses.54:5: For your husband is your Maker—the LORD of hosts is His name—and your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel; the God of all the earth He will be called.
verses.54:6: For as a wife abandoned and sorrowful in spirit the LORD has called you, and as a wife of youth when she is rejected," says your God.
verses.54:7: "For a short moment I abandoned you, yet with great compassion I will gather you.
verses.54:8: In a surge of anger I hid My face from you for a moment, but with everlasting loyal love I will have compassion on you," says your Redeemer, the LORD.
verses.54:9: "For this is to Me like the waters of Noah: just as I swore that the waters of Noah would not pass over the earth again, so I have sworn not to be angry with you and not to rebuke you.
verses.54:10: For though the mountains move away and the hills totter, My loyal love will not move away from you, and the covenant of My peace will not totter," says the LORD, who shows you compassion.
verses.54:11: "Afflicted one, tossed by storms, not comforted: look, I am setting your stones in antimony, and I will lay your foundation with sapphires.
verses.54:12: And I will make your pinnacles of rubies, your gates of sparkling stones, and all your border of precious stones.
verses.54:13: And all your children will be disciples of the LORD, and abundant will be the peace of your children.
verses.54:14: By righteousness you will be established; be far from oppression, for you will not be afraid, and from terror, for it will not approach you.
verses.54:15: Look, if anyone indeed attacks, it is not from Me; whoever attacks you will fall because of you.
verses.54:16: See, I have created the smith who blows on the fire of charcoal and brings out a weapon for its task, and I have created the destroyer to ravage.
verses.54:17: No weapon crafted against you will succeed, and every tongue that rises against you in judgment you will convict. This is the inheritance of the servants of the LORD, and their righteousness is from Me," declares the LORD.
verses.55:1: Come, every thirsty one, come to the waters, and whoever has no silver, come, purchase and eat; and come, purchase wine and milk without silver and without payment.
verses.55:2: Why do you weigh out silver for what is not bread, and your labor for what brings no satisfaction? Listen intently to Me, and eat what is good, and let your soul delight itself in rich fare.
verses.55:3: Turn your ear and come to Me; listen, and your soul will live; and I will make an eternal covenant for you, the sure acts of loyal love to David.
verses.55:4: Look, I have appointed him as a witness to peoples, a ruler and commander of peoples.
verses.55:5: Look, you will summon a nation you do not know, and a nation that has not known you will run to you, for the sake of the LORD your God, and for the Holy One of Israel, because He has glorified you.
verses.55:6: Seek the LORD while He can be found; call out to Him while He is near.
verses.55:7: Let the wicked abandon his way, and the man of iniquity his thoughts; and let him return to the LORD, that He may show him compassion, and to our God, for He will forgive abundantly.
verses.55:8: For My thoughts are not your thoughts, and your ways are not My ways, declares the LORD.
verses.55:9: For just as the heavens are higher than the earth, so My ways stand higher than your ways, and My thoughts than your thoughts.
verses.55:10: For just as the rain and the snow descend from the heavens and do not return there, but instead saturate the earth, causing it to bring forth and sprout, and giving seed to the one who sows and bread to the one who eats,
verses.55:11: so My word will be that goes out from My mouth: it will not return to Me empty, but instead it will carry out what I delight in, and it will succeed in that for which I sent it.
verses.55:12: For with joy you will go out, and in peace you will be led along; the mountains and the hills will burst into joyful shouting before you, and all the trees of the field will clap their hands.
verses.55:13: Instead of the thornbush a cypress will grow up, and instead of the brier a myrtle will grow up; and it will become a name for the LORD, an eternal sign that will not be cut off.
verses.56:1: This is what the LORD says: "Keep justice and practice righteousness, for My salvation is near to come, and My righteousness to be revealed."
verses.56:2: Blessed is the mortal who does this, and the son of man who holds fast to it, who keeps the Sabbath without profaning it, and who keeps his hand from doing anything evil.
verses.56:3: And do not let the foreigner who has joined himself to the LORD say, "The LORD will certainly separate me from His people," and do not let the eunuch say, "Look, I am a dry tree."
verses.56:4: For this is what the LORD says: "To the eunuchs who keep My Sabbaths, and choose what I delight in, and hold fast to My covenant,
verses.56:5: to them I will give in My house and within My walls a monument and a name better than sons and daughters; I will give each one an eternal name that will not be cut off.
verses.56:6: And the foreigners who join themselves to the LORD to minister to Him, and to love the name of the LORD, to be servants to Him, everyone who keeps the Sabbath without profaning it, and those who hold fast to My covenant,
verses.56:7: I will bring them to My holy mountain and gladden them in My house of prayer; their burnt offerings and their sacrifices will find acceptance on My altar, because My house will be called a house of prayer for all the peoples."
verses.56:8: The Lord GOD, who gathers the banished of Israel, declares: "I will gather still others to him, in addition to his gathered ones."
verses.56:9: All you wild animals of the field, come to eat, all you wild animals in the forest!
verses.56:10: His watchmen are blind; they all know nothing. They are all mute dogs that cannot bark, dreaming, lying down, loving to doze.
verses.56:11: And the dogs are fierce in appetite; they do not know satisfaction. And they are shepherds who do not know how to understand; all of them have turned to their own way, each man for his dishonest gain, without exception.
verses.57:1: The righteous one perishes, and no one takes it to heart; and men of loyal love are taken away, with no one understanding that the righteous one is taken away from calamity.
verses.57:2: He comes into peace; they rest on their beds, whoever walks in his uprightness.
verses.57:3: But you, come close here, sons of a sorceress, seed of an adulterer and of her who commits prostitution!
verses.57:4: At whom are you mocking? At whom do you open wide the mouth and stretch out the tongue? Are you not children of rebellion, seed of falsehood,
verses.57:5: you who are inflamed with passion among the oaks, beneath every lush tree, who slaughter the children in the ravines, beneath the clefts of the rocks?
verses.57:6: Your portion is among the smooth stones of the ravine; they, yes they, are your lot. Even to them you have poured out a drink offering; you have offered up a grain offering. Should I be appeased over these things?
verses.57:7: On a high and elevated mountain you placed your bed; even there you went up to offer a sacrifice.
verses.57:8: Behind the door and the doorpost you placed your memorial; for away from Me you uncovered yourself and climbed up, you widened your bed and struck a bargain for yourself with them; you loved their bed, you gazed at nakedness.
verses.57:9: You traveled to the king with oil and multiplied your perfumes; you sent out your envoys far away, and brought yourself low down to Sheol.
verses.57:10: From the length of your way you grew weary, yet you did not say, "It is hopeless." You found revival of your strength; therefore you did not weaken.
verses.57:11: And whom did you dread and fear, that you dealt falsely, and did not remember Me, nor take it to your heart? Have I not been keeping silent, even from long ago, so that you do not fear Me?
verses.57:12: I Myself will announce your righteousness and your works, and they will not benefit you.
verses.57:13: When you cry out, let your gathered throngs rescue you! But a wind will carry them all off; a breath will snatch them away. Yet the one who takes refuge in Me will inherit the land and will possess My holy mountain.
verses.57:14: And it will be said, "Build up, build up, clear a way! Remove the stumbling block from the way of My people!"
verses.57:15: For this is what the One who is high and exalted, who dwells in eternity, and whose name is Holy says: "I dwell in a high and holy place, and with the one who is crushed and lowly in spirit, to revive the spirit of the lowly, and to revive the heart of the crushed.
verses.57:16: For I will not strive forever, and I will not be wrathful perpetually; for the spirit would fail before Me, and the breaths of life that I Myself have made.
verses.57:17: Because of the iniquity of his dishonest gain I was wrathful and struck him; I hid Myself and was wrathful, yet he kept going waywardly in the way of his heart.
verses.57:18: I have seen his ways, yet I will heal him; I will guide him and restore comforts to him and to his mourners,
verses.57:19: creating the fruit of the lips. Peace, peace to the one who is far and to the one who is near," says the LORD, "and I will heal him."
verses.57:20: But the wicked are like the churning sea, for it cannot be still, and its waters churn up mire and mud.
verses.57:21: "There is no peace," my God says, "for the wicked."
verses.58:1: Call out with full throat, do not hold back; raise your voice like a ram's horn, and announce to My people their rebellion, and to the house of Jacob their sins.
verses.58:2: Yet day by day they seek Me, and take pleasure in knowing My ways, like a nation that has done righteousness and has not abandoned the justice of its God; they ask Me for righteous judgments; they take pleasure in the nearness of God.
verses.58:3: "Why have we fasted, and You have not seen? We have afflicted our souls, and You do not take notice." Look, on the day of your fast you find pleasure, and you drive all your workers hard.
verses.58:4: See, you fast for dispute and strife, and to strike with a fist of wickedness. You do not fast as on this day to cause your voice to be heard on high.
verses.58:5: Is a fast that I choose to be like this, a day for a man to afflict his soul? Is it to bow down his head like a reed, and spread out sackcloth and ashes? Will you call this a fast, and a day of favor to the LORD?
verses.58:6: Is this not the fast that I choose: to untie the fetters of wickedness, to undo the straps of the yoke, and to send the crushed away free, and that you snap every yoke?
verses.58:7: Is it not to break your bread for the hungry, and bring the homeless poor into the house; when you see someone naked, to cover him, and not to hide yourself from your own flesh?
verses.58:8: Then your light will burst open like the dawn, and your healing will sprout swiftly; your righteousness will walk ahead of you; the glory of the LORD will serve as your rear guard.
verses.58:9: Then you will call, and the LORD will answer; you will cry for help, and He will say, "Here I am." If you remove the yoke from your midst, the pointing of the finger, and speaking wrongdoing,
verses.58:10: and extend your soul to the hungry, and satisfy the afflicted soul, then your light will rise in the darkness, and your gloom will be like midday.
verses.58:11: And the LORD will lead you continually, and satisfy your soul in scorched places, and invigorate your bones; you will become like a well-watered garden, and like a source of water whose waters never fail.
verses.58:12: Those from among you will rebuild the ancient ruins; you will raise up the foundations of generation upon generation; and you will be called Mender of the Breach, Restorer of Paths to Dwell In.
verses.58:13: If you turn your foot back from the Sabbath, from doing your own pleasures on My holy day, and call the Sabbath a delight, the holy day of the LORD honorable, and honor it by not doing your own ways, not finding your own pleasure, or speaking mere words,
verses.58:14: then you will take delight in the LORD, and I will make you ride upon the heights of the earth, and I will feed you with the inheritance of Jacob your father; for the mouth of the LORD has spoken.
verses.59:1: Look, the hand of the LORD is not too short to save, nor is His ear too heavy to hear.
verses.59:2: Rather, your iniquities have been making a separation between you and your God, and your sins have concealed His face from you so that He does not hear.
verses.59:3: For your palms are defiled with blood, and your fingers with iniquity; your lips have spoken falsehood, your tongue mutters injustice.
verses.59:4: No one brings suit in righteousness, and no one pleads a case in faithfulness; they trust in emptiness and speak lies; they conceive trouble and give birth to wrongdoing.
verses.59:5: They hatch adder's eggs and weave spider's webs; the one who eats from their eggs dies, and what is crushed splits open into a viper.
verses.59:6: Their webs will not become clothing, nor will they cover themselves with their works; their works are works of wrongdoing, and an act of violence is in their palms.
verses.59:7: Their feet run to evil, and they hurry to shed innocent blood; their thoughts are thoughts of wrongdoing; devastation and shattering are on their highways.
verses.59:8: They have not known the way of peace, and there is no justice in their tracks; they have twisted their paths for themselves; whoever treads on them knows no peace.
verses.59:9: Therefore justice is far from us, and righteousness does not reach us; we wait for light, and look, darkness; for brightness, yet we walk about in deep gloom.
verses.59:10: We grope for a wall like the blind, and like those without eyes we grope; we stumble at midday as in twilight; among the vigorous we are like the dead.
verses.59:11: All of us growl like bears, and like doves we moan continually; we wait for justice, and there is none; for salvation, yet it is far from us.
verses.59:12: For our rebellions have multiplied before You, and our sins testify against us; for our rebellions are with us, and as for our iniquities, we know them:
verses.59:13: rebelling against and denying the LORD, and turning back from following our God, speaking oppression and revolt, conceiving and muttering from the heart words of falsehood.
verses.59:14: And justice is turned backward, and righteousness stands far off; for truth has stumbled in the public square, and uprightness cannot enter.
verses.59:15: Thus truth is missing, and the one who turns aside from evil becomes prey. And the LORD saw it, and it was displeasing in His eyes that there was no justice.
verses.59:16: He saw that there was no man, and He was appalled that there was no one to intervene; then His own arm brought salvation for Him, and His righteousness itself upheld Him.
verses.59:17: He put on righteousness like a coat of mail, with a helmet of salvation on His head; He put on garments of vengeance as attire, and wrapped Himself in zeal like a cloak.
verses.59:18: According to deeds, accordingly He will repay: wrath to His adversaries, recompense to His enemies; to the coastlands He will repay recompense.
verses.59:19: And they will fear the name of the LORD from the west, and His glory from the rising of the sun; for He will come like a pent-up river that the breath of the LORD drives forward.
verses.59:20: And a Redeemer will come to Zion, and to those in Jacob who turn from rebellion, declares the LORD.
verses.59:21: "And as for Me, this is My covenant with them," says the LORD: "My Spirit who is upon you, and My words that I have placed in your mouth, will not depart from your mouth, nor from the mouth of your seed, nor from the mouth of your seed's seed," says the LORD, "from this moment and forever."
verses.60:1: Rise up, shine, for your light has come, and the glory of the LORD has dawned upon you.
verses.60:2: For look, darkness will cover the earth, and thick gloom the peoples; yet upon you the LORD will dawn, and His glory will appear over you.
verses.60:3: And nations will walk to your light, and kings to the brightness of your dawn.
verses.60:4: Lift your eyes all around and see: they have all gathered together, they come to you; your sons will come from afar, and your daughters will be carried at the hip.
verses.60:5: Then you will see and be radiant, and your heart will throb and expand; because the abundance of the sea will be turned toward you, the wealth of the nations will come to you.
verses.60:6: A throng of camels will cover you, the young camels of Midian and Ephah; all of them will come from Sheba; they will carry gold and frankincense, and herald the praises of the LORD.
verses.60:7: All the flocks of Kedar will be gathered to you; the rams of Nebaioth will minister to you; they will go up with acceptance onto My altar, and I will beautify the house of My splendor.
verses.60:8: Who are these that fly like a cloud, and like doves to their windows?
verses.60:9: Surely the coastlands wait for Me, and the ships of Tarshish first, to bring your sons from afar, their silver and their gold with them, for the name of the LORD your God, and for the Holy One of Israel, because He has glorified you.
verses.60:10: And foreigners will build your walls, and their kings will minister to you; for in My wrath I struck you, yet in My favor I have had compassion on you.
verses.60:11: Your gates will stand open continually; day and night they will not be shut, to bring to you the wealth of the nations, with their kings led along.
verses.60:12: For the nation and the kingdom that do not serve you will perish, and those nations will be utterly laid waste.
verses.60:13: The glory of Lebanon will come to you, the cypress, the plane tree, and the boxwood together, to beautify the place of My sanctuary; and I will make glorious the place of My feet.
verses.60:14: The sons of those who afflicted you will walk to you bowing low, and all who despised you will bow down at the soles of your feet; and they will call you the City of the LORD, Zion of the Holy One of Israel.
verses.60:15: Instead of your being forsaken and hated, with no one passing through, I will make you an everlasting majesty, a joy from generation to generation.
verses.60:16: You will nurse on the milk of nations, and you will nurse at the breast of kings; and you will know that I, the LORD, am your Savior and your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.
verses.60:17: Instead of bronze I will bring gold, and instead of iron I will bring silver, and instead of wood, bronze, and instead of stones, iron. And I will make your oversight peace, and your taskmasters righteousness.
verses.60:18: Violence will no longer be heard in your land, nor devastation and shattering within your borders; but you will call your walls Salvation, and your gates Praise.
verses.60:19: The sun will no longer serve as your light by day, nor for brightness will the moon give light to you; rather, the LORD will be an everlasting light for you, and your God your splendor.
verses.60:20: Your sun will no longer go down, nor will your moon be withdrawn; for the LORD will be an everlasting light for you, and the days of your mourning will be completed.
verses.60:21: Your people will all be righteous; they will possess the land forever, the shoot of My plantings, the work of My hands, that I may display My splendor.
verses.60:22: The small one will become a thousand, and the least one a mighty nation. I, the LORD, will hasten it at its time.
verses.61:1: The Spirit of the Lord GOD is on me, because the LORD has anointed me to announce good news to the humble; He has sent me to bandage those broken in heart, to proclaim release to the captives and freedom to those who are bound,
verses.61:2: to proclaim a year of the LORD's favor and a day of our God's vengeance, to console all mourners,
verses.61:3: to provide for the mourners of Zion, to give them a headdress in place of ashes, oil of joy in place of mourning, a cloak of praise in place of a failing spirit. And they will be called terebinths of righteousness, a planting of the LORD, so that He may glorify Himself.
verses.61:4: They will build up the ruins of old; they will raise up the desolations of former times, and they will renew the cities of ruin, the desolations of generation after generation.
verses.61:5: Strangers will stand and shepherd your flock, and foreigners will be your plowmen and your vineyard workers.
verses.61:6: But you will be called "Priests of the LORD," and it will be said of you, "Ministers of our God." You will consume the wealth of nations, and you will boast in their glory.
verses.61:7: In place of your shame there will be a double share, and in place of disgrace they will shout for joy over their portion; therefore in their land they will inherit a double share, and everlasting gladness will belong to them.
verses.61:8: For I, the LORD, love justice; I hate robbery in a burnt offering. And I will give their recompense in faithfulness, and I will make an everlasting covenant with them.
verses.61:9: Their seed will become known among the nations, and their posterity in the midst of the peoples; everyone who sees them will recognize them, that they are a seed whom the LORD has blessed.
verses.61:10: I rejoice exceedingly in the LORD; my soul exults in my God, for He has dressed me in garments of salvation, and He has wrapped me in a robe of righteousness, like a bridegroom who puts on a headdress like a priest, and like a bride who arrays herself with her ornaments.
verses.61:11: For just as the earth brings out its sprouts, and as a garden makes its sown seeds sprout, so the Lord GOD will make righteousness and praise sprout in the sight of all the nations.
verses.62:1: For the sake of Zion I will not remain silent, and for the sake of Jerusalem I will not be still, until her righteousness goes out like radiance, and her salvation like a torch that blazes.
verses.62:2: And nations will see your righteousness, and all kings your glory; and you will be called a new name, which the mouth of the LORD will specify.
verses.62:3: And you will be a crown of splendor in the hand of the LORD, and a royal turban in the palm of your God.
verses.62:4: No longer will it be said of you, "Forsaken," and of your land it will no longer be said, "Desolate"; instead, you will be called "My Delight Is in Her," and your land "Married," for the LORD delights in you, and your land will be married.
verses.62:5: For as a young man marries a virgin, your sons will marry you; and with the joy of a bridegroom over a bride, your God will rejoice over you.
verses.62:6: On your walls, Jerusalem, I have stationed watchmen; all day and all night, continually, they will not remain silent. You who remind the LORD, let there be no rest for you,
verses.62:7: and do not give Him rest until He firmly establishes and until He makes Jerusalem a praise in the earth.
verses.62:8: The LORD has sworn by His right hand and by the arm of His strength: "Surely I will no longer give your grain as food to your enemies, nor will foreigners drink your new wine for which you have toiled;
verses.62:9: rather, those who harvest it will eat it and praise the LORD, and those who gather it will drink it in My holy courts."
verses.62:10: Pass through, pass through the gates; clear the way of the people; build up, build up the highway, rid it of stones; raise a banner over the peoples.
verses.62:11: Look, the LORD has announced to the end of the earth: "Say to the daughter of Zion, 'See, your salvation is coming! Look, His reward is with Him, and His recompense is before Him.'"
verses.62:12: And they will call them "The Holy People, the Redeemed of the LORD," and you will be called "Sought After, a City Not Forsaken."
verses.63:1: Who is this coming from Edom, with crimson garments from Bozrah, this One stately in His attire, striding in the abundance of His strength? "It is I, speaking in righteousness, powerful to save."
verses.63:2: Why is there red on Your attire, and Your garments like those of one treading in a winepress?
verses.63:3: "I have trodden the wine trough by Myself, and from the peoples no man was with Me; I trod them in My anger and trampled them in My fury, and their lifeblood spattered onto My garments, and I stained all My attire.
verses.63:4: For a day of vengeance was in My heart, and the year of My redemption had come.
verses.63:5: I looked, and there was no helper; I was astounded, and there was no one to sustain; so My own arm won salvation for Me, and My fury itself sustained Me.
verses.63:6: And I trampled peoples in My anger, made them drunk in My fury, and brought their lifeblood down to the ground."
verses.63:7: I will bring to remembrance the LORD's acts of loyal love, the praises of the LORD, in keeping with everything the LORD has bestowed on us, and the abundant goodness toward the house of Israel that He bestowed on them in accordance with His compassions and in accordance with the multitude of His acts of loyal love.
verses.63:8: And He said, "Truly they are My people, children who will not prove false." So He became a Savior to them.
verses.63:9: In all their distress He was distressed, and the angel of His presence saved them; in His love and in His mercy He Himself redeemed them, and He raised them up and bore them all the days of old.
verses.63:10: Yet they rebelled and grieved His Holy Spirit; so He turned into an enemy toward them, and He Himself fought against them.
verses.63:11: Then His people recalled the days of old, of Moses: "Where is the One who brought them up from the sea along with the shepherds of His flock? Where is the One who placed His Holy Spirit within them,
verses.63:12: who made the arm of His splendor move at the right hand of Moses, who split the waters before them to make an everlasting name for Himself,
verses.63:13: who guided them through the depths?" As a horse in the wilderness, they did not stumble.
verses.63:14: Like livestock descending into the valley, the Spirit of the LORD granted them rest; so You led Your people, to make a name of splendor for Yourself.
verses.63:15: Look down from heaven and see, from the habitation of Your holiness and Your splendor. Where are Your zeal and Your mighty acts? The yearning of Your inner being and Your compassions are held back toward me.
verses.63:16: For You are our Father, even though Abraham does not know us and Israel does not recognize us; You, LORD, are our Father; "Our Redeemer from Everlasting" is Your name.
verses.63:17: Why, LORD, do You cause us to wander from Your ways and harden our heart away from fearing You? Turn back for the sake of Your servants, the tribes of Your inheritance.
verses.63:18: For a short while Your holy people held possession; our adversaries have trampled Your sanctuary.
verses.63:19: We have become like those over whom You have not ruled from long ago, over whom Your name has not been called. If only You would tear open the heavens and come down, so that mountains would quake before Your presence!
verses.64:1: As fire ignites brushwood and fire sets water boiling, to make Your name known to Your foes, nations tremble at Your presence.
verses.64:2: When You performed awesome deeds we did not anticipate, You came down; mountains quaked at Your presence.
verses.64:3: And from ancient times they have not heard nor given ear, nor has an eye seen a God apart from You who acts for the one who waits for Him.
verses.64:4: You meet the one who rejoices and practices righteousness, those who remember You in Your ways. Look, You were angry, and we sinned; in them we have been a long time, and shall we be saved?
verses.64:5: And we have all become like someone unclean, and all our righteous deeds are like a menstrual cloth; we all wither like a leaf, and our iniquities, like the wind, carry us away.
verses.64:6: And there is no one who calls on Your name, who stirs himself to lay hold of You, because You have hidden Your face from us and melted us in the hand of our iniquity.
verses.64:7: Yet now, LORD, You are our Father; we are the clay and You are our potter; all of us are the work of Your hand.
verses.64:8: Do not be exceedingly angry, LORD, and do not remember iniquity forever. Now, please look: all of us are Your people.
verses.64:9: Your holy cities have turned into a wilderness; Zion has turned into a wilderness, Jerusalem a wasteland.
verses.64:10: Our holy and splendid house, where our fathers praised You, has been burned up with fire, and all our treasured things have become a ruin.
verses.64:11: Will You hold Yourself back over these things, LORD? Will You remain silent and afflict us exceedingly?
verses.65:1: I let Myself be consulted by those who did not ask; I let Myself be found by those who did not seek Me. I said, "Here I am, here I am," to a nation that was not called by My name.
verses.65:2: I have spread out My hands all day long to a stubborn people, who walk on a way that is not good, after their own thoughts.
verses.65:3: The people who continually provoke Me before My face, sacrificing in the gardens and burning incense on the bricks,
verses.65:4: who sit in the tombs and stay the night in hidden places, who eat the flesh of swine, while broth of foul meat is in their vessels,
verses.65:5: who say, "Stay by yourself; do not approach me, for I am holier than you"—these are smoke in My nostrils, a fire burning all day long.
verses.65:6: Look, it is written before Me: I will not remain silent, but I will repay—and I will repay onto their lap—
verses.65:7: your iniquities and the iniquities of your fathers together, says the LORD, who burned incense on the mountains and reviled Me on the hills; so I will first measure out their wage into their lap.
verses.65:8: This is what the LORD says: "Just as new wine is found in the cluster and someone says, 'Do not destroy it, because a blessing is in it,' so will I act for the sake of My servants, so as not to destroy all of it.
verses.65:9: I will bring out seed from Jacob, and from Judah an inheritor of My mountains; My chosen ones will inherit it, and My servants will reside there.
verses.65:10: Sharon will become a grazing land for flocks, and the Valley of Achor a resting place for cattle, for My people who have sought Me.
verses.65:11: But as for you who abandon the LORD, who forget My holy mountain, who prepare a table for Fortune and fill up mixed wine for Destiny,
verses.65:12: I will destine you for the sword, and all of you will kneel down to the slaughter, because I called and you did not answer, I spoke and you did not listen; instead, you did evil in My eyes and chose that in which I took no pleasure."
verses.65:13: Therefore, this is what the Lord GOD says: "Look, My servants will eat, but you will go hungry; look, My servants will drink, but you will go thirsty; look, My servants will rejoice, but you will be shamed.
verses.65:14: Look, My servants will shout for joy from gladness of heart, but you will cry out from anguish of heart, and from a broken spirit you will wail.
verses.65:15: You will leave your name behind as an oath-curse for My chosen ones, and the Lord GOD will put you to death, while He will call His servants by a different name,
verses.65:16: so that whoever blesses himself in the land will bless himself by the God of truth, and whoever swears in the land will swear by the God of truth, because the former distresses have been forgotten, and because they have been hidden from My eyes.
verses.65:17: For look, I am creating new heavens and a new earth; the former things will not be remembered, nor will they arise in the heart.
verses.65:18: Instead, be joyful and exult forever and ever in what I am creating; for look, I am creating Jerusalem as exultation and her people as joy.
verses.65:19: I will exult in Jerusalem and be joyful in My people; never again will the sound of weeping or the sound of outcry be heard in her.
verses.65:20: There will no longer be an infant there of a few days, nor an elderly man who does not complete his days; for the youth will die at a hundred years old, and the sinner at a hundred years old will be cursed.
verses.65:21: They will build houses and live in them, and they will plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
verses.65:22: They will not build and another live there; they will not plant and another eat; for like the days of a tree will be the days of My people, and My chosen ones will use to the full the work of their hands.
verses.65:23: They will not toil in vain, nor bear children for sudden disaster, because they are the seed of the LORD's blessed ones, and their descendants are with them.
verses.65:24: And it will happen that before they call, I will answer, and while they are still speaking, I will listen.
verses.65:25: Wolf and lamb will graze together, and the lion will eat straw like cattle; as for the serpent, dust will be its food. They will neither harm nor destroy on all My holy mountain," says the LORD.
verses.66:1: This is what the LORD says: "The heavens are My throne, and the earth is the footstool for My feet. Where is a house that you would build for Me, and where is a place of My rest?
verses.66:2: My hand made all these things, and all these things came into existence," declares the LORD. "Yet to this person I will look: to one who is humble and stricken in spirit, and who trembles at My word.
verses.66:3: One who slaughters an ox is like one who strikes down a man; one who sacrifices a lamb, like one who snaps a dog's neck; one who offers up a grain offering, like offering swine's blood; one who offers a memorial of frankincense, like one who blesses an idol. Just as they have chosen their own ways, and their soul takes pleasure in their detestable things,
verses.66:4: so I too will choose their afflictions and bring the things they fear upon them; because I called and there was no one answering, I spoke and they did not listen; instead, they did evil in My eyes and chose that in which I took no pleasure."
verses.66:5: Listen to the word of the LORD, you who tremble at His word: "Your brothers who hate you, who cast you out for the sake of My name, have said, 'May the LORD show His glory, so that we may witness your joy!' Yet they themselves will be shamed."
verses.66:6: A sound of tumult from the city, a voice from the temple—the voice of the LORD repaying retribution to His enemies!
verses.66:7: Before she writhed in labor, she gave birth; before a birth pang came to her, she delivered a male child.
verses.66:8: Who has heard of something like this? Who has seen things like these? Can a land be brought forth in a single day, or can a nation be born at one stroke? For as soon as Zion writhed in labor, she also gave birth to her sons.
verses.66:9: "Would I bring to the moment of birth and not cause delivery?" says the LORD. "Or would I, the One who causes delivery, close the womb?" says your God.
verses.66:10: Rejoice with Jerusalem and exult in her, all who love her; be joyful with her in joy, all who mourn over her,
verses.66:11: so that you may nurse and be filled from the breast of her comfort, so that you may drink deeply and take delight from the abundance of her glory.
verses.66:12: For this is what the LORD says: "Look, I am extending peace toward her like a river, and the glory of nations like a rushing stream; and you will nurse, you will be carried at the hip, and you will be bounced upon the knees.
verses.66:13: Like a man whose mother comforts him, so I Myself will comfort you, and in Jerusalem you will be comforted.
verses.66:14: You will see, and your heart will be joyful, and your bones will sprout like tender grass; the hand of the LORD will become known among His servants, and He will express indignation against His enemies."
verses.66:15: For look, the LORD is coming in fire, and His chariots are like the whirlwind, to discharge His anger in fury and His rebuke in flames of fire.
verses.66:16: For by fire the LORD is entering into judgment, and by His sword with all flesh; and many will be those struck down by the LORD.
verses.66:17: "Those who consecrate themselves and purify themselves for the gardens, behind one in the middle, eating the flesh of swine and the detestable thing and the mouse—together they will come to an end," declares the LORD.
verses.66:18: "And I know their deeds and their thoughts; the time is coming to gather all the nations and languages, and they will come and see My glory.
verses.66:19: I will place a sign among them and send out survivors from them to the nations—to Tarshish, Pul, and Lud, who draw the bow, to Tubal and Javan, to the distant coastlands that have not heard of My fame and have not seen My glory—and they will proclaim My glory among the nations.
verses.66:20: And they will bring all your brothers out of all the nations as an offering to the LORD—on horses, in chariots, in covered wagons, on mules, and on dromedaries—to My holy mountain Jerusalem," says the LORD, "just as the sons of Israel bring the offering in a clean vessel to the house of the LORD.
verses.66:21: And from among them as well I will take some as priests and as Levites," says the LORD.
verses.66:22: "For just as the new heavens and the new earth that I am making will stand before Me," declares the LORD, "so your seed and your name will stand.
verses.66:23: And it will come about that from one new moon to another, and from one Sabbath to another, all flesh will come to bow down before Me," says the LORD.
verses.66:24: "And they will go out and look upon the corpses of the men who rebelled against Me; for their worm will not die, and their fire will not go out, and they will be a horror to all flesh."

notes.1:7: The Masoretic Text repeats zarim ("foreigners") in the final clause ("an overthrow by foreigners"), matching the preceding line; the noun mahpekah ("overthrow") is also the term commonly associated with the destruction of Sodom (cf. v. 9).
notes.1:12: The Masoretic vocalization points lera'ot as a Niphal infinitive construct of ra'ah ("to appear") with panai ("My face/presence") as an adverbial accusative, the traditional pious pointing of the idiom for appearing at the sanctuary.
notes.1:17: The Piel imperative ashru ("set straight/correct") governs the rare noun chamos, which is understood either as an active agent ("oppressor/ruthless one") or passively as "the oppressed" (yielding "relieve the oppressed").
notes.1:20: Hebrew creates a sharp wordplay with v. 19 using the same verb akal ("eat/devour"): Qal active to'kelu ("you will eat") in v. 19 is answered by Pual passive te'ukkelu ("you will be devoured") with instrumental cherev ("by the sword") in v. 20.
notes.1:29: The Masoretic Text shifts mid-sentence from third-person plural ("they will be ashamed") to second-person plural ("you desired ... you will be disgraced ... you chose"), a classic prophetic shift of person retained here.
notes.2:6: The phrase mal'u miqqedem literally reads "they are filled from the east" without naming the imported practices; yaspiqu (Hiphil of sapaq) denotes slapping or clasping hands to seal a bargain or pact, though some relate it to an Aramaic sense "abound with."
notes.2:12: The final word weshapel is read here as a Qal consecutive perfect verb ("so that it will be brought low"), matching the verbal usage of shapel in vv. 11 and 17 and the list of lofty objects in vv. 13-16, rather than as an adjective ("and low").
notes.2:16: The rare plural construct sekiyyot ("vessels") appears only here in the Hebrew Bible; parallel to "ships of Tarshish," it is widely linked to an Egyptian and Ugaritic term for seagoing craft, though older interpreters derived it from a root meaning "to look at" ("desirable sights" or "works of art").
notes.2:20: The Masoretic Text divides lachpor perot into two words, widely understood as a split spelling of the reduplicated animal name chaparparot ("moles" or "shrews," literally "diggers"), paired here with "bats."
notes.3:1: The masculine and feminine pairing מַשְׁעֵן וּמַשְׁעֵנָה (lit. "support and prop", both from the root שׁען) is a Hebrew merism expressing every kind of support.
notes.3:15: Ketiv reads מלכם (a contracted one-word spelling), while Qere separates it into two words, מַה־לָּכֶם ("what is it to you?"), which is translated here.
notes.3:16: Ketiv reads נטוות while Qere reads נְטוּיוֹת (Qal passive participle feminine plural of נטה, "stretched out"); both convey the same sense with an orthographic/morphological variation.
notes.3:17: The hapax Piel verb שִׂפַּח is traditionally linked to סַפַּחַת ("scab"), though some take it as "make bare/bald"; פׇּתְהֵן ("their private parts") is a euphemism paired with Piel יְעָרֶה ("expose/lay bare").
notes.3:24: The closing phrase כִּי־תַחַת יֹפִי uses the rare noun כִּי ("brand/burn mark", from the root כוה) rather than the conjunction "for", reversing the preceding "instead of X, Y" sequence into a chiastic climax.
notes.4:2: The noun צֶמַח literally means "sprout", "shoot", or "growth" (the same noun used of a Davidic figure in Jer 23:5; 33:15; Zech 3:8; 6:12), standing here in parallelism with פְרִי הָאָרֶץ ("the fruit of the land").
notes.4:4: The conjunction אִם ("if") with a perfect (רָחַץ) and imperfect (יָדִיחַ) functions temporally ("once/when"); the Piel infinitive בָּעֵר carries the dual sense of "burning" and "purging away".
notes.5:1: The idiom בְּקֶרֶן בֶּן־שָׁמֶן literally reads "on a horn, a son of fatness/oil", denoting a fertile hillside or ridge.
notes.5:7: The Hebrew employs striking wordplay pairing near-homophones: מִשְׁפָּט (mishpat, "justice") with מִשְׂפָּח (mispach, "bloodshed/oppression"), and צְדָקָה (tsedaqah, "righteousness") with צְעָקָה (tse'aqah, "outcry").
notes.5:10: A צֶמֶד ("yoke") is the area a pair of oxen could plow in a day (roughly an acre); a בַּת ("bath") is a liquid measure of about 22 liters, and a חֹמֶר ("homer") equals ten אֵיפָה ("ephahs"), indicating a severe crop failure.
notes.5:17: The Masoretic text vocalizes מֵחִים ("fat ones", figuratively the wealthy) and גָּרִים (Qal participle of גור, "sojourners/strangers"), whereas the Septuagint reads "lambs".
notes.5:29: Ketiv reads ושאג (Qal weqatal, "and it will roar"), while Qere reads יִשְׁאַג (Qal imperfect without the conjunction, "they roar"), which is followed here; throughout 5:26b-30 the Hebrew uses collective singular forms for the invading nations named in 5:26a.
notes.6:3: The clause "the fullness of all the earth is His glory" follows the Hebrew construct noun melo ("fullness") literally, meaning that His glory is what fills the entire earth.
notes.6:4: Hebrew ammot hassippim ("bases of the thresholds") uses a rare architectural sense of ammah referring to the structural foundations or door-pivots supporting the temple thresholds.
notes.6:10: The three Hiphil imperatives literally command making the people's heart "fat" (an idiom for dull and unresponsive), its ears "heavy," and its eyes "smeared shut."
notes.6:13: Hebrew lebaer (Piel infinitive construct of b'r) means "for burning" or "for consuming," and beshalleket denotes either the felling of trees or the shedding of leaves, leaving behind a stump (matstsebet).
notes.7:1: The singular verbs "went up" and "was not able" agree grammatically with the first-named subject, Rezin; "not able to fight against it" idiomatically expresses inability to capture the city in battle.
notes.7:3: The Hebrew name Shear-jashub means "A remnant will return," echoing the verb "turn back" in 6:10.
notes.7:9: The concluding warning plays on two stems of the same Hebrew root 'mn: Hiphil ta'aminu ("trust" or "believe") and Niphal te'amenu ("remain firm" or "be established").
notes.7:11: The Masoretic pointing she'alah represents the lengthened pausal Qal imperative of sh'l ("ask"), giving "go deep in asking"; an alternative vocalization (she'olah, reflected in several ancient versions) reads "as deep as Sheol."
notes.7:14: Hebrew ha'almah denotes a young woman of marriageable age, normally unmarried (rendered parthenos, "virgin," in the Greek Septuagint); Immanuel means "God is with us," and weqara't is an archaic third-person feminine singular form ("and she will call").
notes.8:1: Hebrew becheret enosh (literally "with a human stylus") refers to ordinary, legible script; the inscribed name Maher-shalal-hash-baz means "Swift to the plunder, speedy to the prey," prefixed with lamed ("Belonging to").
notes.8:6: The Masoretic Hebrew reads umesos ("and rejoicing") with Rezin and the son of Remaliah, an unusual nominal construction continuing the preceding clause; it is translated as written rather than emended to a verb meaning "melt in fear."
notes.8:9: Hebrew ro'u is the Qal imperative of r'' ("break" or "shatter"), pairing with wechottu ("and be shattered"); some ancient versions instead reflect a reading from yd' ("know") or r'h ("band together").
notes.8:16: Taken here as Isaiah's instruction following the end of the LORD's speech in verse 15 ("my disciples"); some interpreters extend the LORD's speech through verse 16, yielding "My disciples."
notes.8:23: In Masoretic versification this verse concludes chapter 8 (numbered 9:1 in another verse division); it contrasts two Hiphil perfects of opposite roots: heqal (from qll, literally "made light" or "dishonored") and hikbid (from kbd, literally "made weighty" or "honored").
notes.9:2: Ketiv reads לא ("not"), while Qere, translated here, reads לוֹ ("for it"), referring to the nation.
notes.9:4: סְאוֹן סֹאֵן ("boot of one tramping") is a cognate noun and Qal participle occurring only here in the Hebrew Bible, understood via Akkadian and Aramaic cognates as a marching boot or sandal.
notes.9:5: וַיִּקְרָא שְׁמוֹ uses a Qal active verb with unspecified subject ("and one will call his name" or "and He will call his name"), here rendered with an English passive; the titles פֶּלֶא יוֹעֵץ (lit. "Wonder of a Counselor") and אֲבִי־עַד (lit. "Father of Eternity") pair nouns in apposition or construct.
notes.9:6: Ketiv preserves an anomalous final closed mem (ם) in the middle of the word, read by Qere as לְמַרְבֵּה ("of the increase"), derived from the root רבה.
notes.9:18: נֶעְתַּם ("has been scorched") is a Niphal perfect of עתם occurring only here in the Hebrew Bible; depending on Semitic cognates it is interpreted either as "scorched" or "darkened."
notes.10:4: בִּלְתִּי כָרַע (lit. "except bowing down") is an elliptical construction answering the rhetorical questions of 10:3, meaning nothing remains except to crouch beneath the captives or fall beneath the slaughtered.
notes.10:18: כִּמְסֹס נֹסֵס ("like a sick man melting away") combines the Qal infinitive construct of מסס ("melt/waste away") with the Qal participle נֹסֵס, understood from Semitic cognates as a sick or fainting person.
notes.10:27: וְחֻבַּל עֹל מִפְּנֵי־שָׁמֶן (lit. "and a yoke will be destroyed because of fatness/oil") is a noted Hebrew crux; following the Masoretic text, it depicts the yoke broken by fatness (or metaphorically by anointing oil).
notes.10:29: לָנוּ is vocalized identically to both the Qal perfect 3cp of לוּן ("they spent the night/lodged") and "for us"; taking it as the verb parallels the preceding cognate pair עָבְרוּ מַעְבָּרָה ("they crossed the pass") with מָלוֹן לָנוּ ("they took their night's lodging").
notes.10:32: Ketiv reads בית ("house of"), whereas Qere, translated here, reads בַּת ("daughter of"), yielding "Daughter Zion."
notes.11:2: The three parallel appositional phrases (ruach chokhmah..., ruach etsah..., ruach da'at...) lack the definite article in Hebrew and may be rendered either capitalized in apposition to "the Spirit of the LORD" or lowercase ("a spirit of wisdom...").
notes.11:3: וַהֲרִיחוֹ ("and his delight") is a Hiphil infinitive construct of רוח ("smell") with a 3ms suffix, literally "his smelling," an idiom for taking pleasure or delight in the fear of the LORD.
notes.11:8: Both the noun מְאוּרַת ("den") and the Qal perfect verb הָדָה ("stretch out") occur only here in the Hebrew Bible, with their senses inferred from context and parallelism.
notes.11:13: צֹרְרֵי יְהוּדָה (Qal participle construct of צרר + "Judah") can be read objectively as "the adversaries of Judah" or subjectively as "the hostile ones of Judah," paralleling the final clause of the verse.
notes.11:15: The Masoretic text reads וְהֶחֱרִים (Hiphil of חרם, "completely destroy") rather than "dry up" (חרב) reflected in some ancient versions. בַּעְיָם ("with the scorching heat") is a unique form whose exact etymology is uncertain, traditionally understood as glowing heat or fierce strength.
notes.12:1: The verb yashov ("has turned back") is a short prefix form (jussive/preterite) of shuv paired with the Piel imperfect utenachameni ("and You comfort me"), expressing either fulfilled deliverance or a petition ("may Your anger turn back").
notes.12:2: The Hebrew pairs the shortened poetic form of the divine name directly with the full divine name, rendered here as "the LORD, the LORD," echoing Exodus 15:2.
notes.12:5: Ketiv/Qere: The Qere reads the Hophal feminine participle muda'at ("made known"), while the unvocalized Ketiv spells the word with a yod (myd't, likely a Pual participle with the same passive sense).
notes.13:6: The Hebrew creates a wordplay between shod ("devastation") and Shaddai ("the Almighty").
notes.13:16: Ketiv/Qere: The Qere substitutes the euphemistic Niphal form tishshakhavnah ("be lain with," rendered "be violated") for the blunter Ketiv verb shagal ("be ravished").
notes.13:21: Several desert fauna terms in 13:21-22 (tsiyyim, ochim, benot ya'anah, se'irim, iyyim, tannim) are partly uncertain; se'irim literally means "hairy ones" and can denote either wild goats or goat-like demons.
notes.13:22: The MT spells "its citadels" as almenotav (with lamed rather than the usual resh in armenotav), either a phonetic variant or a wordplay on almanah ("widow"), suggesting widowed palaces.
notes.14:4: The MT reads the hapax legomenon madhevah, traditionally derived from Aramaic dehav ("gold") and rendered "exaction of gold"; the Dead Sea Scroll 1QIsa-a and ancient versions point instead to marhevah ("insolent fury").
notes.14:9: Hebrew repha'im denotes the shades or departed spirits in Sheol, and attudey arets ("leaders of the earth") literally means "he-goats of the earth," a metaphor for rulers.
notes.14:12: Hebrew heylel ("Shining One," from halal, "to shine") designates the bright morning star (Venus); the Latin Vulgate rendered it as Lucifer ("light-bearer").
notes.14:19: The phrase levush harugim meto'aney charev literally depicts the king as "clothed with those killed, pierced by the sword," using the hapax Pual participle meto'aney ("pierced").
notes.14:30: "Firstborn of the poor" (bekhorey dallim) is a Hebrew superlative idiom for the poorest of the poor; in the final clause, the MT shifts from first-person singular ("I will put ... to death") to third-person singular yaharog ("he will kill"), referring to the coming northern invader.
notes.15:2: Hebrew habbayit literally means "the house" and is taken here as a Moabite town name (Bayith) paired with Dibon following the Masoretic disjunctive accent on Dibon; alternatively, "he [Moab] has gone up to the temple, and Dibon to the high places."
notes.15:3: The phrase "going down in weeping" renders the Hebrew Qal participle yored babbeki, a vivid idiom for collapsing or dissolving in tears.
notes.15:5: Hebrew beriheha is a defective plural of bariah ("fugitives"; or from beriah, "bars"). "Eglath-shelishiyah" is taken as a Moabite place name near Zoar (literally "third Eglath" or "a three-year-old heifer"); the rare verb ye'o'eru ("they stir up") is a reduplicated stem form of 'ur ("rouse").
notes.15:7: Hebrew yitrah 'asah is an asyndetic relative clause with a singular verb for collective Moab ("the surplus it has acquired"), shifting immediately to plural suffixes and verb ("their stored possessions they carry"). "Wadi of the Willows" (nahal ha'aravim) may also refer to Euphrates poplars or to the Arabah.
notes.16:3: Ketiv reads Hiphil masculine plural imperative havi'u ("Bring," pl.); Qere reads feminine singular havi'i ("Bring," fem. sg.), matching the following feminine singular imperatives and suffixes.
notes.16:4: The Masoretic Text points niddahay ("My outcasts," Niphal participle with first-person suffix) followed by a disjunctive accent before vocative "Moab"; some ancient versions read construct niddahei mo'av ("the outcasts of Moab").
notes.16:7: Hebrew 'ashishei ("raisin cakes") fits the vineyard imagery of vv. 8-10; some older interpreters render it "foundations" from a different root, and the parallel in Jer 48:31 reads "men."
notes.16:8: In "the lords of the nations have struck down its choice vines," standard Hebrew word order treats "the lords of the nations" as subject of halemu (Qal of halam); alternatively, "its choice vines" is subject ("struck down [intoxicated] the lords of the nations").
notes.16:9: Hebrew 'arayyawek ("I will soak you") is an anomalous Piel imperfect of rawah with a second-person feminine singular suffix. Hebrew hedad ("the shouting") in vv. 9-10 carries a deliberate double sense, evoking both enemy battle cries falling on the harvest and joyous vintage shouts now silenced.
notes.17:6: Hebrew bis'ifeha poriyyah ("on the branches of a fruit-bearing tree") uses an anticipatory feminine singular suffix ("its branches") explained by the appositional Qal feminine active participle poriyyah ("fruit-bearing").
notes.17:9: The Masoretic Text reads hahoresh weha'amir ("the woodland and the summit/topmost bough," echoing 'amir in v. 6); the Septuagint reflects a different consonantal reading ("the Hivites and the Amorites").
notes.17:11: Hebrew tesagsegi ("you make it grow") is a hapax legomenon (Pilpel imperfect), alternatively derived from sug ("hedge/fence in"). Hebrew ned ("gone") is taken as a verbal form from nud ("flee/vanish"), though as pointed it also resembles the noun ned ("a heap"); nahalah ("sickness," from halah) puns on nahalah ("inheritance").
notes.17:13: Hebrew shifts to collective masculine singular forms in vv. 13-14 (bo, "it/him"; nas, "flees"; ruddaf, Pual "is pursued"; 'einennu, "it is no more") referring to the assembled nations; these are smoothed to plural "them/they" in English.
notes.18:1: "Buzzing wings" translates a rare construct phrase (tsiltsal kenafayim) from an onomatopoeic root meaning "buzz" or "whir" (cf. Deut 28:42), though some connect it to a homonymous root meaning "shadow."
notes.18:2: Several rare expressions appear here: "tall and smooth" is literally "drawn out and burnished" (Pual participles of mashakh and marat); "far and wide" is literally "from it and onward"; "might and trampling" renders an obscure reduplicated form (qav-qav) paired with "trampling"; and "cut through" translates a rare verb (baza) attested only here and in 18:7.
notes.18:4: The ketiv spells the verb plene (with a vav) while the qere spells it defectively (without a vav); both represent the Qal 1st-person singular cohortative of shaqat ("stay quiet"). The Masoretic Text also reads "in the heat of harvest."
notes.18:7: The Masoretic Text has the preposition "from" (min) only before the second phrase ("and from a people"), either serving poetic double duty for the first phrase as well or leaving "a people tall and smooth" in apposition to "tribute."
notes.19:6: "Will grow foul" renders an unusual double-prefixed Hiphil form (he'eznichu) of zanach ("stink/grow foul"). "Egypt" in "channels of Egypt" translates Matsor, a singular poetic form of the Hebrew name Mitsrayim.
notes.19:10: "Its pillars" translates shatoteha (literally "its foundations/pillars," cf. Ps 11:3, used figuratively of leading citizens), though some derive it from a weaving term ("its weavers"). "All who work for wages" translates the Masoretic Text (osey seker) literally.
notes.19:12: The Masoretic Text reads a Qal jussive (veyed'u, "and let them know"), rather than a causative Hiphil ("make known").
notes.19:18: The Masoretic Text reads Ir ha-Heres ("City of Destruction"); the Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsa-a) and some Hebrew manuscripts read Ir ha-Cheres ("City of the Sun," i.e., Heliopolis).
notes.19:23: The particle et before "Assyria" is taken here as the preposition "with," continuing the cultic sense of "worship" (avad) from 19:21, though grammatically et could also mark a direct object ("serve Assyria").
notes.20:1: "The chief commander" translates Hebrew tartan, a loanword from the Assyrian military title turtanu ("commander-in-chief").
notes.20:2: "Your sandals from your feet" translates collective singular forms in the Masoretic Text (literally "your sandal from your foot").
notes.20:4: "With bared buttocks" translates a rare Qal passive participle masculine plural construct (chasufay) with the noun shet ("buttocks," cf. 2 Sam 10:4).
notes.21:2: Hebrew אַנְחָתָה lacks a mappiq in the final ה, traditionally understood as "her groaning" (an unpointed 3fs suffix referring to the groaning caused by Babylon) or simply "groaning."
notes.21:5: The phrase צָפֹה הַצָּפִית pairs a Qal infinitive absolute with the hapax legomenon צָפִית, meaning either "spread the rugs" (from צפה II, "spread out") or "keep the watch" (from צפה I, "watch").
notes.21:8: The Masoretic Text reads וַיִּקְרָא אַרְיֵה, literally "and he cried out, a lion" (taken comparatively as "like a lion"); this translation follows the MT rather than emending אַרְיֵה to הָרֹאֶה ("the seer/lookout").
notes.21:12: The verbs אָתָה / אֵתָיוּ ("come") and תִּבְעָיוּן / בְּעָיוּ ("inquire") employ Aramaizing roots and forms fitting this pronouncement concerning Seir and Dumah.
notes.22:5: The phrase מְקַרְקַר קִר combines the Pilpel participle of קרר/קור ("tearing down") with the defective spelling קִר ("wall"), creating wordplay that also anticipates the proper name Kir (קִיר) in v. 6.
notes.22:16: The participles חֹצְבִי ("hewing out") and חֹקְקִי ("chiseling") carry the poetic binding vowel (hireq compaginis) rather than a first-person suffix, while the verse shifts abruptly to third-person suffixes ("his tomb," "for himself").
notes.22:17: The Qal participle and infinitive absolute עֹטְךָ עָטֹה (from עטה) mean "wrap you up completely" (preparing for the ball-winding image of v. 18), though some lexicons render the root here as "grasp firmly."
notes.22:19: The Masoretic Text shifts within the verse from first person (וַהֲדַפְתִּיךָ, "I will push you out") to third person (יֶהֶרְסֶךָ, "He will pull you down"), both referring to the LORD.
notes.22:24: Hebrew כְּבוֹד ("glory") also carries its root sense of "weight," linking the "throne of glory" (v. 23) with the "load" hanging on the peg (v. 25).
notes.23:1: Hebrew מִבַּיִת מִבּוֹא uses privative מִן twice, literally "from a house, from entering," indicating Tyre is devastated so that neither house nor entry/harbor remains.
notes.23:10: The Masoretic Text reads עִבְרִי ("overflow/pass over," Qal imperative of עבר) rather than the Septuagint's "till"; the rare noun מֵזַח denotes a "belt" or "girdle" (cf. Ps 109:19), used figuratively here for "restraint."
notes.23:12: Ketiv reads כתיים and Qere reads כִּתִּים, an orthographic variant for the same place name, "Kittim" (Cyprus).
notes.23:13: Qere reads בַחוּנָיו ("its/their siege towers," with 3ms suffix referring to Assyria) where Ketiv reads בחיניו; the clause זֶה הָעָם לֹא הָיָה is literally "this is the people that was not," expressing that it is no more.
notes.24:6: Hebrew charu is the Qal perfect of charar ("be scorched, burned"), matching the consuming curse earlier in the verse.
notes.24:15: Hebrew ba'urim literally means "in the lights" or "in the fires," widely understood as the regions of sunrise in the east, balancing "the coastlands of the sea" in the west.
notes.24:16: Hebrew razi-li literally means "wasting away to me" (from razah, "grow lean, waste away"), paralleling "Woe to me!" rather than referring to a secret.
notes.25:5: Hebrew ya'aneh is the Qal imperfect of anah ("be bowed down, humbled"), conveying that the song of the ruthless is brought low just as scorching heat is subdued by a cloud's shade.
notes.25:10: Following the qere bemo (poetic form of the preposition "in") for "in a dung pit"; the ketiv reads bemei ("in the waters of").
notes.25:11: Hebrew orbot yadav ("craftiness of his hands") uses a hapax legomenon from the root arab ("lie in wait, scheme"), denoting the artifice or cunning skill of Moab's hands.
notes.26:4: The Hebrew pairs the shortened poetic form of the divine name with the full divine name and uses a beth essentiae ("the LORD, the LORD, is an eternal Rock").
notes.26:16: Hebrew tsaqun is a rare Qal perfect third-person plural of tsuq ("pour out") with a paragogic nun.
notes.26:18: Hebrew yipplu (Qal imperfect of naphal) literally means "fall"; some understand it in the sense of "be born," continuing the childbirth imagery of vv. 17-18 and anticipating the Hiphil tappil ("bring forth") in v. 19.
notes.26:19: Masoretic nevelati literally reads "my corpse," used collectively with the plural verb yequmun ("will rise") to express the speaker's solidarity with God's dead; Hebrew orot ("lights") is also taken by some as "herbs."
notes.26:20: Following the qere delatekha (singular, "your door"); the ketiv reads delateikha (plural, "your doors").
notes.27:2: Masoretic Hebrew reads chemer ("wine"), yielding "a vineyard of wine" (some Hebrew manuscripts and the Septuagint read chemed, "delight/pleasantness"). The verb is a Piel imperative of anah ("sing").
notes.27:4: The phrase mi-yitteneni (literally "who will give me") is a Hebrew wish idiom ("if only"). The feminine singular suffixes translated "them" refer collectively to the briers and thorns.
notes.27:7: Masoretic Hebrew has the Qal passive participle harugav ("those killed by Him," or "his killed ones") rather than an active participle ("his killers"), pairing three forms of nkh ("strike") with three forms of hrg ("kill/slaughter").
notes.27:8: The rare form bese'se'ah is commonly analyzed as a reduplication of se'ah (a dry measure), hence "measure by measure," though some understand it as "by driving away." The Qal perfect hagah here means "removed" or "drove away."
notes.27:12: "The River" refers to the Euphrates, and shibbolet ("channel/flowing stream") plays on its homonym meaning "ear of grain," echoing the harvest verb chavat ("beat out grain/thresh").
notes.28:10: The Hebrew tsav la-tsav, tsav la-tsav, qav la-qav, qav la-qav uses staccato monosyllabic wordplay ("command after command ... line after line") that mocks the prophet's teaching while mimicking childish or drunken repetition.
notes.28:15: Two ketiv/qere variants follow the qere: qere shot ("scourge," matching v. 18) for ketiv shayit, and qere Qal imperfect ya'avor ("passes through") for ketiv Qal perfect avar.
notes.28:16: Masoretic Hebrew points the verb as a Piel perfect yissad ("has laid") after hineni ("look, I"). The final clause lo yachish literally means "will not hasten," that is, will not act or flee in panic.
notes.28:28: Opening with an unmarked rhetorical question, the verse repeats the root dqq ("crush": Hophal imperfect yudaq and Qal imperfect yeduqqennu) and uses the unusual infinitive absolute spelling adosh (for dosh) to express continuous threshing.
notes.29:2: "Ariel" plays on its dual resonance as "lion of God" and "altar hearth" (compare Ezek 43:15-16), following the assonant pair ta'aniyyah wa-'aniyyah ("moaning and mourning").
notes.29:6: The Niphal imperfect tippaqed is 3rd feminine singular ("she will be visited"), referring to Ariel and shifting from the 2nd feminine singular address of vv. 3-5 to the 3rd feminine singular pronouns of v. 7.
notes.29:9: The Hithpalpel imperative hitmahmehu ("delay/linger," from mhh) plays on the sound of the Qal imperative temahu ("be astounded," from tmh), and the second half shifts to Qal perfects ("they are drunk ... they stagger").
notes.29:11: Ketiv reads hassefer ("the scroll/writing") with the definite article; the qere omits the article (sefer, matching v. 12) in the idiom yodea sefer (literally "one who knows writing," that is, "knows how to read").
notes.29:13: Masoretic Hebrew points richaq as a Piel perfect ("they have kept far"), and the Pual participle melummadah ("taught/learned") modifies "commandment of men."
notes.30:1: "Seal an alliance" translates Hebrew linsok massekah (Qal infinitive construct of nsk plus cognate noun), literally "to pour out a libation" or "to weave a covering," an idiom for ratifying a treaty.
notes.30:7: The difficult Hebrew clause rahab hem shabet is literally "Rahab, they [are] sitting/inaction," using the Qal infinitive construct shabet (from yshb "sit" or shbt "cease") as an ironic nickname mocking Egypt's boastful power.
notes.30:8: Masoretic vocalization reads la'ad ("forever"), whereas the unvocalized consonants can be read le'ed ("as a witness") as in several ancient versions; translated strictly according to the Masoretic Text.
notes.30:20: Hebrew morekha is morphologically plural ("your teachers"), yet its verb yikkanef (Niphal imperfect 3ms of knf, hapax legomenon, "hide oneself") is singular, indicating an honorific singular ("your Teacher").
notes.30:32: Translated per the Qere bam ("against them") rather than the Ketiv bh ("against her"). Hebrew matteh musadah literally means "staff of appointment" or "staff of foundation."
notes.30:33: Translated per the Qere hi (feminine singular, matching the feminine suffixes later in the verse) rather than the Ketiv hu (masculine singular); both refer to Topheth ("it").
notes.31:5: Hebrew pairs two Qal infinitives absolute with Hiphil verbs (ganon wehitsil pasoah wehimlit), using pasoah—the Passover verb—for "passing over" or "sparing."
notes.31:6: The 2mp imperative shubu ("Return") shifts to the 3mp Hiphil perfect he'miqu ("have deeply revolted"), taking "the sons of Israel" as its subject (alternatively a vocative, "from whom they have deeply revolted, sons of Israel").
notes.31:9: "His rock" (sal'o) metaphorically denotes Assyria's ruler or stronghold, and "at the standard" (minnes) plays on "will flee" (wenas) in v. 8.
notes.32:7: Translated per the Qere aniyyim ("the poor/afflicted") rather than the Ketiv anawim ("the humble"). Hebrew also plays on kelay ("scoundrel") and kelaw ("his devices").
notes.32:11: The four imperatives regazah, peshotah, orah, and hagorah take an unusual -ah form for feminine plural addressees, and "wrap your waists" (hagor al-halatsayim) elliptically omits sackcloth.
notes.32:15: Hebrew ruach ("spirit") lacks the definite article here and may be read either as "a spirit" (or "wind") or as "the Spirit" poured out from on high. "And the orchard" follows the Qere wehakkarmel (with the definite article) rather than the Ketiv wekarmel ("and an orchard").
notes.32:19: The hapax verb ubarad ("it will hail") plays on the sound of beredet ("when ... comes down"), followed by the cognate emphasis ubashshiflah tishpal ("in lowliness ... will be brought low").
notes.33:1: The phrase 'when you cease' translates the rare MT form kanneloteka, traditionally derived from a hapax root nlh parallel in sense to tmm ('finish') in the preceding clause.
notes.33:2: The MT reads 'their arm' with a third-person plural suffix, shifting briefly from the first-person plural petitions ('us,' 'our') surrounding it.
notes.33:7: The hapax legomenon 'er'ellam ('their valiant ones') is traditionally linked to 'ari'el ('hero, lion-like warrior'; cf. 2 Sam 23:20) with a third-person plural suffix.
notes.33:23: The MT shifts abruptly to feminine singular ('your cords') and plural ('their mast') nautical imagery; 'booty' renders the rare noun 'ad (cf. Gen 49:27; Zeph 3:8) paired with shalal ('spoil').
notes.34:6: The verb 'made rich with fat' renders the rare Hothpaal passive-reflexive stem of dshn (huddashnah), echoed by the Pual form of the same root in v. 7.
notes.34:11: The exact species denoted by several desert animals in vv. 11 and 14-15 are uncertain; 'measuring line of formlessness and the plumb stones of emptiness' echoes tohu wabohu in Gen 1:2.
notes.34:12: The MT syntax in the first clause is highly compressed, literally reading 'its nobles--and there is none there--a kingdom they will proclaim,' meaning no noble remains there to proclaim kingship.
notes.34:14: The hapax noun lilit ('night creature,' often transliterated 'Lilith') refers to a nocturnal bird or night demon in ancient Near Eastern lore.
notes.34:16: The MT shifts directly from first person ('My mouth,' pi) to third person ('His Spirit,' rucho), with emphatic independent pronouns reinforcing each subject.
notes.35:1: The MT verb yesusum ('will be glad') displays an unusual final -m ending on a third-person plural Qal imperfect of sws, often explained as assimilation of a paragogic nun before the initial m of midbar ('wilderness').
notes.35:7: The noun sharab can mean either 'mirage' or 'scorching heat/ground' (cf. Isa 49:10); in the second half, chatsir ('grass') may also be taken as its homonym meaning 'abode/enclosure' (echoing 34:13).
notes.35:8: The clause wehu'-lamo ('but it will be for them') is syntactically terse; taking lamo as plural ('for them,' following the Masoretic punctuation) distinguishes the redeemed travelers from the unclean, though some construe lamo as singular ('for him who walks the way').
notes.36:2: Rabshakeh is an Assyrian official title (Akkadian rab-shaqe, chief cupbearer or high officer) treated here without the Hebrew definite article.
notes.36:5: Masoretic Isaiah reads the first-person Qal perfect "I say" (amarti), whereas the parallel in 2 Kings 18:20 reads the second-person "you say" (amarta).
notes.36:12: Ketiv/Qere: the Masoretic qere substitutes the euphemisms "their excrement" (tso'atam) and "the water of their feet" (meme raglehem) for the blunter written ketiv forms meaning "their dung" and "their urine."
notes.36:16: "Make peace with me" literally reads "make a blessing (berakhah) with me," an idiom for concluding a peaceful settlement or treaty of submission.
