notes.37:18: Masoretic Isaiah literally reads "all the lands/countries (ha'aratsot) and their land (artsam)," whereas the parallel in 2 Kings 19:17 reads "the nations (haggoyim) and their land."
notes.37:21: Masoretic Isaiah omits the verb "I have heard" found at the end of 2 Kings 19:20, linking the causal clause ("Because you have prayed to Me...") directly into v. 22.
notes.37:24: "Its farthest height" translates Masoretic Isaiah's merom qitso, whereas the parallel in 2 Kings 19:23 reads "its farthest lodging place" (melon qitso).
notes.37:27: "Of little strength" renders the idiom qitsre-yad (lit. "short of hand"). At the end of the verse, Masoretic Isaiah reads "a field (shedemah) before the standing grain," whereas 2 Kings 19:26 reads "blighted grain" (shedephah).
notes.37:30: Ketiv/Qere: the written ketiv reads a Qal infinitive absolute ("and eating"), while the read qere conforms to the preceding imperatives with the second-person masculine plural Qal imperative "and eat" (we'ikhlu).
notes.38:8: Hebrew ma'alot literally means "steps" or "stairway," possibly a stepped structure serving as a sundial; the feminine verb yaredah ("has gone down") agrees grammatically with feminine shemesh ("sun").
notes.38:10: Hebrew bidmi is rare and may mean either "at the midpoint" or "in the stillness/cutting off" of his days; puqqadti (Pual of paqad) means "I have been deprived of."
notes.38:11: Hebrew doubles the shortened divine name Yah ("the LORD, the LORD"). At the end of the verse, the Masoretic Text reads chadel ("cessation" or "transience," understood here as the transient world), often compared to cheled ("world").
notes.38:16: The Hebrew is terse: "by these things" (alehem) refers back to God's word and deeds in v. 15, and the Hiphil verb tachalimeni (from chalam II) means "restore to health."
notes.38:17: The Masoretic Text reads chashaqta (Qal of chashaq, "loved/clung to"), used in a pregnant construction with min to mean "lovingly kept back from."
notes.39:1: The verb vayyechezaq ("and had grown strong again," Qal of chazaq) creates a Hebrew wordplay on the name Hezekiah (Chizqiyyahu).
notes.39:2: Hebrew bet nekotoh ("his treasure house") uses an archaic third-person masculine singular suffix and a loanword related to Akkadian bit nakamti ("storehouse").
notes.39:7: Hebrew yiqqachu is a pausal Qal imperfect third-person masculine plural of laqach with an indefinite subject ("they will take"), rendered passively here as "will be taken."
notes.40:3: Both the Masoretic accentuation (zaqeph qaton on qore) and the poetic parallelism ("in the wilderness" // "in the desert plain") link "in the wilderness" with "clear the way" rather than with "a voice calls out."
notes.40:6: The Masoretic Text reads third-person va'amar ("and he said") rather than first-person ("and I said") found in some ancient witnesses; chasdo ("its loyal love," from chesed) describes how short-lived human constancy is (cf. Hos 6:4), though it may also suggest loveliness.
notes.40:9: The construct phrase mebasseret tsiyyon (and parallel mebasseret yerushalayim) can be read either appositionally ("Zion, messenger of good news," matching the feminine singular imperatives addressed to the city) or objectively ("messenger of good news to Zion").
notes.40:20: The Masoretic Text points hamesukkan as a Pual participle ("the one too poor for an offering," cf. misken in Eccl 4:13); some lexicographers connect the consonants to Akkadian musukkannu, a durable hardwood.
notes.40:21: The Masoretic Text has no preposition "from" before mosdot ha'arets, allowing it to be read directly as the object of "understood" ("understood the foundations of the earth"), though some carry over "from" from the previous clause.
notes.41:2: The Hebrew clause "righteousness calls/meets him at his foot" is syntactically ambiguous: it may take tsedeq adverbially with God as subject ("whom He calls in righteousness to follow Him," cf. 42:6; 45:13) or as subject ("whom righteousness meets at every step"). The verb yard is an apocopated form of radah ("subdue, have dominion over").
notes.41:10: The verb tishta is the Hithpael jussive of sha'ah ("look about in alarm" or "gaze around anxiously"; the same stem recurs in 41:23). "The right hand of My righteousness" preserves the literal Hebrew construct chain.
notes.41:23: Ketiv/Qere: the Qere reads wenir'eh (Qal imperfect 1cp of ra'ah, "and we will see/look"), which is followed here; the Ketiv lacks the final he and could be read either as a shortened spelling of ra'ah or as defective wenira from yare ("and we will fear").
notes.41:24: The noun epha ("nothingness") is a hapax legomenon parallel to ayin ("nothing"), generally understood as a poetic variant of ephes ("nothingness").
notes.41:27: The opening clause in the Masoretic Text is elliptically compressed (literally, "First to Zion: 'Look, here they are!'"), leaving the verb of speaking implied.
notes.42:4: The verbs yikheh (Qal imperfect of kahah, "grow dim") and yaruts (Qal imperfect of ratsats formed on the analogy of hollow verbs, "be crushed") deliberately echo the adjective kehah ("dim") and Qal passive participle ratsuts ("crushed") in 42:3.
notes.42:19: Meshullam is the Pual participle of shalem ("be complete, at peace"), variously understood as "one at peace," "covenant partner," or "dedicated one." The Masoretic Text repeats iwwer ("blind") in both halves of the second question.
notes.42:20: Ketiv/Qere: the Qere reads ra'ot (a Qal infinitive absolute form of ra'ah, "seeing," paralleling the Qal infinitive absolute paqoah, "opening"), whereas the Ketiv represents the Qal perfect 2ms ra'ita ("you have seen"). The Masoretic Text also shifts from second-person "you observe" to third-person "he hears."
notes.42:22: Hapeah is a Hiphil infinitive absolute of puah (denominative from pah, "snare"), functioning here with passive force ("ensnared"), and bahurim is vocalized as the preposition be with the article plus hurim ("in holes"), paralleling "in prison houses."
notes.42:24: Ketiv/Qere: the Qere reads limshissah ("as spoil/plunder," matching meshissah in 42:22), whereas the Ketiv could be read either as an orthographic variant of the same noun or as a Poel participle ("to the despoiler"). The Masoretic Text shifts from first-person plural "we have sinned" to third-person plural "they were unwilling... they did not listen."
notes.43:8: The opening verb has the Masoretic pointing of a Hiphil perfect or infinitive construct rather than the standard imperative form, but in this courtroom summons it functions as an imperative ('Bring out').
notes.43:9: The verb 'gather together' has the form of a Niphal perfect ('have gathered'), functioning here as a summons parallel to the following Niphal jussive ('let the peoples assemble').
notes.43:13: 'From the first day' renders a terse Hebrew phrase literally meaning 'from day,' idiomatically denoting 'from the beginning of time' or 'from eternity.'
notes.43:14: The Masoretic pointing reads 'fugitives' (whereas a different vowel pattern of the same consonants means 'bars'); the closing phrase literally reads 'in the ships of their shouting' or 'jubilation.'
notes.44:9: In the Masoretic Text, the pronoun rendered 'themselves' carries ancient scribal dots (puncta extraordinaria) marking an early textual query, while remaining in the text.
notes.44:12: The opening clause is syntactically elliptical in Hebrew (literally 'craftsman of iron, a cutting tool, and he works over the coals'), with the tool serving as the object or instrument of the following verb.
notes.44:18: 'Have been plastered shut' translates a third-person masculine singular Qal active verb (literally 'he has plastered over'), functioning either as an impersonal passive or with God as the implied subject.
notes.44:21: 'You will not be forgotten by Me' renders a rare Niphal imperfect carrying a first-person pronominal suffix (literally 'you will not be forgotten to/by Me'), though some construe it actively as 'do not forget Me.'
notes.44:24: Translated following the Qere ('by Myself,' literally 'from with Me'); the Ketiv divides the consonants into two words meaning 'who was with Me?'
notes.45:2: Qere אֲיַשֵּׁר (Piel, "I will make level") is translated; Ketiv אושר represents the Hiphil of the same root ישר with the same sense. The rare plural הֲדוּרִים ("rugged terrain") literally denotes swollen or uneven ground.
notes.45:7: Hebrew רָע ("disaster"), paired directly with שָׁלוֹם ("peace"), denotes calamity or adversity rather than moral evil.
notes.45:9: The clause וּפׇעׇלְךָ אֵין־יָדַיִם לוֹ is syntactically compressed and may be read either as part of the clay's speech ("Your work has no hands/handles") or as an elliptical question ("or will your work say, 'He has no hands'?").
notes.45:11: Following the Masoretic vocalization and accents, שְׁאָלוּנִי ("Ask Me") is a Qal imperative, while the Piel imperfect תְּצַוֻּנִי ("will you command Me?") functions as an unmarked rhetorical question governing both prepositional phrases that precede it.
notes.45:19: Hebrew תֹּהוּ ("in vain," literally "emptiness") echoes תֹהוּ ("wasteland") in 45:18, linking God's purposeful creation of the earth with His clear self-revelation to Israel.
notes.46:8: The Hithpolel imperative הִתְאֹשָׁשׁוּ ("be resolute") occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible; its sense is generally connected with standing firm or taking courage.
notes.46:11: Qere עֲצָתִי ("My counsel") is translated, matching עֲצָתִי in 46:10; Ketiv עצתו reads "his counsel."
notes.46:12: Hebrew אַבִּירֵי לֵב literally means "strong of heart," used here idiomatically for obstinacy ("stubborn of heart").
notes.47:3: Hebrew וְלֹא אֶפְגַּע אָדָם literally means "and I will not meet a human," a difficult idiom understood here as "I will spare no human" (or alternatively "I will not accept any human intercession").
notes.47:9: The preposition בְּ before both "your many sorceries" and "the exceeding power of your spells" carries a concessive force ("in spite of"), anticipating the ironic challenge in 47:12.
notes.47:11: Hebrew שַׁחְרָהּ is taken as a Piel infinitive construct ("charm it away"), matching the parallel Piel infinitive כַּפְּרָהּ ("buy it off"); alternatively, it may be derived from the noun שַׁחַר ("its dawn"). Hebrew רָעָה ("disaster") also plays on רָעָתֵךְ ("your wickedness") in 47:10.
notes.47:13: Qere הֹבְרֵי ("those who divide," Qal active participle construct of the hapax root הבר, referring to astrologers partitioning the sky) is translated; Ketiv הברו reads a plural perfect verb ("they divided") or an archaic spelling.
notes.48:1: The Hebrew literally reads "from the waters of Judah," using "waters" as a poetic idiom for physical descent or lineage.
notes.48:10: The Hebrew Qal verb normally means "I have chosen you," though in parallel with "refined" and "smelting furnace" it is widely understood as a cognate or byform meaning "test, examine."
notes.48:11: The Niphal imperfect verb "could be profaned" has no expressed subject in the Masoretic Text; it refers back to "My name" in verse 9.
notes.48:16: The final clause shifts from the LORD's direct speech to the messenger or Servant; the syntax of "and His Spirit" allows it to be read either as a second subject alongside the Lord GOD or as a second object sent with the speaker.
notes.48:19: The Hebrew forms a wordplay between "your body" and the rare noun rendered "its grains," referring to the grains of sand.
notes.49:5: Following the Qere (read form) "to Him"; the Ketiv (written form) reads "not," which would yield "though Israel is not gathered."
notes.49:6: Following the Qere (read form), a Qal passive participle meaning "the preserved ones of"; the Ketiv (written form) is a related adjectival spelling with the same sense.
notes.49:13: Following the Qere (read form), a Qal imperative with the conjunction ("and burst forth"); the Ketiv (written form) lacks the conjunction and is an imperfect ("they will burst forth").
notes.49:17: The Masoretic Text vocalizes the noun as "your sons"; an alternative ancient tradition vocalizes the same consonants as "your builders."
notes.49:24: The Masoretic Text reads "a righteous one" (sometimes understood as a rightful captor), in contrast to "a tyrant" in verse 25.
notes.50:4: The Hebrew infinitive rendered "to sustain" occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible and is understood from comparative Semitic evidence and context to mean "to support, help, sustain."
notes.50:8: Literally "the master of my legal case," a Hebrew forensic idiom for an adversary or opponent in a lawsuit.
notes.50:11: The Piel participle literally means "girding yourselves with" or "equipping yourselves with" firebrands, picturing hostile adversaries arming themselves with flaming weapons.
notes.51:4: Hebrew אַרְגִּיעַ (Hiphil imperfect 1cs of רגע II, 'settle, establish, give rest') is used transitively with מִשְׁפָּטִי ('My justice') to express establishing justice firmly as a light to the peoples.
notes.51:6: Hebrew כְּמוֹ־כֵן literally means 'like so, in the same way,' though some lexicons take כֵן as a singular related to כִּנִּים ('gnats'), rendering 'like gnats.' Hebrew נִמְלָחוּ is a Niphal perfect 3cp of מלח II ('dissipate, disperse, be torn to shreds').
notes.51:14: Hebrew צֹעֶה (Qal active participle ms of צעה, 'stoop, bend over') depicts a captive bowed down in chains, while לְהִפָּתֵחַ (Niphal infinitive construct of פתח) means 'to be loosed' or 'released.'
notes.51:16: The Masoretic Text reads לִנְטֹעַ (Qal infinitive construct of נטע, 'to plant,' used of pitching tents in Dan 11:45), rather than לִנְטוֹת ('to stretch out') as in v. 13.
notes.51:19: The Masoretic Text has the 1cs Piel imperfect אֲנַחֲמֵךְ ('I comfort you') with interrogative מִי used idiomatically in the sense 'how?' (compare Amos 7:2, 5), rather than a 3ms verb ('who will comfort you?').
notes.52:2: Ketiv reads התפתחו (3cp Hithpael perfect 'they have loosed themselves' or 2mp imperative); the Qere הִתְפַּתְּחִי (2fs Hithpael imperative of פתח, 'loose from yourself') is translated here to match the surrounding feminine singular imperatives addressed to Jerusalem.
notes.52:5: Hebrew יְהֵילִילוּ (Hiphil imperfect 3mp of ילל, unusually retaining the Hiphil ה) normally means 'howl' or 'wail,' here expressing the rulers' mocking or boastful cries. Hebrew מִנֹּאָץ is a Hithpoel participle of נאץ with assimilated ת, meaning 'continually treated with contempt.'
notes.52:13: Hebrew יַשְׂכִּיל (Hiphil imperfect 3ms of שׂכל) combines the senses of acting with wisdom or insight and achieving success or prosperity.
notes.52:14: The Masoretic Text shifts abruptly from 2ms עָלֶיךָ ('at you') to 3ms מַרְאֵהוּ ('his appearance') and וְתֹאֲרוֹ ('and his form'). Hebrew מִשְׁחַת is a rare construct noun from שׁחת ('disfigurement, marring'), introducing an explanatory aside before the correlative כֵּן ('so') resumes in v. 15.
notes.52:15: Hebrew יַזֶּה (Hiphil imperfect 3ms of נזה) elsewhere consistently means 'sprinkle' (typically in ritual purification), though some scholars derive it from a homonymous root meaning 'startle.'
notes.53:1: Shemu'athenu can mean "our report" or "what was heard by us." The Hebrew puts "the arm of the LORD" first in its clause, and that order is kept.
notes.53:2: Lowercase pronouns are used for the servant and capitals for the LORD ("before Him"). The Hebrew does not mark the servant as divine, and the case keeps the two referents apart in verses such as 53:10. The clause break after "splendor" follows the Masoretic athnach accent under hadar.
notes.53:3: Makh'oboth and choli mean "pains" and "sickness"; they are rendered the same way in 53:4. Chadal ishim is literally "ceasing from / lacking men," that is, abandoned by people. Master panim mimmennu is literally "a hiding of faces from him."
notes.53:5: Mecholal means "pierced" or "wounded"; the preposition min here means "because of." Musar is discipline or chastening. Nirpa-lanu is an impersonal passive: "it is healed for us," so "healing has come to us." Chavurah is a welt or bruise from blows.
notes.53:6: Hifgia bo means "made to meet / strike against him"; "made ... land on him" keeps the image of a burden falling on him. The same verb appears in 53:12, where it means "intercede."
notes.53:7: Niggas means "oppressed" or "hard pressed"; na'aneh is passive ("afflicted") but may be reflexive ("he let himself be afflicted"). The repeated imperfect lo yiftach is rendered "would not open" to bring out that he chose silence.
notes.53:8: This verse is difficult. Me'otser umimmishpat may mean "by oppression and judgment" or "without restraint and without justice." Doro ("his generation") may mean his contemporaries or his descendants, and yesocheach means "consider" or "complain." Lamo is literally "to them" (or a poetic "to him"); "on him" follows the sense required by the context. The Hebrew has "my people," spoken by the prophet or the LORD.
notes.53:9: Wayyitten is impersonal, "one gave," rendered "they assigned." Bemothaw is a plural, "in his deaths," which may be intensive (a violent death) or may mean "his tomb"; the Hebrew plural is kept.
notes.53:10: Hecheli is "He made (him) sick," from the same root as choli in 53:3–4. Tasim is either third person feminine with nafsho ("his soul") as subject ("if his soul makes a guilt offering," followed here) or second person addressed to the LORD ("if You make his soul a guilt offering"). Asham is the guilt (reparation) offering of Lev 5.
notes.53:11: The Masoretic Text has "he will see" with no object; the Qumran scroll 1QIsa-a and the Septuagint add "light." Since this column translates only the Hebrew, "light" is not supplied. Yatsdiq tsaddiq is a wordplay: "the righteous one will make righteous." Beda'to can mean "by his knowledge" or "by knowing him."
notes.53:12: He'erah means "laid bare" or "poured out" (Gen 24:20). Yafgia is the verb of 53:6, here meaning to intercede or intervene.
notes.54:5: Both בֹעֲלַיִךְ ('your husband') and עֹשַׂיִךְ ('your Maker') are masculine plural Qal participles used as plurals of majesty referring to the one God (compare Job 35:10; Ps 149:2).
notes.54:8: Hebrew בְּשֶׁצֶף קֶצֶף pairs the hapax legomenon שֶׁצֶף ('surge, outburst, flood,' related to שׁטף) with the rhyming noun קֶצֶף ('anger, wrath') for rhetorical emphasis.
notes.54:9: The Masoretic Text divides כִּי־מֵי נֹחַ as two words ('for ... the waters of Noah,' matching מֵי־נֹחַ later in the verse), whereas some manuscripts and ancient versions divide it as כִּימֵי נֹחַ ('like the days of Noah').
notes.54:15: Hebrew גּוֹר יָגוּר (Qal infinitive absolute plus imperfect 3ms of גור III, 'stir up strife, attack') expresses emphatic attack; אֶפֶס מֵאוֹתִי ('not from Me') uses the rare spelling מֵאוֹתִי for מֵאִתִּי (compare v. 17).
notes.54:16: Ketiv reads הן (הֵן, 'look, see'); the Qere הִנֵּה ('look, see,' rendered 'See') carries the same deictic force.
notes.55:1: Hebrew hoy here functions as an urgent call of summons rather than a lament of woe, and shivru (Qal imperative of shavar II) specifically means to purchase grain or provisions.
notes.55:3: Hebrew chasdei Dawid hanne'emanim (literally 'the proven/sure acts of loyal love of David') uses the Niphal participle of aman in apposition to 'eternal covenant,' referring to the enduring acts of loyal love promised to David.
notes.55:13: Translates the Qere 'and instead of' (wetachat); the Ketiv (tachat) lacks the conjunction. The noun sirpad occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible and denotes a prickly weed such as a brier or nettle.
notes.56:5: Hebrew yad literally means 'hand' and idiomatically denotes a memorial monument or standing place. The final clause shifts in the Masoretic Text to the distributive singular lo (literally 'to him'), rendered 'each one.'
notes.56:10: Hebrew hozim (Qal participle of hazah) occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible and denotes dreaming or drowsing incoherently. Masoretic tzofaw is a defective spelling of tzofayw ('his watchmen,' referring to Israel).
notes.56:11: Hebrew miqqatzehu literally means 'from its end/extremity,' an idiom denoting totality ('without exception').
notes.57:3: Hebrew mena'ef wattizneh literally pairs a masculine Piel participle ('an adulterer') with a third-person feminine singular waw-consecutive Qal imperfect verb ('and she commits prostitution'), continuing the construct phrase idiomatically.
notes.57:6: Hebrew challaqei-nachal chelqekh creates a wordplay between chalaq ('smooth [stones]') and cheleq ('portion').
notes.57:8: Hebrew yad literally means 'hand' and is used here as a euphemism for male nakedness (or possibly a pagan monument/sign, cf. 56:5).
notes.57:13: Hebrew qibbutzayikh (a plural noun occurring only here, from qavatz 'gather') literally means 'your gatherings/collections,' an ironic reference to Judah's assembled idols or foreign allies.
notes.57:19: Translates the Qere niv ('fruit/produce') rather than the Ketiv nov, an alternate spelling of the same noun.
notes.58:8: The Qal verb ya'asfekha (from asaf, "gather") is used idiomatically for gathering in stragglers or serving as a military rear guard.
notes.58:10: The Masoretic Text reads nafshekha ("your soul"), idiomatically expressing offering oneself or what one's own appetite desires to the hungry.
notes.58:13: The privative sense of turning back from the Sabbath carries over to the infinitive asot ("from doing"); the concluding idiom dabber davar (lit. "speaking a word") denotes everyday talk or business chatter.
notes.58:14: Ketiv bmvty (plene spelling with waw) vs. Qere bamotei (construct vocalization without waw); both denote "the heights of" or "high places of."
notes.59:3: The verb nego'alu ("are defiled", from ga'al II) is a rare mixed form blending the Niphal prefix with a Pual vowel pattern.
notes.59:10: The noun ashmannim is a hapax legomenon of uncertain meaning, here derived from the root shaman ("stout, vigorous") to yield "among the vigorous."
notes.59:18: The rare double preposition ke'al ... ke'al ("according to ... accordingly") pairs with a wordplay between gemulot ("deeds") and gemul ("recompense").
notes.59:19: Taking tsar as "pent-up" and nosesah as the Polel of nus ("drive forward") yields a river driven by the LORD's breath; an alternative parsing takes tsar as "an adversary" whom the Spirit of the LORD drives back or raises a banner against.
notes.60:7: In ya'alu al-ratson mizbechi, the preposition al governs ratson ("with acceptance"), while mizbechi ("onto My altar") functions as an adverbial accusative of destination.
notes.60:11: The verb ufittechu is vocalized as an intransitive Piel ("stand open") rather than a passive Pual, emphasizing that the gates remain continuously open.
notes.60:19: Unlike the Septuagint, the Masoretic Text does not include "by night" in the second clause; the translation follows the MT strictly.
notes.60:21: Ketiv mt'v ("His planting", 3ms singular) vs. Qere matta'ai ("My plantings", 1cs plural); the Qere is translated, aligning with 1cs "My hands" in the next clause.
notes.61:1: The rare reduplicated noun peqach-qoach, translated 'freedom,' derives from the root paqach ('to open,' usually of eyes) and literally means a 'wide opening,' pointing to the opening of the prison or release from dungeon darkness into light.
notes.61:3: The Hebrew employs wordplay between pe'er ('headdress') and epher ('ashes'), and concludes with the Hithpael infinitive lehithpa'er ('to glorify Himself' or 'display His splendor') from the same root as 'headdress.'
notes.61:6: The rare Hithpael verb tithyammaru ('you will boast') is usually derived from a by-form of amar ('to boast, exalt oneself'), though some derive it from mur ('to exchange,' i.e., succeed to their glory).
notes.61:8: The Masoretic pointing be'olah literally reads 'in a burnt offering' (rejecting stolen goods offered to God), though the same consonants can represent a contracted spelling of 'awlah, 'wrongdoing' or 'injustice.'
notes.61:10: The verb yekahen ('puts on... like a priest') is the Piel of kahan, normally 'to serve as a priest,' here paired with pe'er ('headdress') to evoke a priest's ceremonial turban (cf. 61:3, 6).
notes.62:3: Following the qere tseniph ('turban' or 'diadem'); the written ketiv reads tsenoph, a variant noun form with the same meaning.
notes.62:4: The symbolic names 'My Delight Is in Her' (Hebrew Hephzibah) and 'Married' (Hebrew Beulah) play directly on the verbs chaphets ('delights') and tiba'el ('will be married') at the end of the verse.
notes.62:5: The Masoretic text reads banayikh ('your sons'), picturing the restored inhabitants taking Zion as a bride; the same Hebrew consonants without vowels could also be vocalized bonayikh ('your Builder').
notes.63:3: The verb eg'alti ('I stained') is an Aramaizing Hiphil perfect form of ga'al II ('to stain, defile'), creating wordplay with ge'ulay ('My redemption,' from ga'al I) in v. 4. The noun netsach ('lifeblood') denotes spurting juice or blood.
notes.63:9: Following the qere lo ('to Him'), forming the Hebrew idiom 'He was distressed' (literally 'it was distressing to Him'); the written ketiv reads lo' ('not').
notes.63:11: The Masoretic text has the compressed clause 'remembered the days of old, Moses, His people,' here smoothed with 'His people' as subject, and reads the plural ro'ey ('shepherds of His flock,' e.g., Moses and Aaron).
notes.63:14: The Masoretic verb tenichennu is the Hiphil of nuach ('granted them rest,' literally 'gave it rest,' referring collectively to the people), rather than nachah ('led').
notes.63:19: In the Masoretic verse division the plea 'If only You would tear open the heavens...' belongs to 63:19, and chapter 64 begins with the next verse. The verb nazollu is the Niphal of zalal ('to quake').
notes.64:1: This verse continues the theophany plea of 63:19, whose second half begins the plea in the Masoretic division. The noun hamasim ("brushwood") is a hapax legomenon denoting dry twigs or kindling.
notes.64:2: The verb nazollu ("quaked") is pointed as a Niphal perfect of zll II ("shake, quake"), matching 63:19, though its sound also evokes nzl ("flow, melt").
notes.64:4: The closing clause bahem olam weniwwashea ("in them we have been a long time, and shall we be saved?") is sharply elliptic in the Masoretic Text; "in them" is usually taken to refer to the sins just confessed, with a verb of continuance understood before the Niphal niwwashea.
notes.64:6: The Masoretic form wattemugenu is a transitive Qal wayyiqtol of mwg ("melt, dissolve"), whereas ancient versions such as the Septuagint and Syriac reflect the root mgn ("deliver up").
notes.65:1: The Masoretic vocalization qora is a Pual perfect passive ("was not called by My name"), rather than the Qal active qara ("did not call on My name") reflected in the Septuagint and Vulgate.
notes.65:4: Ketiv/Qere: the Ketiv reads wprq ("piece" or "broth"), while the Qere followed here reads umeraq ("and broth of").
notes.65:5: The Qal perfect with direct object suffix qedashtika ("I am holier than you") uses a comparative construction, or may express infectious taboo holiness ("I would transmit holiness to you" by contact).
notes.65:7: Ketiv/Qere: the Ketiv reads al ("upon"), while the Qere followed here reads el ("into their lap"), contrasting slightly with al-heqam ("onto their lap") in 65:6.
notes.65:11: "Fortune" and "Destiny" translate the definite divine names ha-Gad and ha-Meni; the latter creates a wordplay with umaniti ("I will destine," from mnh) at the beginning of 65:12.
notes.66:3: The four opening clauses use terse verbless juxtapositions without a comparative particle (literally "one who slaughters an ox—one who strikes down a man"), equating hypocritical sacrifices with pagan abominations; awen ("idol") literally means "iniquity" or "wickedness."
notes.66:11: The verb tamotzu ("drink deeply," Qal of mtz) is a hapax legomenon, and the rare noun ziz ("abundance") is cognate with Akkadian zizu ("teat, breast"), paralleling shod ("breast") in the first half of the verse.
notes.66:17: Ketiv/Qere: the Ketiv reads the masculine ehad ("one"), while the Qere followed here reads the feminine ahat ("one"), likely referring to a female cult leader or goddess figure in the center of the garden rite.
notes.66:18: The opening clause we'anoki ma'asehem umahshevotehem ba'ah is highly elliptic in the Masoretic Text, omitting a finite verb after "And I" (supplied as "know") and using the feminine singular Qal participle ba'ah impersonally for "the time is coming."
notes.66:20: The noun kirkarot ("dromedaries") is a hapax legomenon denoting swift riding camels, and tzabbim ("covered wagons") matches Numbers 7:3.

unplaced.text: Stop relying on man, who has breath in his nostrils. For what is he reckoned to be?
unplaced.note: The opening Hebrew idiom literally reads "cease for yourselves from man."

unplaced.text: "Come," they say, "I will get wine, and we will drink deeply of strong drink. And tomorrow will be like this day—vastly greater."
unplaced.note: "They say" is supplied to introduce the abrupt Hebrew quotation, and the closing phrase literally reads "great, exceedingly much."

native_verses.1:1: The vision of Isaiah son of Amoz that he saw regarding Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
native_verses.1:2: Listen, heavens, and give ear, earth, for the LORD has spoken: "I have raised sons and exalted them, yet they have rebelled against Me.
native_verses.1:3: An ox knows its owner, and a donkey its master's feeding trough; Israel does not know, My people do not discern."
native_verses.1:4: Woe, sinful nation, a people heavy with iniquity, seed of evildoers, sons who act corruptly! They have abandoned the LORD, they have spurned the Holy One of Israel, they have turned backward in estrangement.
native_verses.1:5: Why will you still be struck? You keep adding defection! The entire head is sick, and the entire heart is ailing.
native_verses.1:6: From the sole of the foot to the head there is no soundness in it: gashes, bruises, and fresh wounds; they have not been pressed out, nor bound up, nor softened with oil.
native_verses.1:7: Your land is a desolation; your cities are burned with fire; your soil—in your presence foreigners are devouring it, and it is a desolation like an overthrow by foreigners.
native_verses.1:8: And Daughter Zion is left behind like a booth in a vineyard, like a lodging hut in a cucumber field, like a city under siege.
native_verses.1:9: Had the LORD of hosts not left behind a few survivors for us, we would have become like Sodom; we would have resembled Gomorrah.
native_verses.1:10: Listen to the word of the LORD, leaders of Sodom; give ear to the instruction of our God, people of Gomorrah.
native_verses.1:11: "What is the abundance of your sacrifices to Me?" says the LORD. "I have had My fill of burnt offerings of rams and the fat of fattened beasts, and I take no delight in the blood of bulls, lambs, and male goats.
native_verses.1:12: When you come to appear in My presence, who has required this from your hand, to trample My courts?
native_verses.1:13: Do not keep bringing futile offerings; incense is an abomination to Me. New moon and Sabbath, the summoning of a convocation—I cannot bear iniquity and a solemn gathering.
native_verses.1:14: My soul hates your new moons and your appointed festivals; they have become a burden upon Me; I have grown weary of carrying them.
native_verses.1:15: And when you spread out your palms, I will hide My eyes from you; even though you multiply prayer, I am not listening; your hands are filled with bloodshed.
native_verses.1:16: Wash yourselves, purify yourselves; remove the evil of your practices from before My eyes; stop doing evil.
native_verses.1:17: Learn to do good; seek justice, correct the oppressor; vindicate the fatherless, plead the case of the widow."
native_verses.1:18: "Come now, and let us settle the matter," says the LORD. "Even if your sins are like scarlet, they will turn white like snow; even if they are red like crimson, they will become like wool.
native_verses.1:19: If you are willing and obey, you will eat the good things of the land;
native_verses.1:20: but if you refuse and rebel, by the sword you will be devoured," for the mouth of the LORD has spoken.
native_verses.1:21: How the faithful city has become a prostitute—she who was full of justice! Righteousness used to lodge in her, yet now murderers.
native_verses.1:22: Your silver has turned into dross; your choice drink is diluted with water.
native_verses.1:23: Your officials are rebels and associates of thieves; every one of them loves a bribe and pursues payoffs. They do not vindicate the fatherless, and the case of the widow does not come to them.
native_verses.1:24: Therefore the Lord, the LORD of hosts, the Mighty One of Israel, declares: "Ah, I will gain relief from My adversaries and avenge Myself against My enemies.
native_verses.1:25: And I will turn My hand back against you; I will refine away your dross as with lye, and remove all your alloy.
native_verses.1:26: And I will restore your judges as at first, and your advisers as at the outset; after this you will be called City of Righteousness, Faithful City."
native_verses.1:27: Zion will be redeemed through justice, and those in her who turn back, through righteousness.
native_verses.1:28: Yet shattering awaits rebels and sinners together, and those who abandon the LORD will perish.
native_verses.1:29: For they will be ashamed because of the terebinths that you desired, and you will be disgraced because of the gardens that you chose.
native_verses.1:30: For you will become like a terebinth whose foliage is withering, and like a garden that has no water.
native_verses.1:31: And the mighty one will become tinder, and his work a spark; both of them will burn together, with no one to extinguish them.
native_verses.2:1: The word that Isaiah son of Amoz saw regarding Judah and Jerusalem.
native_verses.2:2: And it will happen in the latter days that the mountain of the house of the LORD will be firmly established at the summit of the mountains and lifted up above the hills, and all the nations will stream to it.
native_verses.2:3: And many peoples will go and say, "Come, let us ascend to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob, so that He may instruct us about His ways and we may walk in His paths." For from Zion instruction will go out, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.
native_verses.2:4: And He will judge between the nations and arbitrate for many peoples; they will pound their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning knives; nation will not raise a sword against nation, and they will not learn warfare anymore.
native_verses.2:5: House of Jacob, come, and let us walk in the light of the LORD.
native_verses.2:6: For You have forsaken Your people, the house of Jacob, because they are filled with what comes from the east, and are diviners like the Philistines, and clasp hands with the children of foreigners.
native_verses.2:7: And their land is filled with silver and gold, and their treasuries have no end; their land is filled with horses, and their chariots have no end.
native_verses.2:8: And their land is filled with idols; to the work of their hands they bow down, to what their fingers have made.
native_verses.2:9: So mankind is bowed down, and each man is brought low; and do not forgive them.
native_verses.2:10: Go into the rock and hide yourself in the dust, away from the dread of the LORD and from the splendor of His grandeur.
native_verses.2:11: The haughty eyes of mankind will be brought low, and the loftiness of men will be bowed down; and the LORD alone will be exalted on that day.
native_verses.2:12: For a day belongs to the LORD of hosts against everything proud and lofty, and against everything lifted up, so that it will be brought low;
native_verses.2:13: and against all the lofty and lifted-up cedars of Lebanon, and against all the oaks of Bashan;
native_verses.2:14: and against all the lofty mountains, and against all the hills that are lifted up;
native_verses.2:15: and against every tall tower, and against every fortified wall;
native_verses.2:16: and against all the ships of Tarshish, and against all the prized vessels.
native_verses.2:17: And the haughtiness of mankind will be bowed down, and the loftiness of men will be brought low; and the LORD alone will be exalted on that day.
native_verses.2:18: And the idols will altogether vanish.
native_verses.2:19: And people will go into caves in the rocks and into holes in the dust, away from the dread of the LORD and from the splendor of His grandeur, when He arises to strike terror into the earth.
native_verses.2:20: On that day people will fling away their idols of silver and their idols of gold, which they made for themselves to bow down to, to the moles and to the bats,
native_verses.2:21: to go into the clefts of the rocks and into the crevices of the cliffs, away from the dread of the LORD and from the splendor of His grandeur, when He arises to strike terror into the earth.
native_verses.2:22: Stop relying on man, who has breath in his nostrils. For what is he reckoned to be?
native_verses.3:1: For look, the Lord, the LORD of hosts, is removing from Jerusalem and from Judah support and mainstay, every support of bread and every support of water;
native_verses.3:2: hero and man of war, judge and prophet, diviner and elder,
native_verses.3:3: commander of fifty and honored man, counselor, skilled craftsman, and expert in charms.
native_verses.3:4: And I will make youths their officials, and willful children will rule over them.
native_verses.3:5: And the people will oppress one another, one against another and each against his neighbor; the youth will act arrogantly toward the elder, and the disdained toward the honored.
native_verses.3:6: When a man takes hold of his brother in his father's house, saying, "You have a cloak; be our leader, and let this ruin be under your hand,"
native_verses.3:7: on that day he will speak up, saying, "I will not be a binder of wounds, and in my house there is no bread and no cloak; you must not make me leader of the people."
native_verses.3:8: For Jerusalem has stumbled and Judah has fallen, because their tongue and their deeds are against the LORD, to defy the eyes of His glory.
native_verses.3:9: The appearance of their faces testifies against them, and they proclaim their sin like Sodom; they do not conceal it. Woe to their souls, for they have dealt evil to themselves!
native_verses.3:10: Say of the righteous that it will be well, for they will eat the fruit of their deeds.
native_verses.3:11: Woe to the wicked! It will go ill, for the repayment of his hands will be done to him.
native_verses.3:12: My people—a child is their taskmaster, and women rule over them. My people, those who direct you are leading you astray, and they confound the way of your paths.
native_verses.3:13: The LORD stations Himself to contend, and He stands to judge peoples.
native_verses.3:14: The LORD comes into judgment with the elders of His people and its officials: "You yourselves have consumed the vineyard; what was robbed from the poor is in your houses.
native_verses.3:15: What right do you have to crush My people and grind the faces of the poor?" declares the Lord GOD of hosts.
native_verses.3:16: And the LORD said, "Because the daughters of Zion are haughty and walk with necks stretched out, flirting with their eyes, tripping along as they walk and jingling with their feet,
native_verses.3:17: therefore the Lord will cover the scalps of the daughters of Zion with scabs, and the LORD will expose their private parts."
native_verses.3:18: On that day the Lord will remove the splendor of the anklets, the sun-disks, and the crescents,
native_verses.3:19: the ear-drops, the bracelets, and the veils,
native_verses.3:20: the headdresses, the ankle chains, the sashes, the scent bottles, and the charms,
native_verses.3:21: the rings and the nose rings,
native_verses.3:22: the festive robes, the mantles, the shawls, and the purses,
native_verses.3:23: and the hand mirrors, the fine linens, the turbans, and the wraps.
native_verses.3:24: And it will be that instead of perfume there will be decay; instead of a belt, a rope; instead of braided hair, baldness; instead of a fine robe, a wrapping of sackcloth; and a brand mark instead of beauty.
native_verses.3:25: Your men will fall by the sword, and your might in war.
native_verses.3:26: And her gates will grieve and mourn, and emptied out, she will sit on the ground.
native_verses.4:1: And seven women will grasp one man on that day, saying, "Our own bread we will eat, and our own garments we will wear; only let your name be called over us; remove our disgrace."
native_verses.4:2: On that day the branch of the LORD will be beauty and glory, and the fruit of the land will be majesty and splendor for the survivors of Israel.
native_verses.4:3: And it will be that whoever is left in Zion and whoever remains in Jerusalem will be called holy, everyone written down for life in Jerusalem,
native_verses.4:4: once the Lord has washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion and rinsed the bloodstains of Jerusalem from her midst with a spirit of judgment and a spirit of burning.
native_verses.4:5: Then the LORD will create over the entire place of Mount Zion and over her assemblies a cloud by day and smoke, and the radiance of a blazing fire by night; indeed, over all the glory there will be a canopy.
native_verses.4:6: And there will be a shelter for shade by day from the heat, and as a refuge and cover from downpour and from rain.
native_verses.5:1: Let me sing now for my dear friend the song of my beloved concerning His vineyard: My dear friend had a vineyard on a fertile ridge.
native_verses.5:2: He hoed it and cleared its stones, and planted it with choice vines. He built a tower inside it and also carved a wine vat in it. Then He hoped for it to produce grapes, but it produced foul grapes.
native_verses.5:3: And now, residents of Jerusalem and men of Judah, please judge between Me and My vineyard.
native_verses.5:4: What else was to be done for My vineyard that I did not do in it? Why, when I hoped for it to produce grapes, did it produce foul grapes?
native_verses.5:5: And now let Me make known to you what I am about to do to My vineyard: I will take away its hedge, and it will be consumed; I will breach its wall, and it will be trampled underfoot.
native_verses.5:6: And I will make it a desolation; it will neither be pruned nor hoed, and thorns and briers will spring up; and I will command the clouds not to rain any rain on it.
native_verses.5:7: For the vineyard of the LORD of hosts is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah are the planting of His delight. He hoped for justice, yet look, bloodshed; for righteousness, yet look, an outcry!
native_verses.5:8: Woe to those who connect house to house, bringing field next to field, until no space remains and you are made to live alone in the middle of the land.
native_verses.5:9: In my ears the LORD of hosts has spoken: "Surely many houses will turn to desolation, large and fine ones, with no one dwelling in them.
native_verses.5:10: For ten acres of vineyard will produce a single bath, and a homer of seed will produce an ephah."
native_verses.5:11: Woe to those who rise early in the morning, chasing after strong drink, who linger into the evening while wine inflames them!
native_verses.5:12: Their feasts are lyre and harp, tambourine and flute and wine, yet they do not look at the deed of the LORD, nor do they see the work of His hands.
native_verses.5:13: Therefore My people have gone into exile for lack of knowledge; their honored ones are men of hunger, and their throng is parched from thirst.
native_verses.5:14: Therefore Sheol has widened its throat and opened its mouth without limit, and down descend her splendor, her throng, her uproar, and whoever exults in her.
native_verses.5:15: So mankind is bowed down and each man is brought low, and the eyes of the lofty will be brought low.
native_verses.5:16: But the LORD of hosts is lifted high by justice, and the holy God proves Himself holy by righteousness.
native_verses.5:17: Then lambs will graze as in their own pasture, and sojourners will feed on the ruins of the wealthy.
native_verses.5:18: Woe to those who haul iniquity with cords of deceit, and sin as with wagon ropes,
native_verses.5:19: who say, "Let Him hurry, let Him speed up His work so that we may see it; let the plan of the Holy One of Israel approach and arrive so that we may know it!"
native_verses.5:20: Woe to those who pronounce evil good and good evil, who set darkness as light and light as darkness, who set bitter as sweet and sweet as bitter!
native_verses.5:21: Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes and discerning before their own faces!
native_verses.5:22: Woe to those who are champions at drinking wine and men of valor at mixing strong drink,
native_verses.5:23: who declare the wicked righteous for a bribe, yet take away the righteousness of the righteous from each of them!
native_verses.5:24: Therefore, as a tongue of fire eats up stubble and dry grass sinks into flame, so their root will become like decay and their blossom will rise like dust; because they have rejected the instruction of the LORD of hosts and have spurned the word of the Holy One of Israel.
native_verses.5:25: For this reason the anger of the LORD flared against His people, and He stretched out His hand against them and struck them. The mountains quaked, and their corpses were like refuse in the middle of the streets. Despite all this, His anger has not turned back, and still His hand is stretched out.
native_verses.5:26: He will raise a banner for the nations far away and whistle for them from the end of the earth; and look, swiftly and rapidly they come!
native_verses.5:27: Not one among them is weary, and not one stumbles; not one dozes and not one sleeps; no belt on their waists is loosened, nor is any strap of their sandals snapped.
native_verses.5:28: Their arrows are sharpened, and all their bows are strung; the hooves of their horses are reckoned like flint, and their wheels like a storm wind.
native_verses.5:29: Their roar is like a lion; they roar like young lions. They growl and seize prey, and carry it away, with no one to rescue.
native_verses.5:30: And on that day they will roar over it like the roaring of the sea. And if one looks to the land, look, darkness and distress, and the light has grown dark in its clouds.
native_verses.6:1: In the year of the death of King Uzziah, I saw the Lord seated on a throne, lofty and lifted up, and the hems of His robe were filling the temple.
native_verses.6:2: Seraphim were standing above Him; each one had six wings: with two he would cover his face, and with two he would cover his feet, and with two he would fly.
native_verses.6:3: And one would call to another and say, "Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of hosts; the fullness of all the earth is His glory."
native_verses.6:4: And the bases of the thresholds trembled at the voice of the one calling, and the house was filling with smoke.
native_verses.6:5: Then I said, "Woe to me, for I am destroyed, because I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips; for my eyes have seen the King, the LORD of hosts."
native_verses.6:6: And one of the seraphim flew to me, and in his hand was a glowing coal that he had taken with tongs from the altar.
native_verses.6:7: He touched it to my mouth and said, "Look, this has touched your lips; your iniquity has departed, and your sin is atoned for."
native_verses.6:8: And I heard the Lord's voice saying, "Whom shall I send, and who will go for Us?" So I said, "Here I am; send me."
native_verses.6:9: And He said, "Go and tell this people, 'Keep hearing, yet do not understand; and keep seeing, yet do not know.'
native_verses.6:10: Make the heart of this people fat, make its ears heavy, and smear its eyes shut, otherwise it might see with its eyes, and hear with its ears, and understand with its heart, and turn back and be healed."
native_verses.6:11: Then I said, "How long, Lord?" And He said, "Until cities fall into ruins without an inhabitant, and houses without a human being, and the ground is ruined into a desolation,
native_verses.6:12: and the LORD has sent humanity far away, and forsakenness grows vast in the midst of the land.
native_verses.6:13: And even though a tenth still remains in it, it will again be for burning—like a terebinth and like an oak which, when felled, still have a stump in them; a holy seed is its stump."
native_verses.7:1: Now it happened in the days of Ahaz, son of Jotham, son of Uzziah, king of Judah, that Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up to Jerusalem for war against it, yet he was not able to fight against it.
native_verses.7:2: When it was reported to the house of David, "Aram has settled upon Ephraim," his heart and the heart of his people trembled as the trees of a forest tremble before the wind.
native_verses.7:3: Then the LORD said to Isaiah, "Go out now to meet Ahaz, you and your son Shear-jashub, at the end of the water channel of the upper pool, by the highway of the launderer's field,
native_verses.7:4: and say to him, 'Take care and keep calm; do not be afraid, and do not let your heart grow faint because of these two tail ends of smoking firebrands, at the burning anger of Rezin and Aram and the son of Remaliah.
native_verses.7:5: Because Aram has devised evil against you, along with Ephraim and the son of Remaliah, saying,
native_verses.7:6: "Let us go up against Judah and fill it with dread, and breach it for ourselves, and install a king in its midst, the son of Tabeel,"
native_verses.7:7: this is what the Lord GOD says: "It will not stand, and it will not happen.
native_verses.7:8: For the head of Aram is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin; and within another sixty-five years Ephraim will be shattered from being a people.
native_verses.7:9: And the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is the son of Remaliah. If you do not trust, surely you will not remain firm."'"
native_verses.7:10: And the LORD spoke again to Ahaz, saying,
native_verses.7:11: "Ask a sign for yourself from the LORD your God; go deep in asking, or go high above."
native_verses.7:12: Then Ahaz said, "I will not ask, and I will not test the LORD."
native_verses.7:13: Then he said, "Listen now, house of David: is it too small a thing for you to weary men, that you weary my God as well?
native_verses.7:14: Therefore the Lord Himself will give you a sign: see, the young woman is pregnant and will give birth to a son, and she will call his name Immanuel.
native_verses.7:15: He will eat curds and honey by the time he knows how to reject the evil and choose the good.
native_verses.7:16: For before the boy knows how to reject the evil and choose the good, the land that you dread because of its two kings will be forsaken.
native_verses.7:17: The LORD will bring on you, and on your people, and on your father's house, days that have not come since the day Ephraim departed from Judah—the king of Assyria.
native_verses.7:18: And it will happen on that day that the LORD will whistle for the fly that is at the end of the streams of Egypt, and for the bee that is in the land of Assyria.
native_verses.7:19: And all of them will come and settle in the precipitous ravines, and in the crevices of the crags, and on all the thornbushes, and at all the watering places.
native_verses.7:20: On that day, with a razor hired from the regions beyond the River—with the king of Assyria—the Lord will shave the head and the hair of the feet, and it will sweep away the beard as well.
native_verses.7:21: And it will happen on that day that a man will keep alive a young cow of the herd and two sheep,
native_verses.7:22: and it will happen that because of the abundance of milk they produce, he will eat curds; for everyone remaining in the midst of the land will eat curds and honey.
native_verses.7:23: And it will happen on that day that every spot where there are a thousand vines, valued at a thousand silver pieces, will belong to briers and thorns.
native_verses.7:24: With arrows and a bow one will go there, for the whole land will be briers and thorns.
native_verses.7:25: And as for all the hills that used to be hoed with a hoe, you will not go there out of fear of briers and thorns; instead, it will become a place for turning an ox loose and a trampling ground for sheep."
native_verses.8:1: Then the LORD said to me, "Take for yourself a large tablet and write on it with a human stylus, 'Belonging to Maher-shalal-hash-baz.'
native_verses.8:2: And I will summon for Myself trustworthy witnesses—Uriah the priest and Zechariah son of Jeberechiah."
native_verses.8:3: Then I approached the prophetess, and she conceived and bore a son. And the LORD said to me, "Call his name Maher-shalal-hash-baz;
native_verses.8:4: for before the boy knows how to call out, 'My father' and 'My mother,' the wealth of Damascus and the plunder of Samaria will be carried off before the king of Assyria."
native_verses.8:5: And the LORD spoke to me yet again, saying,
native_verses.8:6: "Because this people has rejected the waters of Shiloah that flow gently, and rejoices with Rezin and the son of Remaliah,
native_verses.8:7: therefore, look, the Lord is bringing up over them the mighty and abundant waters of the River—the king of Assyria and all his glory; and it will rise over all its channels and flow over all its banks.
native_verses.8:8: It will sweep on into Judah, overflowing and passing through; it will reach up to the neck, and the spread of its wings will fill the width of your land, Immanuel."
native_verses.8:9: Break to pieces, peoples, and be shattered, and give ear, all far reaches of the earth! Gird yourselves, and be shattered; gird yourselves, and be shattered!
native_verses.8:10: Devise a plan, and it will be frustrated; speak a word, and it will not stand, for God is with us.
native_verses.8:11: For this is how the LORD spoke to me with the force of His hand, and admonished me not to walk in the way of this people, saying,
native_verses.8:12: "You must not call 'conspiracy' all that this people calls 'conspiracy,' and what it fears you must not fear, nor regard with dread.
native_verses.8:13: The LORD of hosts—Him you must regard as holy; He is to be your fear, and He is to be your dread.
native_verses.8:14: And He will become a sanctuary, and a stone of striking and a rock of stumbling to the two houses of Israel, a trap and a snare to the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
native_verses.8:15: And many will stumble over them; they will fall and be broken, and be snared and captured."
native_verses.8:16: Bind up the testimony; seal the instruction among my disciples.
native_verses.8:17: And I will wait for the LORD, who conceals His face from the house of Jacob, and I will hope for Him.
native_verses.8:18: Look, I and the children whom the LORD has given me are for signs and portents in Israel from the LORD of hosts, who dwells on Mount Zion.
native_verses.8:19: And when they say to you, "Inquire of the mediums and the spiritists who chirp and mutter," should not a people inquire of its God? Should they inquire of the dead on behalf of the living?
native_verses.8:20: To the instruction and to the testimony! If they do not speak in accordance with this word, it is because there is no dawn for them.
native_verses.8:21: Each one will pass through the land, hard-pressed and hungry; and it will happen that when he is hungry, he will grow enraged and curse his king and his God, and turn upward.
native_verses.8:22: Then he will look toward the earth, and see: distress and darkness, the gloom of anguish; and he will be thrust into thick darkness.
native_verses.8:23: Yet there will be no gloom for her who was in anguish. In the earlier time He brought dishonor upon the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, but in the later time He will bring honor to the way of the sea, the region across the Jordan, Galilee of the nations.
native_verses.9:1: The people walking in darkness have seen a great light; on those living in a land of death's shadow, light has shone.
native_verses.9:2: You have multiplied the nation; for it You have made the joy great. They rejoice before You like the joy in the harvest, just as they exult when they divide plunder.
native_verses.9:3: For You have shattered the yoke of its burden, and the staff across its shoulder, the rod of the one oppressing it, just as on the day of Midian.
native_verses.9:4: For every boot of one tramping in tumult, and every cloak rolled in blood, will be for burning, food for fire.
native_verses.9:5: For a child has been born to us, a son has been given to us; and the dominion will be on his shoulder, and his name will be called Wonder-Counselor, Mighty God, Father of Eternity, Prince of Peace.
native_verses.9:6: Of the increase of the dominion and of peace there will be no end, upon the throne of David and over his kingdom, to establish it and to sustain it with justice and with righteousness, from now on and forever. The zeal of the LORD of hosts will perform this.
native_verses.9:7: The Lord sent a word against Jacob, and it has fallen upon Israel.
native_verses.9:8: And the whole people will know it—Ephraim and those dwelling in Samaria—saying in pride and haughtiness of heart,
native_verses.9:9: "Bricks have fallen, yet we will build with hewn stone; sycamores have been felled, yet we will substitute cedars for them."
native_verses.9:10: So the LORD raised high the adversaries of Rezin against him and spurred on his enemies.
native_verses.9:11: Aram from the east and the Philistines from the west—they devoured Israel with wide-open mouth. Despite all this, His anger has not turned back, and His hand is still outstretched.
native_verses.9:12: Yet the people have not turned back to Him who struck them, and they have not sought the LORD of hosts.
native_verses.9:13: So the LORD cut off from Israel head and tail, palm frond and bulrush, in a single day.
native_verses.9:14: The elder and the distinguished man is the head, and the prophet teaching falsehood is the tail.
native_verses.9:15: And those guiding this people have become ones who lead astray, and those guided by them are swallowed up.
native_verses.9:16: Therefore the Lord will not rejoice over their young men, nor will He show compassion to their orphans and their widows; for each of them is godless and practices evil, and every mouth utters folly. Despite all this, His anger has not turned back, and His hand is still outstretched.
native_verses.9:17: For wickedness has burned like fire; it devours briers and thorns; it ignites among the thickets of the forest, and they billow upward in a swelling of smoke.
native_verses.9:18: Through the fury of the LORD of hosts, the land has been scorched, and the people have become like food for fire; no one spares his brother.
native_verses.9:19: One slices off on the right and remains hungry, and eats on the left, yet they are not filled; each person consumes the flesh of his own arm.
native_verses.9:20: Manasseh consumes Ephraim, and Ephraim consumes Manasseh, and both together are against Judah. Despite all this, His anger has not turned back, and His hand is still outstretched.
native_verses.10:1: Woe to those who enact statutes of iniquity, and to scribes who write out oppression,
native_verses.10:2: to turn the poor away from justice and to rob the afflicted of My people of their legal right, so that widows become their plunder and they may loot the orphans.
native_verses.10:3: And what will you do for the day of reckoning, and at the devastation arriving from far away? To whom will you flee for aid, and where will you leave your glory?
native_verses.10:4: There is nothing left except to bow down beneath the captives or to fall beneath the slaughtered. Despite all this, His anger has not turned back, and His hand is still outstretched.
native_verses.10:5: Woe, Assyria, rod of My anger—and the staff in their hand is My indignation!
native_verses.10:6: I send him forth against a godless nation, and against the people of My fury I charge him, to plunder spoil and to loot booty, and to make them a trampling place like mud of the streets.
native_verses.10:7: Yet he does not intend it this way, and his heart does not think this way; rather, it is in his heart to destroy and to cut off not a few nations.
native_verses.10:8: For he says, "Are not my princes kings altogether?
native_verses.10:9: Is Calno not like Carchemish? Is Hamath not like Arpad? Is Samaria not like Damascus?
native_verses.10:10: Just as my hand found the kingdoms of the idols, whose carved images surpassed those of Jerusalem and Samaria,
native_verses.10:11: just as I have done to Samaria and to her idols, will I not do the same to Jerusalem and to her images?"
native_verses.10:12: And it will happen, when the Lord has finished all His work on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, that I will punish the fruit of the king of Assyria's haughty heart and the boastfulness of his lofty eyes.
native_verses.10:13: For he said, "By the strength of my hand I have acted, and by my wisdom, for I am discerning; I removed the borders of peoples, and their stored treasures I pillaged, and like a mighty one I brought down the inhabitants.
native_verses.10:14: And like a nest my hand found the wealth of the peoples; just as someone gathers abandoned eggs, I myself gathered the whole earth, and there was not one flapping a wing, or opening a mouth, or chirping."
native_verses.10:15: Will the ax boast over the one who chops with it, or will the saw exalt itself over the one who swings it? As though a rod should swing those who lift it, or as though a staff should lift someone who is not wood!
native_verses.10:16: Therefore the Lord, the LORD of hosts, will send a wasting illness among his stout ones, and beneath his glory a burning will blaze like the blaze of fire.
native_verses.10:17: And the Light of Israel will turn into a fire, and its Holy One into a flame; it will blaze and consume his thorns and his briers in a single day.
native_verses.10:18: And He will bring to an end the glory of his forest and his fruitful orchard, from soul even to flesh, and it will be like a sick man melting away.
native_verses.10:19: And the remnant of the trees in his forest will be few in number, and a boy could write them down.
native_verses.10:20: And it will happen in that day that the remnant of Israel and the surviving ones of the house of Jacob will no longer lean on the one who struck them, but will lean in truth on the LORD, the Holy One of Israel.
native_verses.10:21: A remnant will return—the remnant of Jacob—to Mighty God.
native_verses.10:22: For even though your people Israel should be like the sand of the sea, a remnant among them will return; annihilation is decreed, flooding with righteousness.
native_verses.10:23: For the Lord GOD of hosts is carrying out a complete and decreed destruction in the midst of the entire earth.
native_verses.10:24: Therefore this is what the Lord GOD of hosts says: "Do not fear Assyria, My people dwelling in Zion, when he strikes you with the rod and raises his staff against you in the manner of Egypt.
native_verses.10:25: For in just a very short while, indignation will be over, and My anger will turn to their destruction."
native_verses.10:26: And the LORD of hosts will rouse a whip against him, like the striking of Midian at the rock of Oreb; and His staff will be over the sea, and He will raise it in the manner of Egypt.
native_verses.10:27: And it will happen in that day that his burden will lift from your shoulder, and his yoke from your neck, and the yoke will be destroyed because of fatness.
native_verses.10:28: He has come upon Aiath; he has passed through Migron; at Michmash he deposits his supplies.
native_verses.10:29: They have crossed the pass; at Geba they took their night's lodging; Ramah quakes; Gibeah of Saul has fled.
native_verses.10:30: Cry shrilly with your voice, daughter of Gallim! Listen closely, Laishah! Afflicted Anathoth!
native_verses.10:31: Madmenah flees away; the residents of Gebim have taken refuge.
native_verses.10:32: Even today he will stop at Nob; he shakes his hand against the mountain of Daughter Zion, the hill of Jerusalem.
native_verses.10:33: Look, the Lord, the LORD of hosts, is lopping off the boughs with terrifying force; the tall in stature are felled, and the high ones will sink low.
native_verses.10:34: And He will chop down the thickets of the forest with iron, and Lebanon will fall by a Mighty One.
native_verses.11:1: Yet a shoot will come out from the stump of Jesse, and a sprout from his roots will bear fruit.
native_verses.11:2: And the Spirit of the LORD will rest on him—the Spirit of wisdom and discernment, the Spirit of counsel and power, the Spirit of knowledge and the fear of the LORD.
native_verses.11:3: And his delight will be in the fear of the LORD; he will not judge according to the sight of his eyes, nor decide according to the hearing of his ears.
native_verses.11:4: Rather, he will judge the poor in righteousness, and he will decide in fairness for the humble of the earth; with the rod of his mouth he will strike the earth, and with the breath of his lips he will put the wicked to death.
native_verses.11:5: And righteousness will be the sash around his waist, and faithfulness the sash around his loins.
native_verses.11:6: And a wolf will dwell with a lamb, and a leopard will lie down with a young goat; a calf and a young lion and a fatling will be together, and a small boy will lead them.
native_verses.11:7: A cow and a bear will graze; together their young will lie down, and a lion, like the ox, will eat straw.
native_verses.11:8: And a nursing infant will play over a cobra's hole, and a weaned child will stretch out his hand over a viper's den.
native_verses.11:9: They will do no harm and cause no destruction throughout all My holy mountain, for the earth will be filled with knowledge of the LORD, just as the waters cover the sea.
native_verses.11:10: And it will happen in that day that the root of Jesse, who stands as a banner for peoples—nations will seek him out, and his place of rest will be glorious.
native_verses.11:11: And it will happen in that day that the Lord will once more reach out His hand a second time to reclaim the remnant of His people that is left from Assyria, from Egypt, from Pathros, from Cush, from Elam, from Shinar, from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea.
native_verses.11:12: And He will raise a banner for the nations, and He will gather the outcasts of Israel and assemble the scattered ones of Judah from the four corners of the earth.
native_verses.11:13: And Ephraim's envy will pass away, and the adversaries of Judah will be cut off; Ephraim will not envy Judah, and Judah will not show hostility toward Ephraim.
native_verses.11:14: And they will swoop down on the slope of the Philistines toward the west; together they will loot the sons of the east. Against Edom and Moab they will stretch out their hand, and the sons of Ammon will be obedient to them.
native_verses.11:15: And the LORD will completely destroy the tongue of the Sea of Egypt; He will wave His hand over the River with the scorching heat of His wind, and He will strike it into seven streams and make people walk across in sandals.
native_verses.11:16: And there will be a highway for the remnant of His people that is left from Assyria, just as there was for Israel on the day they came up from the land of Egypt.
native_verses.12:1: And on that day you will say, "I will thank You, LORD, for although You were angry with me, Your anger has turned back and You comfort me.
native_verses.12:2: Look, God is my salvation; I will trust and will not be terrified, for the LORD, the LORD, is my strength and song, and He has become salvation to me."
native_verses.12:3: And you will draw water with gladness from the springs of salvation.
native_verses.12:4: And on that day you will say, "Give thanks to the LORD; call on His name; make His deeds known among the peoples; declare that His name is exalted.
native_verses.12:5: Sing praises to the LORD, for He has done majestic things; this is made known in all the earth.
native_verses.12:6: Cry aloud and sing out, inhabitant of Zion, for the Holy One of Israel is great in your midst."
native_verses.13:1: The pronouncement concerning Babylon that Isaiah the son of Amoz saw.
native_verses.13:2: On a bare mountain lift up a banner; raise your voice to them; wave a hand, so that they may enter the gates of the nobles.
native_verses.13:3: I Myself have commanded My consecrated ones; I have also summoned My mighty warriors for My anger, those who exult in My majesty.
native_verses.13:4: The sound of a tumult on the mountains, the likeness of a vast people! The sound of an uproar of kingdoms, of nations assembling together! The LORD of hosts is marshaling an army for war.
native_verses.13:5: They are coming from a distant land, from the end of the heavens, the LORD and the instruments of His indignation, to ruin all the earth.
native_verses.13:6: Wail, for the day of the LORD is near; like devastation from the Almighty it will come.
native_verses.13:7: Therefore all hands will go limp, and the heart of every mortal will melt.
native_verses.13:8: And they will be terrified; pangs and birth pains will grip them; like a woman giving birth they will writhe. Each will stare aghast at his companion; their faces will be faces of flames.
native_verses.13:9: Look, the day of the LORD is coming, cruel, with wrath and burning anger, to make the earth a desolation, and He will wipe out its sinners from it.
native_verses.13:10: For the stars of the heavens and their constellations will not shine out their light; the sun will grow dark as it rises, and the moon will not cause its light to shine.
native_verses.13:11: And I will call the world to account for evil, and the wicked for their iniquity; I will make the arrogance of the insolent cease, and the pride of the ruthless I will bring low.
native_verses.13:12: I will make mortals scarcer than refined gold, and human beings than the choice gold of Ophir.
native_verses.13:13: Therefore I will make the heavens tremble, and the earth will quake from its place at the wrath of the LORD of hosts and on the day of His burning anger.
native_verses.13:14: And it will be that like a chased gazelle, and like a flock with no one gathering it, each will turn to his own people, and each will flee to his own land.
native_verses.13:15: Everyone who is found will be pierced through, and everyone who is caught will fall by the sword.
native_verses.13:16: And their little children will be dashed to pieces before their eyes; their houses will be looted, and their wives will be violated.
native_verses.13:17: Look, I am rousing the Medes against them, who do not value silver, and as for gold, they take no pleasure in it.
native_verses.13:18: And bows will dash young men to pieces; they will have no compassion on the fruit of the womb; their eye will not spare children.
native_verses.13:19: And Babylon, the splendor of kingdoms, the beauty of the pride of the Chaldeans, will be as in God's overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah.
native_verses.13:20: It will never be inhabited, nor will it be dwelt in from generation to generation; no Arab will pitch a tent there, and no shepherds will let their flocks lie down there.
native_verses.13:21: But desert animals will lie down there, and their houses will be filled with howling creatures; ostriches will dwell there, and wild goats will leap about there.
native_verses.13:22: Hyenas will howl in its citadels, and jackals in palaces of luxury. Its time is near to come, and its days will not be drawn out.
native_verses.14:1: For the LORD will show compassion to Jacob and will choose Israel once more, and settle them on their own land; and the sojourner will join himself to them, and they will attach themselves to the house of Jacob.
native_verses.14:2: And peoples will take them and bring them to their place, and the house of Israel will take them as an inheritance on the land of the LORD, as male servants and female servants; and they will be captors of their captors and rule over their oppressors.
native_verses.14:3: And it will happen on the day the LORD gives you rest from your pain and your agitation, and from the hard labor you were made to serve,
native_verses.14:4: that you will take up this taunt against the king of Babylon and say, "How the oppressor has ceased! The exaction of gold has ceased!
native_verses.14:5: The LORD has broken the staff of the wicked, the rod of the rulers,
native_verses.14:6: that struck peoples in wrath with a blow without ceasing, that ruled nations in anger with persecution without restraint.
native_verses.14:7: All the earth rests and is still; they burst forth into a shout of joy.
native_verses.14:8: Even the cypresses rejoice over you, the cedars of Lebanon: 'Since you have lain down, no woodcutter comes up against us.'
native_verses.14:9: Sheol below is agitated for you to meet your coming; it rouses the shades for you, all the leaders of the earth; it raises up from their thrones all the kings of the nations.
native_verses.14:10: All of them will answer and say to you, 'You also have been made weak like us; you have become just like us.'
native_verses.14:11: Your pomp has been brought down to Sheol, the music of your harps; beneath you maggots are spread out, and worms are your coverings.
native_verses.14:12: How you have fallen from the heavens, Shining One, son of the dawn! You have been hewn down to the earth, you who laid nations prostrate!
native_verses.14:13: Yet you said in your heart, 'To the heavens I will ascend; above the stars of God I will lift up my throne, and I will sit on the mountain of assembly, in the farthest recesses of the north;
native_verses.14:14: I will ascend above the cloud heights; I will become like the Most High.'
native_verses.14:15: Instead, you will be brought down to Sheol, to the farthest recesses of the Pit.
native_verses.14:16: Those who see you will gaze intently at you; they will consider you closely: 'Is this the man who made the earth tremble, who made kingdoms quake,
native_verses.14:17: who made the world like the wilderness and demolished its cities, who did not release his prisoners to go home?'
native_verses.14:18: All the kings of the nations, all of them, lie in honor, each in his own house.
native_verses.14:19: But you have been thrown out away from your grave like a detested branch, clothed with those killed, pierced by the sword, who go down to the stones of the Pit, like a corpse trampled underfoot.
native_verses.14:20: You will not be united with them in burial, for you have ruined your land, you have killed your people. The seed of evildoers will never be named.
native_verses.14:21: Prepare a slaughter place for his sons because of the iniquity of their fathers, so that they will not rise up and possess the earth and fill the surface of the world with cities."
native_verses.14:22: "And I will rise up against them," declares the LORD of hosts, "and I will cut off from Babylon name and remnant, offspring and descendants," declares the LORD.
native_verses.14:23: "And I will turn it into a possession for the hedgehog and marshes of water, and I will sweep it away with the broom of destruction," declares the LORD of hosts.
native_verses.14:24: The LORD of hosts has sworn, saying, "Surely, just as I have intended, so it will happen, and just as I have planned, that will stand:
native_verses.14:25: to break Assyria in My land, and on My mountains I will trample him underfoot; and his yoke will depart from them, and his burden will depart from his shoulder."
native_verses.14:26: This is the plan that has been planned over all the earth, and this is the hand stretched out over all the nations.
native_verses.14:27: For the LORD of hosts has planned, and who will thwart it? And His outstretched hand—who will turn it back?
native_verses.14:28: In the year of King Ahaz's death, this pronouncement came:
native_verses.14:29: Do not rejoice, Philistia, all of you, that the rod of the one who struck you has been broken; for out of the snake's root a viper will come forth, and its fruit will be a flying fiery serpent.
native_verses.14:30: And the firstborn of the poor will graze, and the needy will lie down in security; but I will put your root to death by famine, and he will kill your remnant.
native_verses.14:31: Wail, gate; cry out, city; melt away, Philistia, all of you! For smoke is coming from the north, and no one straggles in his ranks.
native_verses.14:32: And what will one reply to the messengers of the nation? "The LORD has founded Zion, and in it the afflicted of His people will take refuge."
native_verses.15:1: The pronouncement concerning Moab: Truly, in a night Ar of Moab is ravaged, it is cut off; truly, in a night Kir of Moab is ravaged, it is cut off.
native_verses.15:2: Bayith and Dibon have gone up to the high places to weep; over Nebo and over Medeba Moab wails. On all its heads is baldness; every beard is shaved off.
native_verses.15:3: In its streets they have wrapped themselves in sackcloth; on its rooftops and in its public squares everyone wails, going down in weeping.
native_verses.15:4: Heshbon and Elealeh cry out; as far as Jahaz their voice is heard. Therefore the armed warriors of Moab shout aloud; its soul quivers within it.
native_verses.15:5: My heart cries out for Moab; its fugitives flee as far as Zoar, to Eglath-shelishiyah. For on the ascent of Luhith one goes up with weeping; for along the road to Horonaim they stir up a cry of ruin.
native_verses.15:6: For the waters of Nimrim will become desolations; indeed, the grass has dried up, the tender shoots have vanished, no greenery remains.
native_verses.15:7: Therefore the surplus it has acquired and their stored possessions they carry across the Wadi of the Willows.
native_verses.15:8: For the outcry has encircled the border of Moab; as far as Eglaim reaches its wailing, and to Beer-elim its wailing.
native_verses.15:9: For the waters of Dimon are full of blood; indeed, I will lay still more upon Dimon: a lion for those of Moab who escape, and for the remnant of the land.
native_verses.16:1: Send a lamb for the ruler of the land, from Sela across the wilderness to the mountain of Daughter Zion.
native_verses.16:2: And it will be that like a fleeing bird, a nest driven out, so the daughters of Moab will be at the fords of the Arnon.
native_verses.16:3: Bring counsel, execute judgment; set your shade like the night in the middle of noon; hide the outcasts, do not expose the fugitive.
native_verses.16:4: Let My outcasts sojourn with you, Moab; be a shelter for them from the ravager. For the oppressor has ceased, ravaging has come to an end, and those who trample are gone from the land.
native_verses.16:5: And a throne will be established in loyal love, and in truth a judge will sit upon it in the tent of David, seeking justice and swift in righteousness.
native_verses.16:6: We have heard of Moab's pride, how exceedingly proud it is—of its arrogance, its pride, and its insolence; its boasts are not true.
native_verses.16:7: Therefore Moab will wail for Moab; all of it will wail. For the raisin cakes of Kir-hareseth you will groan, utterly crushed.
