native_verses.16:8: For the fields of Heshbon wither, as does the vine of Sibmah; the lords of the nations have struck down its choice vines—they reached as far as Jazer, they strayed into the wilderness; its shoots spread out, they crossed the sea.
native_verses.16:9: Therefore I will weep with Jazer's weeping for the vine of Sibmah; I will soak you with My tears, Heshbon and Elealeh, for upon your summer fruit and upon your harvest the shouting has fallen.
native_verses.16:10: And gladness and joy are withdrawn from the orchard; in the vineyards there will be no singing for joy and no cheering; no treader will tread wine in the winepresses; I have made the shouting cease.
native_verses.16:11: Therefore My inward parts groan like a lyre for Moab, and My inner being for Kir-heres.
native_verses.16:12: And it will happen that when Moab appears, when it wears itself out on the high place and comes to its sanctuary to pray, it will not prevail.
native_verses.16:13: This is the word that the LORD spoke about Moab long ago.
native_verses.16:14: And now the LORD has spoken, saying, "In three years, as the years of a hired laborer, the glory of Moab will be dishonored, along with all the great multitude; and the remnant will be very small and meager, not mighty."
native_verses.17:1: The pronouncement concerning Damascus: Look, Damascus is being removed from being a city, and it will become a fallen heap of ruins.
native_verses.17:2: Abandoned are the cities of Aroer; they will belong to flocks, and they will lie down with no one to alarm them.
native_verses.17:3: The fortress will cease from Ephraim, and kingship from Damascus, and the remnant of Aram—they will be like the glory of the sons of Israel, declares the LORD of hosts.
native_verses.17:4: And it will come about on that day that the glory of Jacob will dwindle, and the fatness of his flesh will waste away.
native_verses.17:5: And it will be as when a harvester gathers standing grain and his arm harvests the heads of grain; and it will be like someone gleaning heads of grain in the Valley of Rephaim.
native_verses.17:6: Yet gleanings will remain in it, as at the beating of an olive tree: two or three berries at the tip of the topmost bough, four or five on the branches of a fruit-bearing tree, declares the LORD, the God of Israel.
native_verses.17:7: On that day man will look toward his Maker, and his eyes will gaze upon the Holy One of Israel.
native_verses.17:8: And he will not look toward the altars, the work of his hands, nor will he gaze upon what his fingers have made—the Asherah poles and the incense altars.
native_verses.17:9: On that day the cities of his stronghold will be like the abandoned places of the woodland and the summit, which they abandoned before the sons of Israel; and it will become a desolation.
native_verses.17:10: For you have forgotten the God of your salvation and have not remembered the Rock of your stronghold. Therefore you plant plantings of delight and sow alien vine shoots.
native_verses.17:11: On the day of your planting you make it grow, and in the morning you bring your seed to blossom; yet gone is the harvest on a day of sickness and incurable pain.
native_verses.17:12: Woe! The roar of many peoples—like the roaring of seas they roar! And the thunder of nations—like the thunder of mighty waters they thunder!
native_verses.17:13: Nations thunder like the thunder of many waters, yet He will rebuke them, and they will flee far away, and be pursued like chaff of the mountains before the wind and like tumbleweed before a whirlwind.
native_verses.17:14: At evening time, look—terror! Before morning, they are gone. This is the share of those who despoil us, and the lot for those who loot us.
native_verses.18:1: Ah, land of buzzing wings, which lies beyond the rivers of Cush,
native_verses.18:2: sending envoys by the sea and in papyrus vessels upon the surface of the waters. Go, swift messengers, to a nation tall and smooth, to a people dreaded far and wide, a nation of might and trampling, whose land rivers cut through.
native_verses.18:3: All inhabitants of the world and dwellers on the earth, when a banner is lifted on the mountains, look, and when a horn is blown, listen.
native_verses.18:4: For this is what the LORD has said to me: "I will stay quiet and watch from My dwelling place, like glowing heat in sunlight, like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest."
native_verses.18:5: For before the harvest, when the blossoming is over and the flower becomes a ripening grape, He will cut off the shoots with pruning knives, and the spreading branches He will remove and lop off.
native_verses.18:6: They will be left together for the birds of prey of the mountains and for the beasts of the earth; the birds of prey will pass the summer on them, and all the beasts of the earth will pass the winter on them.
native_verses.18:7: At that time tribute will be brought to the LORD of hosts from a people tall and smooth, and from a people dreaded far and wide, a nation of might and trampling, whose land rivers cut through, to the place of the name of the LORD of hosts, Mount Zion.
native_verses.19:1: A pronouncement concerning Egypt. Look, the LORD is riding on a swift cloud and coming into Egypt; the idols of Egypt will shake before Him, and the heart of Egypt will melt within it.
native_verses.19:2: "And I will incite Egypt against Egypt, and they will fight, each against his brother and each against his neighbor, city against city, kingdom against kingdom.
native_verses.19:3: And the spirit of Egypt will be emptied out within it, and I will confound its counsel; they will consult the idols and the ghosts, the mediums and the spiritists.
native_verses.19:4: And I will deliver Egypt into the hand of a harsh master, and a fierce king will rule over them," declares the Lord, the LORD of hosts.
native_verses.19:5: And the waters will fail from the sea, and the river will be parched and dry up.
native_verses.19:6: The rivers will grow foul; the channels of Egypt will dwindle and be parched; reed and rush will wither away.
native_verses.19:7: There will be bare places along the Nile, at the mouth of the Nile, and all the sown land of the Nile will dry up, be blown away, and be no more.
native_verses.19:8: The fishermen will lament, and all who cast a hook into the Nile will mourn, and those who spread a net upon the surface of the waters will languish.
native_verses.19:9: Those who work with combed flax and those who weave white cloth will be put to shame.
native_verses.19:10: Its pillars will be crushed; all who work for wages will be grieved in soul.
native_verses.19:11: The officials of Zoan are sheer fools; the wisest of Pharaoh's counselors give senseless counsel. How can you say to Pharaoh, "I am a son of the wise, a son of kings of old"?
native_verses.19:12: Where, then, are your wise men? Let them tell you now, and let them know what the LORD of hosts has planned against Egypt.
native_verses.19:13: The officials of Zoan have become fools; the officials of Memphis are deceived; the cornerstones of its tribes have led Egypt astray.
native_verses.19:14: The LORD has mixed a spirit of bewilderment within it, and they have caused Egypt to reel in all its work, like a drunkard reeling in his vomit.
native_verses.19:15: And there will be no work for Egypt that head or tail, palm branch or reed can do.
native_verses.19:16: In that day Egypt will be like women, and it will tremble and be terrified before the brandishing of the hand of the LORD of hosts that He brandishes against it.
native_verses.19:17: And the land of Judah will become a terror to Egypt; everyone to whom it is mentioned will be terrified, because of the plan of the LORD of hosts that He is planning against it.
native_verses.19:18: In that day there will be five cities in the land of Egypt speaking the language of Canaan and swearing loyalty to the LORD of hosts; one will be called City of Destruction.
native_verses.19:19: In that day there will be an altar to the LORD in the middle of the land of Egypt, and a pillar beside its border to the LORD.
native_verses.19:20: It will be a sign and a witness to the LORD of hosts in the land of Egypt. When they cry out to the LORD because of oppressors, He will send them a savior and a champion, and will rescue them.
native_verses.19:21: And the LORD will make Himself known to Egypt, and the Egyptians will know the LORD in that day; they will worship with sacrifice and offering, and they will make a vow to the LORD and fulfill it.
native_verses.19:22: And the LORD will strike Egypt, striking and healing; they will return to the LORD, and He will respond to their plea and heal them.
native_verses.19:23: In that day there will be a highway from Egypt to Assyria; Assyria will come into Egypt and Egypt into Assyria, and the Egyptians will worship with the Assyrians.
native_verses.19:24: In that day Israel will be a third alongside Egypt and Assyria, a blessing in the midst of the earth,
native_verses.19:25: whom the LORD of hosts has blessed, saying, "Blessed be My people Egypt, and the work of My hands, Assyria, and My inheritance, Israel."
native_verses.20:1: In the year that the chief commander came to Ashdod, when Sargon king of Assyria sent him, he fought against Ashdod and captured it.
native_verses.20:2: At that time the LORD spoke through Isaiah son of Amoz, saying, "Go and untie the sackcloth from your waist, and remove your sandals from your feet." And he did so, walking naked and barefoot.
native_verses.20:3: Then the LORD said, "Just as My servant Isaiah has walked naked and barefoot for three years as a sign and a portent against Egypt and against Cush,
native_verses.20:4: so the king of Assyria will drive away the captives of Egypt and the exiles of Cush, young and old, naked and barefoot, with bared buttocks, Egypt's nakedness.
native_verses.20:5: And they will be dismayed and put to shame because of Cush, their hope, and because of Egypt, their pride.
native_verses.20:6: And the inhabitants of this coastland will say in that day, 'Look, so it is with our hope, to which we fled for help to be rescued from the king of Assyria! And how can we ourselves escape?'"
native_verses.21:1: A pronouncement concerning the wilderness of the sea: Like stormwinds in the Negev sweeping by, it comes out of the wilderness, from a fearsome land.
native_verses.21:2: A severe vision has been declared to me: the betrayer betrays, and the devastator devastates. "Go up, Elam! Lay siege, Media! I have put an end to all her groaning."
native_verses.21:3: Therefore my loins are filled with writhing pain; pangs have gripped me like the pangs of a woman giving birth. I am doubled over, unable to hear; I am dismayed, unable to see.
native_verses.21:4: My heart reels; shuddering has terrified me. He has turned the twilight of my desire into trembling for me.
native_verses.21:5: Set the table, spread the rugs, eat, drink! Rise up, commanders, oil the shield!
native_verses.21:6: For the Lord spoke to me in this way: "Go, station the lookout; whatever he sees, let him declare.
native_verses.21:7: When he sees chariotry, a pair of horsemen, riders on donkeys, riders on camels, let him listen intently, with utmost attentiveness."
native_verses.21:8: Then he cried out like a lion, "On the watchtower, Lord, I stand continually by day, and at my guard post I am stationed all the nights.
native_verses.21:9: And look, here comes a chariot of men, a pair of horsemen!" Then he answered and said, "Babylon has fallen, has fallen! And all the carved images of her gods He has smashed to the ground."
native_verses.21:10: My threshed one and son of my threshing floor, what I have heard from the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, I have declared to you.
native_verses.21:11: A pronouncement concerning Dumah: Someone is calling to me from Seir, "Watchman, what is left of the night? Watchman, what is left of the night?"
native_verses.21:12: The watchman said, "Morning has come, and night as well. If you wish to inquire, inquire; return, come!"
native_verses.21:13: A pronouncement concerning Arabia: In the thicket in Arabia you will spend the night, caravans of Dedanites.
native_verses.21:14: Bring water to meet the thirsty, inhabitants of the land of Tema; greet the fugitive with his bread.
native_verses.21:15: For they have fled from swords, from the unsheathed sword, from the strung bow, and from the heaviness of battle.
native_verses.21:16: For this is what the Lord said to me: "Within one more year, like the years of a hired laborer, all the glory of Kedar will come to an end,
native_verses.21:17: and the remainder of the number of bows of the mighty men of the sons of Kedar will be few," for the LORD, the God of Israel, has spoken.
native_verses.22:1: A pronouncement concerning the valley of vision: What is wrong with you now, that you have all gone up to the rooftops,
native_verses.22:2: you who are full of clamor, noisy city, exultant town? Your fallen are not fallen by the sword, nor dead in battle.
native_verses.22:3: All your commanders have fled together; without a bow they were taken prisoner. All of your people who were found were taken prisoner together, though they had escaped to a distance.
native_verses.22:4: Therefore I said, "Look away from me; let me weep bitterly. Do not press to comfort me over the devastation of the daughter of my people."
native_verses.22:5: For the Lord GOD of hosts has a day of turmoil and trampling and perplexity in the valley of vision, a tearing down of the wall and a cry for help to the mountain.
native_verses.22:6: Elam took up the quiver, with chariots of men and horsemen, and Kir uncovered the shield.
native_verses.22:7: Your finest valleys became filled with chariots, and the horsemen firmly stationed themselves at the gate.
native_verses.22:8: He stripped away the covering of Judah, and on that day you looked to the weaponry of the House of the Forest.
native_verses.22:9: And you saw that the breaches of the city of David were numerous, and you gathered the waters of the lower pool.
native_verses.22:10: And you numbered the houses of Jerusalem, and you demolished the houses to fortify the wall.
native_verses.22:11: You also made a reservoir between the two walls for the waters of the old pool; yet you did not look to Him who made it, nor did you see Him who fashioned it long ago.
native_verses.22:12: On that day the Lord GOD of hosts called for weeping and lamentation, for baldness and for binding on sackcloth.
native_verses.22:13: Yet look, jubilation and gladness, killing cattle and slaughtering sheep, eating meat and drinking wine: "Eat and drink, for tomorrow we die!"
native_verses.22:14: And the LORD of hosts revealed Himself in my ears: "This iniquity will certainly not be atoned for you until you die," said the Lord GOD of hosts.
native_verses.22:15: This is what the Lord GOD of hosts says: "Go, approach this steward, to Shebna, who is over the household:
native_verses.22:16: 'What do you have here, and whom do you have here, that you have hewn out a tomb for yourself here, hewing out his tomb on high, chiseling a dwelling for himself in the rock?
native_verses.22:17: Look, the LORD is about to hurl you violently away, strong man, and He will wrap you up completely.
native_verses.22:18: He will surely wind you up tightly like a ball into a broad land. There you will die, and there will be the chariots of your glory, you disgrace of the house of your master.
native_verses.22:19: And I will push you out of your post, and from your station He will pull you down.
native_verses.22:20: And it will happen on that day that I will call for My servant Eliakim, the son of Hilkiah,
native_verses.22:21: and I will dress him in your tunic, and fasten your sash securely on him, and put your authority into his hand; and he will be a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem and to the house of Judah.
native_verses.22:22: And I will put the key of the house of David on his shoulder; he will open, and no one will close; he will close, and no one will open.
native_verses.22:23: I will drive him as a peg into a secure place, and he will become a throne of glory for the house of his father.
native_verses.22:24: And they will hang upon him all the glory of the house of his father, the offspring and the offshoots, every small vessel, from the bowls all the way to all the jars.'"
native_verses.22:25: "On that day," declares the LORD of hosts, "the peg driven into a secure place will come loose; it will be sheared off and fall, and the load that was on it will be cut off," for the LORD has spoken.
native_verses.23:1: A pronouncement concerning Tyre: Wail, ships of Tarshish, for it has been devastated, with no house and no entry! From the land of Kittim it has been revealed to them.
native_verses.23:2: Be silent, inhabitants of the coastland, whom the merchants of Sidon, crossing the sea, have filled.
native_verses.23:3: And across many waters the grain of Shihor, the harvest of the Nile, was her revenue; and she became the marketplace of nations.
native_verses.23:4: Be ashamed, Sidon, for the sea has spoken, the stronghold of the sea, saying, "I have not been in labor, and I have not given birth; I have not raised young men, nor reared virgins."
native_verses.23:5: When the news comes to Egypt, they will writhe in anguish at the news of Tyre.
native_verses.23:6: Cross over to Tarshish! Wail, inhabitants of the coastland!
native_verses.23:7: Is this your exultant one, whose antiquity is from ancient days, whose feet used to carry her far off to sojourn?
native_verses.23:8: Who has purposed this against Tyre, who bestows crowns, whose merchants are princes, whose traders are the esteemed of the earth?
native_verses.23:9: The LORD of hosts has purposed it, to profane the pride of all splendor, to bring into contempt all the esteemed of the earth.
native_verses.23:10: Overflow your land like the Nile, daughter of Tarshish; there is no longer any restraint.
native_verses.23:11: He has stretched out His hand over the sea; He has caused kingdoms to tremble. The LORD has commanded concerning Canaan to destroy her strongholds.
native_verses.23:12: And He said, "You will exult no longer, oppressed virgin daughter of Sidon. Rise up, cross over to Kittim; even there you will have no rest."
native_verses.23:13: Look at the land of the Chaldeans! This is the people that is no more; Assyria appointed her for desert creatures. They raised up their siege towers, stripped bare her citadels; it made her a ruin.
native_verses.23:14: Wail, ships of Tarshish, for your stronghold has been devastated.
native_verses.23:15: And it will come about on that day that Tyre will be forgotten for seventy years, like the days of one king. At the end of seventy years, it will be with Tyre as in the song of the prostitute:
native_verses.23:16: "Take a lyre, walk around the city, forgotten prostitute! Play skillfully, sing many songs, so that you may be remembered."
native_verses.23:17: And it will come about at the end of seventy years that the LORD will visit Tyre, and she will return to her hire and prostitute herself with all the kingdoms of the earth upon the face of the ground.
native_verses.23:18: Yet her merchandise and her hire will be holy to the LORD; it will not be stored up nor hoarded, for her merchandise will belong to those who dwell before the LORD, for eating to satisfaction and for stately clothing.
native_verses.24:1: Look, the LORD is emptying the earth and stripping it bare; He warps its surface and disperses its inhabitants.
native_verses.24:2: And it will be: like the people, so the priest; like the servant, so his master; like the female servant, so her mistress; like the buyer, so the seller; like the lender, so the borrower; like the creditor, so the one who owes him.
native_verses.24:3: The earth will be entirely emptied and entirely plundered, because the LORD has spoken this word.
native_verses.24:4: The earth mourns and fades; the world languishes and fades; the lofty ones of the people of the earth languish.
native_verses.24:5: And the earth is defiled beneath its inhabitants, because they have transgressed laws, altered the statute, and broken the eternal covenant.
native_verses.24:6: Therefore a curse devours the earth, and those who dwell in it bear guilt; therefore the inhabitants of the earth are scorched, and few mortals remain.
native_verses.24:7: The new wine mourns, the vine languishes, and all who are glad of heart groan.
native_verses.24:8: The joy of tambourines has ceased, the clamor of the revelers has ended, the joy of the lyre has ceased.
native_verses.24:9: With singing they do not drink wine; strong drink turns bitter to those who drink it.
native_verses.24:10: The city of chaos is shattered; every house is shut up so that no one may come in.
native_verses.24:11: An outcry for wine is in the streets; all gladness has darkened; the joy of the earth has gone into exile.
native_verses.24:12: Desolation remains in the city, and the gate is smashed into ruin.
native_verses.24:13: For so it will be in the midst of the earth, among the peoples: like the beating of an olive tree, like the gleanings when the grape harvest has ended.
native_verses.24:14: They lift up their voice; they sing for joy; over the majesty of the LORD they cry out from the sea.
native_verses.24:15: Therefore in the east honor the LORD; in the coastlands of the sea, the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
native_verses.24:16: From the edge of the earth we have heard songs: "Splendor to the Righteous One!" But I said, "I am wasting away! I am wasting away! Woe to me! The treacherous have acted treacherously; with treachery the treacherous have acted treacherously."
native_verses.24:17: Terror, pit, and snare are upon you, inhabitant of the earth!
native_verses.24:18: And it will happen that whoever flees from the sound of the terror will fall into the pit, and whoever climbs up from the midst of the pit will be caught in the snare; for the windows from on high are opened, and the foundations of the earth quake.
native_verses.24:19: The earth is completely shattered; the earth is thoroughly split apart; the earth totters violently.
native_verses.24:20: The earth staggers wildly like a drunkard and sways to and fro like a shelter; its transgression weighs heavily upon it, and it falls and will not rise again.
native_verses.24:21: And it will come about on that day that the LORD will punish the host of the height on high, and the kings of the earth on the earth.
native_verses.24:22: They will be gathered together as prisoners into a pit, and they will be shut away in prison; after many days they will be punished.
native_verses.24:23: Then the moon will be abashed and the sun put to shame, because the LORD of hosts reigns on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, and before His elders there will be glory.
native_verses.25:1: LORD, You are my God; I will exalt You and give thanks to Your name, because You have done marvelous deeds, plans from long ago, in faithfulness and sureness.
native_verses.25:2: For You have turned a city into a heap, a fortified town into a ruin; the citadel of foreigners is no longer a city, and forever it will not be rebuilt.
native_verses.25:3: Therefore a strong people will honor You; the city of ruthless nations will fear You.
native_verses.25:4: For You have been a fortress for the poor, a fortress for the needy in his distress, a refuge from the rainstorm, and shade from the heat; for the blast of the ruthless is like a rainstorm against a wall.
native_verses.25:5: Like heat in a parched land, You subdue the clamor of foreigners; as heat by the shade of a cloud, the song of the ruthless is brought low.
native_verses.25:6: And the LORD of hosts will prepare for all the peoples on this mountain a banquet of rich fare, a banquet of aged wine: rich fare full of marrow, aged wine thoroughly refined.
native_verses.25:7: And He will swallow up on this mountain the surface of the shroud that enshrouds all the peoples, and the veil that is spread over all the nations.
native_verses.25:8: He will swallow up death forever, and the Lord GOD will wipe tears from every face; and the reproach of His people He will remove from the entire earth, because the LORD has spoken.
native_verses.25:9: And it will be said on that day, "Look, this is our God; we waited for Him so that He would save us. This is the LORD; we waited for Him; let us exult and be glad in His salvation!"
native_verses.25:10: For the hand of the LORD will rest on this mountain, while Moab will be trampled down in his own place, just as straw is trampled down in a dung pit.
native_verses.25:11: And he will spread out his hands inside it just as a swimmer spreads out his hands to swim, but He will bring down his pride along with the craftiness of his hands.
native_verses.25:12: And the lofty fortification of your walls He will humble, bring low, and bring down to the ground, to the very dust.
native_verses.26:1: On that day this song will be sung in the land of Judah: "We have a strong city; He appoints salvation as walls and a rampart.
native_verses.26:2: Open the gates so that a righteous nation may enter, one that keeps faithfulness.
native_verses.26:3: You will guard a steadfast mind in complete peace, because it trusts in You.
native_verses.26:4: Trust in the LORD forever and ever, because the LORD, the LORD, is an eternal Rock.
native_verses.26:5: For He has humbled those who dwell on high, the exalted city; He brings it low, He brings it low to the ground; He brings it down to the dust.
native_verses.26:6: The foot tramples it down, the feet of the afflicted, the footsteps of the poor."
native_verses.26:7: The way of the righteous is level; Upright One, You make even the course of the righteous.
native_verses.26:8: Yes, in the way of Your judgments, LORD, we have waited for You; the longing of the soul is for Your name and for Your remembrance.
native_verses.26:9: With my soul I long for You in the night; yes, with my spirit within me I seek You eagerly; for when Your judgments are on the earth, those who dwell in the world learn righteousness.
native_verses.26:10: Even if grace is shown to a wicked person, he does not learn righteousness; in a land of uprightness he commits injustice and does not see the majesty of the LORD.
native_verses.26:11: LORD, Your hand is raised high, yet they do not see it. Let them see Your zeal for the people and be put to shame; indeed, let the fire for Your adversaries devour them.
native_verses.26:12: LORD, You will ordain peace for us, because You have also accomplished all our deeds for us.
native_verses.26:13: LORD our God, masters besides You have ruled over us, yet by You alone we call Your name to remembrance.
native_verses.26:14: Dead, they will not live; departed spirits, they will not rise; therefore You have punished them and destroyed them, and blotted out every remembrance of them.
native_verses.26:15: You have increased the nation, LORD, You have increased the nation; You have shown Yourself glorious; You have pushed far out all the boundaries of the land.
native_verses.26:16: LORD, in distress they sought You out; they poured out a whisper when Your chastening was on them.
native_verses.26:17: As a pregnant woman nears the time to give birth, writhing and crying out in her labor pangs, so have we been in Your presence, LORD.
native_verses.26:18: We conceived, we writhed in labor, and it was as if we gave birth to wind; we have not achieved deliverance for the earth, nor have those who dwell in the world fallen.
native_verses.26:19: Your dead will live; my corpses will rise! Awake and ring out in joy, you who dwell in the dust! For Your dew is a dew of lights, and the earth will bring forth the departed spirits.
native_verses.26:20: Go, my people, enter your inner rooms and shut your door behind you; hide yourself for a brief moment until indignation passes by.
native_verses.26:21: For look, the LORD is coming out from His place to punish the inhabitant of the earth for his iniquity; and the earth will uncover its bloodshed and will no longer cover over those killed upon it.
native_verses.27:1: On that day the LORD, with His severe, great, and strong sword, will punish Leviathan the fleeing serpent and Leviathan the coiled serpent, and He will kill the dragon that is in the sea.
native_verses.27:2: On that day: A vineyard of wine! Sing about it:
native_verses.27:3: "I, the LORD, am its keeper; moment by moment I water it. So that no one harms it, night and day I guard it.
native_verses.27:4: There is no wrath in Me. If only briers and thorns faced Me in battle! I would stride against them; I would set them ablaze altogether.
native_verses.27:5: Or else let him take hold of My stronghold; let him make peace with Me, let him make peace with Me."
native_verses.27:6: In the days to come Jacob will take root; Israel will blossom and bud, and they will fill the face of the world with fruit.
native_verses.27:7: Has He struck him like the striking of his striker? Or has he been killed like the slaughter of those killed by Him?
native_verses.27:8: Measure by measure, by sending her away, You contended with her; He removed her with His severe wind on the day of the east wind.
native_verses.27:9: Therefore, by this Jacob's iniquity will be atoned for, and this is all the fruit of taking away his sin: when he makes all the altar stones like shattered chalkstones, Asherah poles and incense altars will not stand.
native_verses.27:10: For the fortified city is solitary, a dwelling place deserted and forsaken like the wilderness; there a calf grazes, and there it lies down and consumes its branches.
native_verses.27:11: When its boughs grow dry, they are broken off; women come and kindle fires with them. For they are not a people of understanding; therefore their Maker will not have compassion on them, and the One who formed them will not be gracious to them.
native_verses.27:12: And it will happen on that day that the LORD will thresh from the channel of the River to the Brook of Egypt, and you will be gleaned one by one, sons of Israel.
native_verses.27:13: And it will happen on that day that a great ram's horn will be sounded, and those who were perishing in the land of Assyria and the outcasts in the land of Egypt will come, and they will bow down to the LORD on the holy mountain in Jerusalem.
native_verses.28:1: Woe to the crown of pride of the drunkards of Ephraim, and to the fading flower, the beauty of its splendor, which is at the head of the rich valley of those overcome with wine!
native_verses.28:2: Look, the Lord has a strong and mighty one; like a downpour of hail, a storm of destruction, like a downpour of massive sweeping waters, he casts it down to the ground by hand.
native_verses.28:3: Underfoot it will be trampled, the crown of pride of the drunkards of Ephraim.
native_verses.28:4: And the fading flower, the beauty of its splendor, which is at the head of the rich valley, will be like a first-ripe fig before summer, which the observer sees, and while it is still in his palm he swallows it.
native_verses.28:5: On that day the LORD of hosts will be a crown of beauty and a diadem of splendor for the remnant of His people,
native_verses.28:6: and a spirit of justice for the one who sits in judgment, and strength for those who turn back the battle to the gate.
native_verses.28:7: And these also reel with wine and stagger with strong drink: priest and prophet reel with strong drink, they are swallowed up by wine, they stagger from strong drink; they reel in vision, they stumble in judgment.
native_verses.28:8: For all tables are full of vomit and filth; there is no space left.
native_verses.28:9: "To whom will he teach knowledge, and to whom will he explain the message? Those weaned from milk, those taken away from the breasts?
native_verses.28:10: For it is command after command, command after command, line after line, line after line, a little there, a little there."
native_verses.28:11: For with stammering speech and with another tongue He will speak to this people,
native_verses.28:12: to whom He said, "This is the place of rest; give rest to the weary, and this is repose," yet they were unwilling to listen.
native_verses.28:13: So the word of the LORD will become to them, "Command after command, command after command, line after line, line after line, a little there, a little there," so that they may go and stumble backward, and be broken, ensnared, and captured.
native_verses.28:14: Therefore, hear the word of the LORD, men of scoffing, rulers of this people who are in Jerusalem.
native_verses.28:15: For you have said, "We have made a covenant with death, and with Sheol we have made an agreement; when the sweeping scourge passes through, it will not reach us, for we have made falsehood our refuge, and in deceit we have hidden ourselves."
native_verses.28:16: Therefore, this is what the Lord GOD says: "Look, I have laid a stone in Zion, a proven stone, a precious cornerstone, a firmly laid foundation: the one who trusts will not act in haste.
native_verses.28:17: And I will make justice the measuring line and righteousness the plumb line; hail will sweep away the refuge of falsehood, and waters will overflow the hiding place.
native_verses.28:18: Then your covenant with death will be annulled, and your agreement with Sheol will not stand; when the sweeping scourge passes through, you will be trampled down by it.
native_verses.28:19: As often as it passes through, it will seize you; for morning after morning it will pass through, by day and by night, and it will be nothing but terror to understand the message.
native_verses.28:20: For the bed is too short to stretch out on, and the covering is too narrow when one wraps up in it."
native_verses.28:21: For the LORD will rise up as on Mount Perazim; He will rage as in the valley at Gibeon, to do His deed—strange is His deed—and to perform His work—alien is His work.
native_verses.28:22: And now, do not scoff, or your bonds will grow stronger; for I have heard of a complete and decreed destruction from the Lord GOD of hosts upon the whole earth.
native_verses.28:23: Give ear and hear my voice; pay attention and hear my speech.
native_verses.28:24: Does the plowman plow all day long to sow, opening and harrowing his ground?
native_verses.28:25: When he has leveled its surface, does he not scatter black cumin and broadcast cumin, and plant wheat in rows, barley in its marked-off place, and spelt along its border?
native_verses.28:26: For He instructs him in the proper way; his God teaches him.
native_verses.28:27: For black cumin is not threshed with a threshing sledge, nor is a cartwheel rolled over cumin; rather, black cumin is beaten out with a stick, and cumin with a rod.
native_verses.28:28: Is bread grain crushed? Indeed, he does not keep threshing it forever; when he drives the wheel of his cart and his horses, he does not crush it.
native_verses.28:29: This also comes from the LORD of hosts; He makes counsel wonderful and makes sound wisdom great.
native_verses.29:1: Woe to Ariel, Ariel, the city where David encamped! Add year to year; let the festivals complete their cycle.
native_verses.29:2: Yet I will bring distress to Ariel, and there will be moaning and mourning, and she will be to Me like Ariel.
native_verses.29:3: And I will encamp in a circle against you, and I will besiege you with a garrison, and I will raise up siegeworks against you.
native_verses.29:4: Then you will be brought low; from the ground you will speak, and from the dust your utterance will sink low. Your voice will be like a ghost from the ground, and from the dust your utterance will whisper.
native_verses.29:5: Yet the throng of your foreign foes will become like fine dust, and the throng of the ruthless like passing chaff; and it will happen in an instant, suddenly.
native_verses.29:6: By the LORD of hosts she will be visited, with thunder and earthquake and great noise, whirlwind and tempest, and flame of devouring fire.
native_verses.29:7: And the throng of all the nations that wage war against Ariel—all who wage war against her and her stronghold, and those who distress her—will be like a dream, a vision of the night.
native_verses.29:8: And it will be just as when a hungry man dreams, and look, he is eating, but he wakes up and his soul is empty; and as when a thirsty man dreams, and look, he is drinking, but he wakes up, and look, he is faint and his soul is craving—so will be the throng of all the nations that wage war against Mount Zion.
native_verses.29:9: Delay and be astounded; blind yourselves and be blind! They are drunk, but not with wine; they stagger, but not with strong drink.
native_verses.29:10: For the LORD has poured out upon you a spirit of deep sleep; He has tightly closed your eyes—the prophets—and covered your heads—the seers.
native_verses.29:11: And the vision of all this has become to you like the words of a sealed scroll, which they give to one who knows how to read, saying, "Please read this," and he says, "I cannot, for it is sealed."
native_verses.29:12: Then the scroll is given to one who does not know how to read, saying, "Please read this," and he says, "I do not know how to read."
native_verses.29:13: And the Lord said, "Because this people draws near—with their mouth and with their lips they honor Me—yet they have kept their heart far from Me, and their fear of Me has become a taught commandment of men,
native_verses.29:14: therefore, look, I will once more deal wondrously with this people, wondrously and with wonder; and the wisdom of their wise men will perish, and the discernment of their discerning men will conceal itself."
native_verses.29:15: Woe to those who go deep to hide a plan from the LORD, and their deeds are in a dark place, and they say, "Who sees us, and who knows us?"
native_verses.29:16: What perversity of yours! Shall the potter be reckoned like clay, so that what is made would say of its maker, "He did not make me," or what is formed say of the one who formed it, "He does not understand"?
native_verses.29:17: Is it not yet a very little while before Lebanon will turn into an orchard, and the orchard will be reckoned as a forest?
native_verses.29:18: On that day the deaf will hear the words of a scroll, and out of gloom and darkness the eyes of the blind will see.
native_verses.29:19: The humble will increase joy in the LORD, and the needy among mankind will exult in the Holy One of Israel.
native_verses.29:20: For the ruthless one will be no more, and the scoffer will come to an end, and all who keep watch for iniquity will be cut off—
native_verses.29:21: those who make a person guilty by a word, and lay a snare for the one who reproves at the gate, and turn aside the righteous with emptiness.
native_verses.29:22: Therefore, this is what the LORD, who redeemed Abraham, says to the house of Jacob: "Jacob will not now be ashamed, nor will his face now grow pale.
native_verses.29:23: For when he sees his children, the work of My hands, in his midst, they will sanctify My name; they will sanctify the Holy One of Jacob and stand in awe of the God of Israel.
native_verses.29:24: And those who stray in spirit will know understanding, and those who grumble will learn instruction."
native_verses.30:1: "Woe to rebellious sons," declares the LORD, "who form a plan, yet not from Me, and seal an alliance, yet not by My Spirit, in order to add sin upon sin;
native_verses.30:2: who set out to go down to Egypt without inquiring of My mouth, to seek shelter in Pharaoh's stronghold and to take refuge in the shadow of Egypt.
native_verses.30:3: So Pharaoh's stronghold will become shame for you, and the refuge in Egypt's shadow, disgrace.
native_verses.30:4: For his officials are at Zoan, and his messengers reach Hanes.
native_verses.30:5: Everyone comes to shame because of a people who cannot profit them, bringing neither help nor profit, but shame and also reproach."
native_verses.30:6: A pronouncement concerning the beasts of the Negev: Through a land of distress and anguish, from which come the lioness and the lion, the viper and the flying fiery serpent, they carry their wealth on the shoulders of young donkeys and their treasures on the humps of camels to a people who cannot profit them.
native_verses.30:7: Indeed, Egypt helps in futility and emptiness; therefore I have called this one, "Rahab: they sit idle."
native_verses.30:8: Now go, write it on a tablet before them and inscribe it on a scroll, so that it may remain for a future day, forever and ever.
native_verses.30:9: For this is a rebellious people, deceitful sons, sons unwilling to listen to the instruction of the LORD,
native_verses.30:10: who say to the seers, "Do not see," and to the visionaries, "Do not envision right things for us; speak smooth things to us, envision illusions;
native_verses.30:11: turn aside from the way, veer off from the path; remove the Holy One of Israel from before us."
native_verses.30:12: Therefore, this is what the Holy One of Israel says: "Because you have rejected this word and trusted in oppression and crookedness and leaned upon it,
native_verses.30:13: therefore this iniquity will be to you like a breach ready to fall, bulging out in a lofty wall, whose collapse comes suddenly, in an instant,
native_verses.30:14: and it will be shattered like the shattering of a potter's jar, crushed without sparing, so that among its crushed pieces no shard will be found to scoop fire from a hearth or to dip water from a cistern."
native_verses.30:15: For this is what the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel, says: "By returning and rest you will be saved; in calm and in confidence your strength will be." Yet you were unwilling,
native_verses.30:16: and you said, "No, rather on horses we will flee"—therefore you will flee!—"and on swift steeds we will ride"—therefore those who pursue you will be swift!
native_verses.30:17: One thousand will flee at the threat of one; at the threat of five you will flee, until you are left like a flagpole on the summit of a mountain and like a banner on a hill.
native_verses.30:18: Therefore the LORD waits to show you grace, and therefore He rises on high to have compassion on you. For the LORD is a God of justice; blessed are all who wait for Him.
native_verses.30:19: For a people will dwell in Zion, in Jerusalem; you will surely weep no more. He will certainly show you grace at the sound of your outcry; the moment He hears it, He will answer you.
native_verses.30:20: And though the Lord gives you bread of distress and water of oppression, your Teacher will no longer hide Himself, and your eyes will continually see your Teacher.
native_verses.30:21: And your ears will hear a word behind you, saying, "This is the way; walk in it," whenever you turn to the right or turn to the left.
native_verses.30:22: And you will defile the plating of your silver carved images and the sheathing of your gold cast image. You will scatter them like a menstrual cloth; "Get out!" you will say to it.
native_verses.30:23: Then He will give rain for your seed with which you sow the ground, and bread from the produce of the ground, and it will be rich and plentiful. In that day your livestock will graze in a broad pasture.
native_verses.30:24: And the oxen and the young donkeys that work the ground will eat seasoned fodder that has been winnowed with shovel and winnowing fork.
native_verses.30:25: And on every high mountain and on every elevated hill there will be streams and channels of water, on the day of great slaughter, when towers fall.
native_verses.30:26: And the light of the moon will be like the light of the sun, and the light of the sun will be sevenfold, like the light of seven days, on the day the LORD binds up the fracture of His people and heals the bruise of their wound.
native_verses.30:27: Look, the name of the LORD comes from afar, His anger burning, with heavy rising smoke; His lips are filled with indignation, and His tongue is like a devouring fire.
native_verses.30:28: And His breath is like a surging torrent reaching up to the neck, to sift nations in a sieve of ruin, with a bridle that leads astray upon the jaws of the peoples.
native_verses.30:29: You will have a song as on the night a festival is consecrated, and gladness of heart like one who walks with a flute to come to the mountain of the LORD, to the Rock of Israel.
native_verses.30:30: And the LORD will make the majesty of His voice heard and will show the descent of His arm in furious anger and a flame of devouring fire, with cloudburst, downpour, and hailstones.
native_verses.30:31: For at the voice of the LORD Assyria will be terror-stricken; with the rod He will strike.
native_verses.30:32: And every stroke of the appointed staff that the LORD brings down upon him will be with tambourines and lyres; and in battles of brandishing He will fight against them.
native_verses.30:33: For Topheth has been set in order from long ago; indeed, it has been prepared for the king. He has made it deep and wide; its pyre has fire and wood in abundance. The breath of the LORD, like a torrent of sulfur, sets it ablaze.
native_verses.31:1: Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help and lean upon horses, trusting in chariots because they are numerous and in horsemen because they are exceedingly mighty, while they do not look to the Holy One of Israel and do not seek the LORD.
native_verses.31:2: Yet He too is wise and brings disaster, and He does not retract His words; He will rise up against the house of evildoers and against the help of those who practice iniquity.
native_verses.31:3: And the Egyptians are human and not God, and their horses are flesh and not spirit. When the LORD stretches out His hand, the one who helps will stumble and the one who is helped will fall, and all of them together will perish.
native_verses.31:4: For this is what the LORD has said to me: "Just as the lion, even the young lion, growls over its prey when a full band of shepherds is summoned against it—it is not dismayed at their voice nor humbled by their uproar—so the LORD of hosts will come down to wage war upon Mount Zion and upon its hill.
native_verses.31:5: Like hovering birds, so the LORD of hosts will shield Jerusalem; shielding it, He will also deliver it; passing over it, He will also rescue it."
native_verses.31:6: Return to Him from whom the sons of Israel have deeply revolted.
native_verses.31:7: For in that day each one will reject his idols of silver and his idols of gold, which your own hands have made for you as a sin.
native_verses.31:8: And Assyria will fall by a sword not of a man, and a sword not of a mortal will devour him; he will flee from the sword, and his young men will become forced laborers.
native_verses.31:9: And his rock will pass away in terror, and his officials will be terrified at the standard, declares the LORD, whose fire is in Zion and whose furnace is in Jerusalem.
native_verses.32:1: See, a king will reign according to righteousness, and officials will rule according to justice.
native_verses.32:2: And a man will be like a refuge from the wind and a shelter from a downpour, like channels of water in a dry place, like the shade of a massive crag in a weary land.
native_verses.32:3: Then the eyes of those who see will not be shut, and the ears of those who hear will pay close attention.
native_verses.32:4: And the heart of the hasty will understand knowledge, and the tongue of stammerers will hasten to speak plainly.
native_verses.32:5: No longer will a fool be called noble, nor a scoundrel be spoken of as honorable.
native_verses.32:6: For a fool speaks folly, and his heart works iniquity, to practice godlessness and to speak error against the LORD, to leave the appetite of the hungry empty and to withhold drink from the thirsty.
native_verses.32:7: As for a scoundrel, his devices are evil; he devises wicked plots to ruin the poor with words of falsehood, even when the needy speaks what is just.
native_verses.32:8: But a noble man devises noble things, and upon noble things he stands.
native_verses.32:9: Women at ease, rise up, listen to my voice; self-assured daughters, give ear to my speech!
native_verses.32:10: In a year and some days you will tremble, you self-assured ones; for the vintage is finished, and the harvest gathering will not arrive.
native_verses.32:11: Shudder, you women at ease; tremble, you self-assured ones! Strip off and bare yourselves, and wrap your waists!
native_verses.32:12: They beat their breasts in mourning for the pleasant fields, for the fruitful vine.
native_verses.32:13: Upon the soil of my people thorns and briers will grow up, yes, upon all the houses of joy in the jubilant city.
native_verses.32:14: For the palace has been abandoned, the throng of the city has been deserted; the citadel and watchtower have become caves forever, a joy for wild donkeys, a pasture for flocks,
native_verses.32:15: until a spirit is poured out on us from on high, and the wilderness turns into an orchard, and the orchard is reckoned as a forest.
native_verses.32:16: Then justice will dwell in the wilderness, and righteousness will abide in the orchard.
native_verses.32:17: And the work of righteousness will be peace, and the labor of righteousness will be calm and security forever.
native_verses.32:18: And my people will dwell in a home of peace, and in dwellings of security, and in tranquil resting places.
native_verses.32:19: Yet it will hail when the forest comes down, and in lowliness the city will be brought low.
native_verses.32:20: Blessed are you who sow by all waters, who send out the foot of the ox and the donkey.
native_verses.33:1: Woe, ravager, though you have not been ravaged, and treacherous one, though they have not acted treacherously against him! When you finish ravaging, you will be ravaged; when you cease acting treacherously, they will act treacherously against you.
native_verses.33:2: LORD, show grace to us; for You we have waited. Be their arm every morning, indeed our salvation in a time of distress.
native_verses.33:3: At the sound of uproar, peoples flee; at Your exaltation, nations scatter.
native_verses.33:4: And your spoil will be gathered like the gathering of the caterpillar; like the rushing of locusts, one rushes upon it.
native_verses.33:5: Exalted is the LORD, for He dwells in the height; He has filled Zion with justice and righteousness.
native_verses.33:6: And He will be the steadiness of your times, a store of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge; the fear of the LORD, that is his treasure.
native_verses.33:7: Look, their valiant ones cry aloud outside; the messengers of peace weep bitterly.
native_verses.33:8: The highways stand desolate; the wayfarer has ceased. He has violated the covenant, he has scorned cities, he regards no mortal.
native_verses.33:9: The land mourns and droops; Lebanon is disgraced and withers; Sharon has become like an arid plain, and Bashan and Carmel shake themselves bare.
native_verses.33:10: "Now I will rise," says the LORD, "now I will exalt Myself, now I will be lifted up.
native_verses.33:11: You conceive dry grass, you bear stubble; your breath is a fire that will devour you.
native_verses.33:12: And peoples will become burnings of lime, cut thorns that will burn in the fire.
native_verses.33:13: Hear, you who are distant, what I have done; and know, you who are near, My might!"
native_verses.33:14: Sinners in Zion are in dread; shuddering has gripped the godless: "Who of us can reside with a devouring fire? Who of us can reside with eternal burnings?"
native_verses.33:15: The one who walks in righteous deeds and speaks with uprightness, who scorns profit from oppressions, who shakes his hands away from grasping a bribe, who closes his ear against hearing of bloodshed, and shuts his eyes against looking at evil;
native_verses.33:16: he himself will dwell on the heights; strongholds of cliffs will be his high refuge; his bread is given, his water unfailing.
native_verses.33:17: Your eyes will gaze upon a king in his beauty; they will see a land of far distances.
native_verses.33:18: Your heart will ponder terror: "Where is the one who counted? Where is the one who weighed? Where is the one who counted the towers?"
native_verses.33:19: You will not see a fierce people, a people too deep in speech to understand, stammering in tongue with no comprehension.
native_verses.33:20: Gaze upon Zion, the city of our appointed festival! Your eyes will see Jerusalem, a tranquil dwelling, a tent that will not be moved; its stakes will never be pulled out, and none of its cords will be snapped.
native_verses.33:21: Instead, there the LORD will be majestic for us, a place of rivers and broad streams; no vessel with oars will travel on it, and no majestic ship will cross it.
native_verses.33:22: Because the LORD is our judge, the LORD is our lawmaker, the LORD is our king; He Himself will save us.
native_verses.33:23: Your cords hang slack; they cannot keep the base of their mast secure; they cannot spread a sail. Then abundant booty and spoil will be divided; the lame will plunder the loot.
native_verses.33:24: And no dweller will say, "I am ill"; the people living in it will have their iniquity forgiven.
native_verses.34:1: Come near, nations, to hear, and pay close attention, peoples! Let the earth hear, and its fullness, the world and everything that comes forth from it.
native_verses.34:2: For the LORD has wrath against all the nations, and fury against all their host; He has doomed them to destruction, He has given them to the slaughter.
native_verses.34:3: And their fallen will be thrown out, and from their corpses their stench will rise, and mountains will dissolve with their blood.
native_verses.34:4: And all the host of the heavens will decay, and the heavens will be rolled together like a scroll; and all their host will wither, like the withering of a leaf from a vine and like what withers from a fig tree.
native_verses.34:5: For My sword has been drenched in the heavens; look, it will descend upon Edom, and upon the people I have doomed to destruction, for judgment.
native_verses.34:6: The LORD has a sword, full of blood, made rich with fat, with the blood of lambs and male goats, with the fat of rams' kidneys; for the LORD holds a sacrifice in Bozrah, and a great slaughter in the land of Edom.
native_verses.34:7: And wild oxen will go down with them, and young bulls with mighty ones; their land will be drenched with blood, and their dust will be made rich with fat.
native_verses.34:8: For a day of vengeance belongs to the LORD, a year of retribution for Zion's cause.
native_verses.34:9: And its streams will be turned to pitch, and its dust to sulfur, and its land will become blazing pitch.
native_verses.34:10: Night and day it will not go out; forever its smoke will ascend. From generation to generation it will remain waste; for all eternity no one will pass through it.
native_verses.34:11: The desert owl and the hedgehog will possess it, and the great owl and the raven will dwell in it; and He will stretch out over it the measuring line of formlessness and the plumb stones of emptiness.
native_verses.34:12: As for its nobles, there is no one there to proclaim a kingdom, and all its officials will come to nothing.
native_verses.34:13: And thorns will spring up in its citadels, nettles and brambles in its fortresses; it will become a lair of jackals, an enclosure for ostriches.
native_verses.34:14: And desert beasts will meet with hyenas, and a wild goat will call to its companion; indeed, there the night creature will settle down and find a resting place for herself.
native_verses.34:15: There the arrow snake will make a nest and lay eggs, and hatch and brood in its shade; indeed, there the kites will be gathered, each with her companion.
native_verses.34:16: Search from the scroll of the LORD and read: not one of them will be missing; none will lack her companion. For it is My mouth that has commanded, and it is His Spirit who has gathered them.
native_verses.34:17: And He Himself has cast a lot for them, and His hand has apportioned it to them with the measuring line; forever they will possess it, from generation to generation they will dwell in it.
native_verses.35:1: The wilderness and the parched ground will be glad, and the arid plain will exult and bloom like a crocus.
native_verses.35:2: It will bloom richly and exult, yes, with exultation and ringing shouts. The glory of Lebanon is given to it, the splendor of Carmel and Sharon. They themselves will see the glory of the LORD, the splendor of our God.
native_verses.35:3: Strengthen drooping hands, and make stumbling knees firm.
native_verses.35:4: Say to those of agitated heart, "Be strong; do not be afraid! Look, your God will come with vengeance, with God's repayment; He Himself will come and save you."
native_verses.35:5: Then the eyes of the blind will open wide, and the ears of the deaf will be opened.
native_verses.35:6: Then the lame will bound like a deer, and the tongue of the mute will ring out with joy; for waters will burst out in the wilderness, and streams in the arid plain.
native_verses.35:7: And the mirage will turn into a pool, and the thirsty land into springs of water; in the lair of jackals, its resting place, grass will become reeds and papyrus.
native_verses.35:8: And a highway and a road will be there, and it will be called the Way of Holiness. No unclean person will pass over it, but it will be for them; whoever walks the way, even fools, will not stray.
native_verses.35:9: There will be no lion there, and no predatory beast will climb onto it; none will be found there, but the redeemed will walk on it.
native_verses.35:10: And those ransomed by the LORD will return and enter Zion with ringing shouts, with eternal joy upon their heads; gladness and joy they will attain, and grief and groaning will flee.
native_verses.36:1: And it happened in the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah that Sennacherib, king of Assyria, came up against all the fortified cities of Judah and captured them.
native_verses.36:2: Then the king of Assyria sent Rabshakeh from Lachish to Jerusalem, to King Hezekiah, with a large army. And he stood by the conduit of the upper pool, on the highway of the launderer's field.
native_verses.36:3: Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder, went out to him.
native_verses.36:4: And Rabshakeh said to them, "Say now to Hezekiah, 'This is what the great king, the king of Assyria, says: What is this confidence in which you have trusted?
native_verses.36:5: I say, counsel and strength for war are merely words of the lips. Now in whom have you trusted, that you have rebelled against me?
native_verses.36:6: Look, you have trusted in the staff of this crushed reed, in Egypt, on which if a man leans, it will go into his palm and pierce it. So is Pharaoh, king of Egypt, to all who trust in him.
native_verses.36:7: And if you say to me, "We have trusted in the LORD our God," is it not He whose high places and whose altars Hezekiah removed, and said to Judah and to Jerusalem, "Before this altar you shall worship"?
native_verses.36:8: Now then, make a wager with my master, the king of Assyria, and I will give you two thousand horses, if you are able on your part to put riders on them.
native_verses.36:9: How then could you turn back even a single governor among the least of my master's servants, while you trust in Egypt for chariots and for horsemen?
native_verses.36:10: And now, is it apart from the LORD that I have come up against this land to destroy it? The LORD said to me, "Go up against this land and destroy it."'"
native_verses.36:11: Then Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said to Rabshakeh, "Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, for we understand it; and do not speak to us in Judean in the hearing of the people who are on the wall."
native_verses.36:12: But Rabshakeh said, "Has my master sent me to your master and to you to speak these words? Was it not to the men sitting on the wall, who are to eat their own excrement and to drink the water of their feet with you?"
native_verses.36:13: Then Rabshakeh stood and called out with a loud voice in Judean and said, "Hear the words of the great king, the king of Assyria.
native_verses.36:14: This is what the king says: 'Do not let Hezekiah deceive you, for he will not be able to rescue you.
native_verses.36:15: And do not let Hezekiah make you trust in the LORD by saying, "The LORD will certainly rescue us; this city will not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria."'
native_verses.36:16: Do not listen to Hezekiah, for this is what the king of Assyria says: 'Make peace with me and come out to me, and eat, each one from his own vine and each one from his own fig tree, and drink, each one the water of his own cistern,
native_verses.36:17: until I come and take you away to a land like your own land, a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards.
native_verses.36:18: Beware that Hezekiah does not mislead you, saying, "The LORD will rescue us." Have the gods of the nations rescued each his own land from the hand of the king of Assyria?
native_verses.36:19: Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim? And have they rescued Samaria from my hand?
native_verses.36:20: Who among all the gods of these lands have rescued their land from my hand, that the LORD should rescue Jerusalem from my hand?'"
native_verses.36:21: But they kept silent and did not answer him a word, for the king's command was, "Do not answer him."
native_verses.36:22: Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder, came to Hezekiah with torn garments and reported to him the words of Rabshakeh.
native_verses.37:1: Now when King Hezekiah heard this, he tore his garments, covered himself with sackcloth, and entered the house of the LORD.
native_verses.37:2: And he sent Eliakim, who was over the household, Shebna the scribe, and the elders of the priests, covered with sackcloth, to Isaiah son of Amoz, the prophet.
native_verses.37:3: And they said to him, "This is what Hezekiah says: This day is a day of distress, rebuke, and contempt; for children have come to the point of birth, and there is no strength to give birth.
native_verses.37:4: Perhaps the LORD your God will hear the words of Rabshakeh, whom his master, the king of Assyria, has sent to revile the living God, and will rebuke the words that the LORD your God has heard. So lift up a prayer for the remnant that remains."
native_verses.37:5: So the servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah.
native_verses.37:6: And Isaiah said to them, "This is what you shall say to your master: 'This is what the LORD says: Do not be afraid because of the words that you have heard, with which the attendants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed Me.
native_verses.37:7: Look, I am putting a spirit in him, and he will hear a report and return to his own land; and I will make him fall by the sword in his own land.'"
native_verses.37:8: Then Rabshakeh returned and found the king of Assyria fighting against Libnah, for he had heard that he had departed from Lachish.
native_verses.37:9: Now he heard concerning Tirhakah, king of Cush, "He has come out to fight against you." When he heard it, he sent messengers to Hezekiah, saying,
native_verses.37:10: "This is what you shall say to Hezekiah, king of Judah: 'Do not let your God, in whom you trust, deceive you by saying, "Jerusalem will not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria."
native_verses.37:11: Look, you yourself have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the lands, destroying them completely. And will you be rescued?
native_verses.37:12: Did the gods of the nations that my fathers destroyed rescue them—Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the sons of Eden who were in Telassar?
native_verses.37:13: Where is the king of Hamath, the king of Arpad, and the king of the city of Sepharvaim, of Hena, and of Ivvah?'"
native_verses.37:14: Then Hezekiah took the letter from the hand of the messengers and read it; and he went up to the house of the LORD, and Hezekiah spread it out before the LORD.
native_verses.37:15: And Hezekiah prayed to the LORD, saying,
native_verses.37:16: "LORD of hosts, God of Israel, enthroned above the cherubim, You alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth; You made the heavens and the earth.
native_verses.37:17: Incline Your ear, LORD, and hear; open Your eyes, LORD, and see; and hear all the words of Sennacherib, which he has sent to revile the living God.
native_verses.37:18: Truly, LORD, the kings of Assyria have laid waste all the countries and their land,
native_verses.37:19: and have cast their gods into the fire, for they were not gods, but the work of human hands, wood and stone; so they destroyed them.
native_verses.37:20: And now, LORD our God, save us from his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that You alone are the LORD."
native_verses.37:21: Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent to Hezekiah, saying, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Because you have prayed to Me concerning Sennacherib, king of Assyria,
native_verses.37:22: this is the word that the LORD has spoken against him: The virgin daughter of Zion despises you, she mocks you; the daughter of Jerusalem shakes her head behind you.
native_verses.37:23: Whom have you reviled and blasphemed? Against whom have you raised your voice and lifted your eyes on high? Against the Holy One of Israel!
native_verses.37:24: By the hand of your servants you have reviled the Lord, and you have said, 'With my many chariots I have gone up to the height of the mountains, to the far recesses of Lebanon; I will cut down its tallest cedars, the choicest of its cypresses, and I will come to its farthest height, its lush forest.
native_verses.37:25: I dug wells and drank water, and with the sole of my feet I will dry up all the streams of Egypt.'
native_verses.37:26: Have you not heard? Long ago I did it; from days of old I formed it. Now I have brought it about, that you should turn fortified cities into heaps of ruins.
native_verses.37:27: And their inhabitants, of little strength, were dismayed and put to shame; they became plants of the field and tender green shoots, grass on the rooftops and a field before the standing grain.
native_verses.37:28: But I know your sitting down, your going out, and your coming in, and your raging against Me.
native_verses.37:29: Because of your raging against Me, and because your arrogance has come up into My ears, I will put My hook in your nose and My bridle in your lips, and I will turn you back along the way by which you came.
native_verses.37:30: And this shall be the sign for you: this year you shall eat what grows of itself, and in the second year what springs from that; and in the third year sow and reap, plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
native_verses.37:31: And the survivors of the house of Judah who remain will again take root downward and bear fruit upward.
native_verses.37:32: For out of Jerusalem a remnant will go forth, and survivors from Mount Zion. The zeal of the LORD of hosts will accomplish this.
native_verses.37:33: Therefore this is what the LORD says concerning the king of Assyria: He will not enter this city, nor shoot an arrow there, nor confront it with a shield, nor heap up a siege ramp against it.
native_verses.37:34: By the way that he came, he will return, and he will not enter this city, declares the LORD.
native_verses.37:35: And I will defend this city to save it, for My own sake and for the sake of My servant David."
native_verses.37:36: Then the angel of the LORD went out and struck down one hundred eighty-five thousand in the camp of Assyria; and when they rose early in the morning, look, all of them were dead bodies.
native_verses.37:37: So Sennacherib, king of Assyria, departed, went away, and returned, and he lived in Nineveh.
native_verses.37:38: And it happened as he was worshiping in the house of Nisroch his god that Adrammelech and Sharezer, his sons, struck him down with the sword, and they escaped to the land of Ararat. And Esarhaddon his son became king in his place.
native_verses.38:1: In those days Hezekiah became sick to the point of death, and Isaiah son of Amoz, the prophet, came to him and said to him, "This is what the LORD says: 'Give instructions for your household, for you are dying and will not live.'"
native_verses.38:2: Hezekiah turned his face toward the wall and prayed to the LORD.
native_verses.38:3: He said, "Please, LORD, remember now how I have walked before You in faithfulness and with a complete heart, and have done what is good in Your eyes." Then Hezekiah wept with great weeping.
native_verses.38:4: Now the word of the LORD came to Isaiah, saying,
native_verses.38:5: "Go and speak to Hezekiah: 'This is what the LORD, the God of David your father, says: I have heard your prayer; I have seen your tears. Look, I am adding fifteen years to your days.
native_verses.38:6: And from the grasp of the king of Assyria I will rescue you and this city, and I will shield this city.
native_verses.38:7: And this is the sign for you from the LORD that the LORD will carry out this matter that He has spoken:
native_verses.38:8: Look, I am making the shadow of the steps, which has gone down on the steps of Ahaz with the sun, go back ten steps.'" So the sun went back ten steps on the steps that it had gone down.
native_verses.38:9: A writing of Hezekiah, king of Judah, when he fell sick and recovered from his sickness:
native_verses.38:10: I said, "At the midpoint of my days I must pass through the gates of Sheol; I have been deprived of the remainder of my years."
native_verses.38:11: I said, "I will not see the LORD, the LORD in the land of the living; I will gaze on humanity no more among the dwellers of the fleeting world."
native_verses.38:12: My dwelling has been pulled up and carried away from me like a shepherd's tent; I have rolled up my life like a weaver; from the loom He severs me. From day until night You put an end to me.
native_verses.38:13: I calmed myself until morning; like a lion, so He shatters all my bones. From day until night You put an end to me.
native_verses.38:14: Like a swift or a crane, so I twitter; I moan like a dove. My eyes grow dim toward the height. Lord, distress is upon me; stand as my surety!
native_verses.38:15: What can I speak? He has spoken to me, and He Himself has acted. I will tread slowly all my years on account of the bitterness of my soul.
native_verses.38:16: Lord, by these things people live, and wholly in them is the life of my spirit; restore me to health and make me live!
native_verses.38:17: Look, it was for peace that bitterness upon bitterness came to me; yet You have lovingly kept my soul from the pit of nothingness, for You have thrown all my sins behind Your back.
native_verses.38:18: For Sheol does not give You thanks, nor does death praise You; those who descend to the pit do not hope for Your faithfulness.
native_verses.38:19: The living, the living, he is the one who gives You thanks, just as I do today; a father makes Your faithfulness known to children.
native_verses.38:20: The LORD is ready to save me; so we will play my stringed music all the days of our lives at the house of the LORD.
native_verses.38:21: And Isaiah said, "Let them take a cake of figs and rub it on the boil, so that he may recover."
native_verses.38:22: And Hezekiah said, "What sign is there that I will go up to the house of the LORD?"
native_verses.39:1: At that time Merodach-baladan son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a gift to Hezekiah, for he heard that he had fallen sick and had grown strong again.
native_verses.39:2: Hezekiah rejoiced over them and showed them his treasure house, the silver, the gold, the spices, and the fine oil, as well as his entire armory and everything found in his treasuries. There was not a thing in his house or in all his realm that Hezekiah did not show them.
native_verses.39:3: Then the prophet Isaiah came to King Hezekiah and said to him, "What did these men say, and where do they come from to you?" And Hezekiah said, "From a distant land they have come to me, from Babylon."
native_verses.39:4: He said, "What did they see in your house?" Hezekiah said, "Everything that is in my house they saw; there was not a thing in my treasuries that I did not show them."
native_verses.39:5: Isaiah then said to Hezekiah, "Listen to the word of the LORD of hosts:
native_verses.39:6: Look, days are coming when everything in your house and what your fathers have stored up until this day will be carried off to Babylon; nothing will remain, says the LORD.
native_verses.39:7: And some of your sons who come forth from you, whom you will father, will be taken, and they will become eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon."
native_verses.39:8: Then Hezekiah said to Isaiah, "Good is the word of the LORD that you have spoken." And he said, "For there will be peace and truth in my days."
native_verses.40:1: "Comfort, comfort My people," your God says.
native_verses.40:2: "Speak to the heart of Jerusalem and call out to her that her hard service has been fulfilled, that her iniquity has been paid off, that she has received from the hand of the LORD double for all her sins."
native_verses.40:3: A voice calls out: "In the wilderness clear the way of the LORD; level in the desert plain a highway for our God.
native_verses.40:4: Every valley will be raised up, and every mountain and hill will become low; the uneven ground will become a level plain, and the rugged ridges a broad valley.
native_verses.40:5: The glory of the LORD will be unveiled, and all flesh together will see it, because the mouth of the LORD has spoken."
native_verses.40:6: A voice says, "Call out!" And he said, "What shall I call out?" "All flesh is grass, and all its loyal love is like a blossom of the field.
native_verses.40:7: The grass dries up, the blossom wilts, when the breath of the LORD blows across it; indeed, the people are grass.
native_verses.40:8: The grass dries up, the blossom wilts, yet the word of our God stands forever."
native_verses.40:9: Go up onto a high mountain, Zion, messenger of good news; raise your voice with strength, Jerusalem, messenger of good news; raise it up, do not be afraid! Say to the cities of Judah, "Here is your God!"
native_verses.40:10: See, the Lord GOD is coming with strength, and His arm rules for Him; look, His reward is with Him, and His recompense is ahead of Him.
native_verses.40:11: Like a shepherd He tends His flock; with His arm He gathers the lambs and carries them against His chest; the nursing ewes He gently guides.
native_verses.40:12: Who has measured waters in His cupped hand, and gauged the heavens with a span, and held the dust of the earth in a measure, and weighed mountains with a balance and hills on scales?
native_verses.40:13: Who has gauged the Spirit of the LORD, or as His counselor instructed Him?
native_verses.40:14: Whom did He consult to give Him understanding, to teach Him in the path of justice, to teach Him knowledge, and to make known to Him the way of understanding?
native_verses.40:15: Look, the nations are like a drop from a bucket, and like fine dust on the scales they are reckoned; look, He lifts the coastlands like a speck of dust.
native_verses.40:16: Lebanon is not enough for burning, nor are its wild animals enough for a burnt offering.
native_verses.40:17: All the nations are like nothing in His presence; as less than nothing and emptiness they are reckoned by Him.
native_verses.40:18: To whom then will you liken God, and what likeness will you set alongside Him?
native_verses.40:19: As for an idol, a craftsman casts it, and a metalworker plates it with gold and casts chains of silver.
native_verses.40:20: The one too poor for an offering picks wood that will not decay; he searches for a skilled craftsman to set up an idol that will not topple.
native_verses.40:21: Do you not know? Do you not hear? Was it not declared to you from the beginning? Have you not understood the foundations of the earth?
native_verses.40:22: He is the One who sits enthroned above the circle of the earth, and its dwellers are like grasshoppers; who stretches out the heavens like a thin veil and spreads them like a tent to dwell in.
native_verses.40:23: He is the One who reduces princes to nothing, and makes the judges of the earth like emptiness.
native_verses.40:24: Barely have they been planted, barely have they been sown, barely has their stem taken root in the earth, when He blows upon them and they dry up, and a stormwind carries them away like stubble.
native_verses.40:25: "To whom then will you liken Me, that I might be equal?" says the Holy One.
native_verses.40:26: Raise your eyes to the height and see: who created these? He is the One who brings out their host by number; He calls all of them by name. Because of the abundance of His vigor, and because He is mighty in strength, not a single one is missing.
native_verses.40:27: Why do you say, Jacob, and speak, Israel, "My way is concealed from the LORD, and my justice passes away from my God"?
native_verses.40:28: Have you not known, or have you not heard? The eternal God, the LORD, Creator of the ends of the earth, does not grow weary and does not become exhausted; there is no searching out His understanding.
native_verses.40:29: He gives strength to the weary, and to the one without vigor He multiplies power.
native_verses.40:30: Even youths grow weary and become exhausted, and young men utterly stumble;
native_verses.40:31: but those who wait for the LORD will gain fresh strength; they will ascend on wings like eagles; they will run and not become exhausted; they will walk and not grow weary.
native_verses.41:1: Keep silent before Me, coastlands, and let the peoples regain their strength. Let them step forward, then let them speak; together let us draw near for judgment.
native_verses.41:2: Who has roused one from the east, whom He calls in righteousness to follow Him? He hands over nations before him and subdues kings; He makes them like dust with his sword, like blown stubble with his bow.
native_verses.41:3: He pursues them and passes on in safety, along a path he has not gone with his feet.
native_verses.41:4: Who has acted and done this, summoning the generations from the beginning? I, the LORD, am the first, and with the last ones, I am He.
native_verses.41:5: The coastlands saw and became afraid; the ends of the earth shuddered; they drew near and came.
native_verses.41:6: Each man helps his neighbor, and to his brother he says, "Be strong!"
native_verses.41:7: The artisan strengthens the metalworker, and the one who smooths with the hammer strengthens the one who strikes the anvil, saying about the soldering, "It is good"; and he secures it with nails so that it will not topple.
native_verses.41:8: Yet you, Israel, My servant, Jacob whom I chose, seed of Abraham, My friend,
native_verses.41:9: you whom I took hold of from the ends of the earth and summoned from its remote corners, and I said to you, "You are My servant; I chose you and did not reject you."
native_verses.41:10: Do not be afraid, for I am with you; do not look about in alarm, for I am your God. I will make you strong; indeed, I will help you; indeed, I will support you with the right hand of My righteousness.
